items.title: Feature — Multi-tenant (SaaS): varios clientes en una instancia, licencia de pago unico

labels.name: area:fullstack
labels.description: Product work: one vertical slice, datos + API + pantalla

items.body:
## Context

Hoy el ERP es single-tenant: una instancia, una base y una configuracion fiscal para una sola distribuidora medica. Para poder vender el sistema a varias distribuidoras hay que aislar los datos por cliente (tenant) y hacer que lo que hoy es global (razon social, CUIT, certificados ARCA, puntos de venta, numeracion, parametros) pase a ser por tenant.

Modelo comercial: **pago unico por adquirir el sistema (licencia perpetua), sin suscripcion, y el cobro ocurre por fuera de la plataforma.** Por lo tanto el sistema NO integra pasarela de pagos ni facturacion recurrente ni bloqueo por mora; solo necesita que un operador (ASOME) pueda dar de alta, activar y desactivar tenants manualmente.

> **Problema del mapa operativo:** pendiente de confirmar — el relevamiento actual (`docs/`) esta hecho para un unico cliente y no menciona multi-tenant. Antes de priorizar, validar con producto que existe demanda concreta de un segundo cliente (regla "Solo lo necesario").

> **Decision 2026-09-30:** multi-tenant con **una sola base y columna `tenantId`** (shared schema) en lugar de una base por cliente. Justificacion: un solo despliegue y migraciones unicas. Alternativa a evaluar en el spike: schema/DB por tenant (mejor aislamiento, mas costo operativo).

## Scope

### Datos

```
Tenant
  id            uuid pk
  name          string          -- razon social
  slug          string unique   -- subdominio / identificador de login
  status        enum ACTIVE | SUSPENDED
  licensedAt    date            -- fecha de alta de la licencia (informativo)
  createdAt / updatedAt

TenantSettings (1:1)            -- lo que hoy es global/hardcodeado
  tenantId, cuit, razonSocial, condicionIva, puntoVenta[],
  arcaCert / arcaKey (cifrados), ambiente (homologacion|produccion)

+ tenantId NOT NULL (FK, indexado) en TODAS las tablas de negocio
  (users, products, suppliers, customers, stock_ledger, purchases,
   sales, payments, receipts, cheques, cash, audit_log, ...)
+ unicos compuestos: (tenantId, sku), (tenantId, email), (tenantId, cuit), etc.
+ numeracion (recibos, comprobantes, OC) por tenant
```

Migracion: crear un tenant "default" con los datos actuales y hacer backfill de `tenantId` en todas las tablas antes de poner `NOT NULL`. Migracion reversible.

### API

- Resolver tenant en cada request desde el JWT (claim `tenantId`), nunca desde un header/param enviado por el cliente.
- Aislamiento centralizado, no por endpoint: filtro automatico por `tenantId` en repositorios/queries (subscriber o base repository de TypeORM, y/o Row Level Security de PostgreSQL como defensa en profundidad).
- Login: `tenantSlug + email + password`; el email deja de ser unico global.
- Jobs BullMQ (importador, contingencia fiscal, worker) deben llevar `tenantId` en el payload y ejecutar en su contexto.
- Servicio ARCA: credenciales y punto de venta leidos de `TenantSettings`, no de variables de entorno globales.
- Panel de plataforma (rol `SUPERADMIN`, fuera de cualquier tenant): `POST/GET/PATCH /platform/tenants` para alta, listado, suspender/reactivar y crear el primer administrador del tenant. Sin pasarela de pagos: "activar" es una accion manual tras cobrar por fuera.

### Pantalla

- Selector/campo de organizacion en el login (o resolucion por subdominio).
- Vista `SUPERADMIN`: listado de tenants, alta, estado, fecha de licencia, boton suspender/reactivar.
- Configuracion del tenant (administrador del tenant): datos fiscales y carga de certificados ARCA.
- Tenant `SUSPENDED`: login rechazado con mensaje claro; datos conservados.

## Technical notes

- **Riesgo #1 = fuga de datos entre tenants.** Cada modulo existente (stock, ventas, cobros, importador, reportes) debe auditarse; agregar tests e2e que verifiquen que el tenant A nunca lee ni escribe datos del tenant B (incluyendo consultas raw/`QueryBuilder`).
- Sin billing: no agregar Stripe/MercadoPago, planes, limites por plan ni cron de vencimiento. `licensedAt` es solo informativo.
- Certificados ARCA y claves: almacenar cifrados, nunca en logs ni en respuestas de la API.
- Revisar `docs/decimal_policy.md`, `docs/domain_model.md` y ADRs vigentes; agregar un ADR con la decision de estrategia de aislamiento.
- Impacto en despliegue (Railway / `docs/deployment`): un solo servicio sirve a todos los tenants; definir dominio/subdominios y backups por tenant.
- Datos de seed y fixtures de tests deben crearse dentro de un tenant.
- Sugerencia de corte: si el esfuerzo excede un sprint, dividir en **slices verticales** (p. ej. tenant + auth/usuarios extremo a extremo → ARCA por tenant → resto de modulos), no por capa.

## Preguntas abiertas

- [ ] Confirmar que hay un segundo cliente real (o pipeline) que justifique el trabajo.
- [ ] Schema compartido vs base por tenant (resultado del spike/ADR).
- [ ] Subdominio por cliente o campo `slug` en el login.
- [ ] Entrega de actualizaciones: todos los tenants en la misma version (asumido) vs versiones por cliente.
- [ ] Alcance de "licencia perpetua": soporte/actualizaciones incluidas por cuanto tiempo (decision comercial, fuera del sistema).

---

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Feature implemented and working locally
- [ ] Tests written (incl. e2e de aislamiento entre tenants)
- [ ] Linting passes
- [ ] Type-check passes
- [ ] Migracion con backfill del tenant actual aplicada y reversible
- [ ] ADR de estrategia de aislamiento escrito
- [ ] PR opened, reviewed, merged to `main`
- [ ] Issue closed, Stage → Done on board

---

|                  |            |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| **Sprint start** | Backlog (sin sprint asignado) |
| **Sprint end**   | Backlog (sin sprint asignado) |

items.title: Plugin-owned table DDL & migration strategy (enabling manifest storage.ownTables)
items.body:
## Context

Gap identified during the 2026-07-22 #59/#84 design review: the plugin manifest declares `storage.ownTables[]`, and #59's update-consent section notes that "own-table migrations may make rollback unsafe" — but nothing specifies **who runs plugin DDL, when, or how**. Per #59 decision D-H, `storage.ownTables` is **inert at MVP**: validated for shape and naming rules, declaration-only, no DDL executes. This issue designs and implements activation.

## Problem

Plugins that need persistent relational state (beyond the `metadataSchemaVersion` lazy-migrated JSON metadata pattern) have no sanctioned way to create or evolve their tables. Options span a wide trust/complexity range and interact with:

- The no-code-executes-at-install guarantee (#84 trust model)
- Rollback semantics (server-level whole-plugin rollback exists; own-table migrations can make it unsafe — #59)
- Update flow ordering (migrate before or after activation; failure handling)
- Multi-tenant hosted deployments (schema/prefix isolation)

## Candidate designs (to be evaluated)

1. **Declarative SQL migration files in the tarball**, executed by the *host* at install/update inside a transaction, restricted to a per-plugin schema or enforced table-name prefix (`plugin_<slug>_*`). No plugin code runs; migrations are inspectable at review time and by the #84 static pipeline. Ordered, forward-only, checksummed (Flyway-style).
2. **Host-provided migration API** invoked from plugin code at first load — violates no-code-at-install only weakly (runs at load, not install) but makes migrations opaque and rollback reasoning worse.
3. **No relational DDL ever** — plugins get a host-managed KV/JSON store (`plugin_data` table keyed by pluginId + scope) and nothing else. Simplest; may be sufficient for most categories.

Initial lean: **(1)**, with **(3)** offered as the zero-ceremony default so most plugins never need DDL. Decision to be locked before implementation.

## Open questions

- Per-plugin Postgres schema vs shared schema + name-prefix enforcement
- Down-migrations: supported, or rollback declared unsafe when migrations present (current #59 stance)?
- Migration failure during update: block activation (server-gating semantics) — presumably yes
- Interaction with `bundled` plugins upgrading with BGE core
- `bge-plugin validate` checks for migration file naming/ordering/checksums (#84 toolkit)
- Multi-tenant/hosted: schema-per-plugin-per-tenant explosion — constraints for the SaaS deployment

## Dependencies

- #59 (manifest field, loader lifecycle, D-H inert baseline)
- #84 (tarball layout carries migration files; validation pipeline step)

## Out of scope

- The MVP inert validation of `storage.ownTables` (ships in #59 Phase A)
- Plugin metadata lazy migration (`metadataSchemaVersion`, plugin-internal per #59)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

HMS runs shared-schema multi-tenancy with PostgreSQL row-level security by default, with schema-per-tenant and database-per-tenant reserved for premium tiers. That shared default means every tenant competes for the same connection pool, the same JetStream consumers, the same Redis instance and the same Knative capacity. The brief requires per-tenant rate limits and resource quotas to prevent noisy-neighbour degradation — but a quota cannot be set, tuned or enforced without per-tenant consumption data, and none exists.

The absence has concrete effects:

- **One tenant can degrade every other and we cannot prove it.** A 900-bed hospital running an unpaged bulk export against the appointments API during morning OPD saturates the connection pool. Every other tenant sees slow page loads. The estate-wide dashboards from #610 show degraded latency with no attribution, so the incident is diagnosed as "the database is slow" and mitigated by scaling, which pays for one tenant's behaviour across the whole estate.
- **Infrastructure cost is not attributable, so pricing is a guess.** Subscription tiers are priced without knowing what a tenant of a given size actually consumes in database time, storage, egress and event volume.
- **Tenant health is invisible until churn.** A hospital whose staff have stopped using the discharge module, or whose vendor integration has been failing for three weeks, looks identical to a healthy one until renewal. The brief calls for tenant health and NPS in AdminConnect; that needs a signal.
- **Onboarding failures go unnoticed.** A newly provisioned tenant whose ABDM HIP registration never completed, or whose facility master was never populated, produces no error — just an absence of activity nobody is watching for.
- **Quota enforcement without measurement is dangerous.** Applying a limit without first observing the distribution risks throttling a legitimate hospital during peak clinical hours, which is a patient-care consequence, not a performance one.

Affected: SRE on-call attributing a degradation, the customer-success contact for larger tenants, the commercial team pricing tiers, the hospital admin whose facility is being throttled by another tenant's behaviour, and the platform engineers sizing capacity.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** platform SRE, customer-success contact and commercial owner
**I want** per-tenant consumption, saturation, error and adoption signals with quota tracking and noisy-neighbour attribution
**So that** I can identify within minutes which tenant is degrading the estate, set defensible quotas from observed distributions, attribute infrastructure cost, and spot an unhealthy or failing tenant before it churns.

### Scope

**In scope**

* **Per-tenant resource accounting**: request rate, error rate and latency by product; PostgreSQL time consumed and rows read/written; connection-pool occupancy; Redis key count and memory; object-storage bytes stored and egressed; JetStream messages published and consumed; Temporal workflow executions. Sourced from the metric store in #606, with high-cardinality detail carried on trace exemplars in #607 rather than as labels.
* **Quota definition and tracking**: declared per-tier quotas for request rate, concurrent connections, storage, event volume and export operations, with current utilisation, a soft-threshold warning at 80% and a hard limit, all expressed as country-profile- and tier-aware configuration.
* **Noisy-neighbour attribution**: during an estate degradation, rank tenants by contribution to the saturated resource, so the answer names a tenant and a route rather than a component.
* **Tenant health score**: a composite of adoption (active users, modules in use, feature usage trend), reliability (error rate, failed integrations), operational signals (support ticket volume and severity) and commercial signals (subscription tier, renewal date), with the contributing factors always visible so the score is explicable rather than oracular.
* **Onboarding and integration health**: whether a tenant's ABDM HIP/HIU registration, HPR and HFR linkage, payment gateway configuration and WhatsApp sender registration are complete and currently succeeding.
* **Internal tenant view** in AdminConnect: one page per tenant with consumption, quota utilisation, health score, integration status and recent incidents.
* **Alerting**: quota approach and breach, health-score decline beyond a threshold, and a tenant contributing disproportionately to a saturated shared resource.
* **Cost attribution**: infrastructure cost allocated per tenant from the consumption series, exported for the commercial team.

**Out of scope**

* **Metric storage, recording rules and cardinality governance** — owned by #606; this issue is a consumer and must respect the declared attribute budgets.
* **Trace and log storage** — owned by #607 and #605.
* **Error grouping** — owned by #608.
* **Synthetic probe execution** — owned by #609; synthetic tenants are excluded from every view in this issue.
* **SLO attainment, error budgets and the tenant-facing availability view** — owned by #610. That reports our performance to a tenant; this reports a tenant's behaviour to us and is deliberately internal.
* **Enforcement of rate limits and quotas at the gateway.** This issue measures, tracks and alerts; the enforcement mechanism at Istio and the application layer is owned by the SRE reliability epic and depends on this measurement landing first.
* **Clinical workflow completion and turnaround monitoring** — owned by #612.
* **De-identified product analytics and funnel analysis** — owned by #613.
* **Billing and invoicing** — this issue supplies the attribution; billing consumes it.

---

## Recommended Solution

### Consumption accounting without a cardinality explosion

`tenant.id` on every metric series would multiply the estate's cardinality by the tenant count, which is exactly the failure #606 is designed to prevent. The approach is therefore tiered:

- A **bounded set of tenant-labelled series** — request rate, error rate, latency histogram, event volume, storage bytes — declared in the #606 registry with an explicit `MaxSeries` covering the tenant population plus headroom.
- **Database and cache attribution by aggregation, not by label.** PostgreSQL time is attributed by a periodic job reading `pg_stat_statements` on a read replica joined to the tenant-scoped data-access layer's query registry, producing a per-tenant rollup at 5-minute granularity rather than a live per-tenant series per statement.
- **Everything else via exemplars** into #607, so an SRE moves from a saturated aggregate to a representative tenant trace in one step.

### Data model

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenant_consumption (
  tenant_id      uuid NOT NULL,
  period_start   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  resource       text NOT NULL,   -- requests | db_time_ms | storage_bytes | egress_bytes
                                  -- | events | workflow_executions | redis_bytes
  quantity       numeric NOT NULL,
  product        text,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, period_start, resource, product)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (period_start);

CREATE TABLE tenant_quota (
  tenant_id      uuid NOT NULL,
  resource       text NOT NULL,
  tier           text NOT NULL,
  soft_limit     numeric NOT NULL,
  hard_limit     numeric NOT NULL,
  window         interval NOT NULL,
  effective_from timestamptz NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, resource, effective_from),
  CHECK (soft_limit <= hard_limit)
);

CREATE TABLE tenant_health (
  tenant_id      uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  score          numeric(5,2) NOT NULL CHECK (score BETWEEN 0 AND 100),
  adoption       numeric(5,2) NOT NULL,
  reliability    numeric(5,2) NOT NULL,
  operational    numeric(5,2) NOT NULL,
  factors        jsonb NOT NULL,   -- explicit contributing factors, for explicability
  computed_at    timestamptz NOT NULL,
  trend_28d      numeric(5,2)
);
```

`tenant_consumption` is partitioned monthly. All three tables carry `tenant.kind <> 'synthetic'` filters in every read path, so the probe tenants from #609 never appear in a health score or a cost allocation.

### Noisy-neighbour attribution

When a shared resource crosses a saturation threshold, an attribution job answers "who" rather than "what":

```
saturation event (db_connections > 85%)
  → rank tenants by db_time_ms in the preceding 5 minutes
  → for the top contributor, rank routes by db_time_ms
  → publish TenantResourceContention{tenant_id, resource, share, top_routes}
```

The alert then reads "tenant X consumed 62% of database time in the last 5 minutes, concentrated on `GET /api/v1/appointments/export`" — which is directly actionable, where "database saturated" is not.

### API surface

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{id}/consumption` | consumption by resource and product over a period |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{id}/quota` | quotas and current utilisation |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{id}/health` | score with contributing factors and 28-day trend |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/{id}/integrations` | ABDM, HPR, HFR, payment and WhatsApp status |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/contention` | current ranked contributors per saturated resource |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/tenants/cost-attribution` | allocated infrastructure cost per tenant per period |

### Authorisation (OpenFGA)

```
type tenant_operations
  relations
    define consumption_viewer: [user, group#member]    # SRE, customer success
    define cost_viewer: [user, group#member]           # commercial only
    define health_viewer: [user, group#member]
```

Every surface here is internal. There is no tenant-facing route in this issue — a hospital admin must never see another tenant's consumption or a ranked contention list, and separating cost from consumption relations keeps commercial data away from on-call engineers who do not need it. Access to any tenant view is audited, because browsing a tenant's operational profile is a privileged act even when it contains no PHI.

### Events

Consumes `TenantProvisioned`, `SubscriptionChanged`, `ConsentGranted`/`ConsentRevoked` counts and integration-status events. Publishes `TenantQuotaSoftThresholdReached`, `TenantQuotaExceeded`, `TenantResourceContention` and `TenantHealthDeclined`. The enforcement layer in the reliability epic subscribes to the quota events rather than reimplementing the measurement.

### Sequencing and dependencies

#606 is a hard prerequisite; #607 is required for exemplar drill-down; #610 should land first so estate-level degradation is detected before tenant attribution is applied to it. Quota *enforcement* must not ship before this issue has run long enough to establish observed distributions — enforcing an unmeasured limit during morning OPD is a clinical risk.

### Risks

- **Cardinality growth as the tenant population scales.** Mitigated by the bounded labelled-series set, aggregation for database and cache attribution, and a declared budget in the #606 registry with an alert as the tenant count approaches it.
- **Setting a quota that throttles legitimate clinical peak load.** Mitigated by a measurement-only phase, quotas derived from an observed high percentile with headroom, EmergencyConnect exempted from hard limits by policy, and a documented emergency override.
- **A health score that nobody trusts.** Mitigated by always exposing contributing factors alongside the number, versioning the scoring model, and never using the score alone to trigger a commercial action.
- **PHI leaking into consumption or health data.** Structurally avoided — every field here is a count, a byte figure or a status. A test asserts no patient-level identifier is present in any of the three tables.
- **`pg_stat_statements` attribution overhead on the primary.** Mitigated by reading from a replica on a 5-minute cycle rather than sampling the primary continuously.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** one tenant runs an unpaged bulk export against `GET /api/v1/appointments/export` during morning OPD, driving PostgreSQL connection-pool occupancy above 85% and degrading latency for other tenants
**When** the saturation threshold is crossed
**Then** within 5 minutes the contention endpoint ranks that tenant as the top contributor with its percentage share of database time and names the offending route, `TenantResourceContention` is published, an alert reaches on-call naming the tenant and route rather than the component, the affected tenant's quota utilisation shows the breach, and no other tenant's data appears in the alert payload beyond aggregate share.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a customer-success user holds `health_viewer` and `consumption_viewer` but not `cost_viewer`
**When** they request `/api/v1/tenants/{id}/cost-attribution` for a tenant they support
**Then** OpenFGA denies the request, the response is a 403 with no cost figure or partial data included, the denial is written to the audit trail with the actor and target tenant, and the tenant page renders the consumption and health panels normally with the cost panel absent rather than showing an empty or zeroed cost figure that could be misread as free.

### Edge Cases

* A newly provisioned tenant has no consumption history — quota utilisation, health score and trend render an explicit "insufficient data" state rather than a zero score that would trigger a false churn-risk alert, and the onboarding integration checklist is shown instead.
* A synthetic probe tenant from #609 generates continuous traffic — it is excluded from consumption reporting, health scoring, contention ranking and cost attribution by the `tenant.kind` filter, verified by an automated check.
* A tenant on the database-per-tenant premium tier — consumption is attributed from its dedicated instance's statistics rather than the shared `pg_stat_statements` path, and the tenant view is identical so an operator need not know the isolation tier to read it.
* EmergencyConnect traffic from a tenant exceeds its hard quota during a mass-casualty incident — the quota event is published and recorded, but the policy exemption prevents any throttling recommendation, and the event is annotated as an exempt breach so it does not distort the tenant's health score.
* A tenant's ABDM HIP registration lapses because a certificate expired — the integration panel shows the failing check with the expiry date, `TenantHealthDeclined` is published, and the failure is attributed to the tenant's configuration rather than counted against platform availability in #610.
* Two tenants each contribute 45% of a saturated resource — the contention ranking reports both rather than naming only the top one, so a mitigation targeting a single tenant is not mistaken for a complete remedy.
## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** Every tenant has continuously measured consumption, quota utilisation, integration health and an explicable health score, and any estate degradation can be attributed to a named tenant and route within minutes.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** Noisy-neighbour incidents are mitigated by addressing the cause rather than by scaling the whole estate at everyone's expense; per-tier quotas are set from observed distributions rather than guesses, which is the prerequisite for enforcement; infrastructure cost becomes attributable so subscription tiers can be priced on evidence; failing onboarding and lapsed integrations surface before the tenant notices.
* **Success metric or validation method:**
  - Time to attribute an estate degradation to a specific tenant and route **under 5 minutes** at p95, verified by injecting a contention scenario in staging and during a production game day.
  - **100%** of active tenants have consumption series for every declared resource, and **≥ 95%** have a computed health score with populated contributing factors, measured by a daily conformance job.
  - Tenant-labelled series stay **below 70%** of their declared cardinality budget in #606 at the projected 24-month tenant count.
  - Quota utilisation figures reconcile with the metric store to within **1%**, verified by an automated daily reconciliation.
  - Infrastructure cost attributed to tenants accounts for **≥ 90%** of the country deployment's total cost, with the unattributed remainder explicitly labelled as shared overhead rather than silently dropped.
  - **Zero** synthetic-tenant records appearing in any consumption, health, contention or cost output over a rolling 30-day window.
  - **Zero** cross-tenant or unauthorised cost disclosures in adversarial authorisation tests.
* **Monitoring period:** 60 days after production rollout, in measurement-only mode, with a quota-distribution review at day 30 before any enforcement is proposed.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

None — all guardrails apply. The AdminConnect tenant view is a real user interface used daily by customer-success and SRE staff, so the accessibility guardrail applies in full: consumption and quota charts need accessible tabular equivalents, quota status must not be conveyed by colour alone, and the health score must be announced with its contributing factors rather than as a bare number. Authorisation separation between consumption, health and cost relations, synthetic-tenant exclusion, cardinality discipline and audited access to tenant views are all directly in scope.

> ⏰ **Deferred (see #875) — trigger:** a concrete second-org / tenant requirement (no current demand).

---

## Hypotese

Støtte for flere organisasjoner løses ved å kjøre én instans av plattformen per organisasjon, fremfor å bygge multi-tenancy inn i datamodellen.

## Begrunnelse

- Tilgangskontroll blir trivielt — ingen risiko for datalekkasje på tvers av org
- Ingen `organisationId` overalt i schema og queries
- Isolert deployment — nedetid hos én org påvirker ikke andre
- GDPR-sletting er enkel: slett instansen og databasen
- Løsningen er allerede containerisert med migrasjonsbasert DB — ny instans er i praksis bare ny konfigurasjon

## Avveininger

- Operasjonell overhead skalerer lineært med antall orgs
- Bugfixer må rulles ut til alle instanser (kan automatiseres via pipeline)
- Aggregert rapportering på tvers av orger blir vanskelig
- Grunnkostnad per instans (DB, compute, storage)

## Vurdering

Riktig tilnærming frem til ~10+ organisasjoner. På det tidspunktet bør man vurdere om shared-schema multi-tenancy eller en orkestreringsplattform (f.eks. Kubernetes + Helm) gir bedre avkastning.

## Aksjonspunkter (når aktuelt)

- [ ] Dokumentere konfigurasjonsvariable som er org-spesifikke (Entra-grupper, e-postdomene, etc.)
- [ ] Vurdere om deploy-pipeline kan parameteriseres for multi-instans utrulling
- [ ] Avklare navnekonvensjon for instanser (Azure resource naming)

items.title: Optional per-schema change-log tables for schema-per-tenant deployments (structural isolation without RLS)
items.body:
## Background

The change-spine change-log lives in a single shared table `core.tb_entity_change_log` for **all** deployments, regardless of tenancy mode. #443 (audit #437 F6) added Row-Level Security to it so a non-`BYPASSRLS` role is deny-by-default — defence-in-depth for a table that holds every tenant's before/after payloads. That fix is correct for **row-mode** tenancy (shared tables + WHERE-injection), where one shared change-log is the natural model.

But FraiseQL also supports **schema-per-tenant** tenancy (`[fraiseql.tenancy] mode = "schema"`): the adapter issues `SET search_path TO tenant_{key}, public` per request and `TenantExecutorFactory` provisions/drops a schema per tenant. For those deployments, a **per-schema change-log table** (`tenant_{key}.tb_entity_change_log`) would give tenant isolation *structurally* — search_path already scopes reads to the tenant's schema — with **no RLS, no `BYPASSRLS` requirement, and no silent-empty-pipeline footgun**. It's arguably the cleaner posture for the schema-isolation users who already accept per-tenant schemas.

This issue proposes making the change-log's location an **opt-in choice** so schema-per-tenant deployments can keep the change-log inside the tenant schema instead of the shared `core` schema.

## Proposed shape (opt-in)

A config toggle (e.g. `[changelog] location = "shared" | "per_tenant_schema"`, default `shared`) selecting where the change-log contract is installed:

- `shared` (today): `core.tb_entity_change_log` + the #443 RLS posture. Unchanged default.
- `per_tenant_schema`: the contract table, views, capture-trigger function, and per-table triggers are installed into each tenant schema; reads scope via search_path; no RLS needed for the table itself.

There is a useful existing seam: the GraphQL `entity_change_logs` query already qualifies its source with a configurable schema (`crates/fraiseql-core/src/schema/changelog.rs` — `with_sql_source(format!("{}.v_entity_change_log", cfg.schema))`), so the read side is partly parameterized already.

## The hard part — CDC fan-out (why this is a design discussion, not a toggle)

The reason the change-log is shared today is the **cross-tenant CDC fan-out**: the poller (`crates/fraiseql-observers/src/listener/change_log.rs`) and the three NATS bridges (`crates/fraiseql-observers/src/transport/{bridge,mysql_bridge,mssql_bridge}.rs`) read **one** ordered stream (`ORDER BY pk_entity_change_log`) across all tenants and fan out events. Per-schema tables break that single stream:

- Polling N per-tenant schemas does not scale and has no defined global ordering.
- A monotonic global cursor (`pk_entity_change_log` / `seq`) no longer exists across schemas.
- Subscription matching, dedup `(object_type, seq)`, and `nats_event_id` mark-published all assume one table.

So the open question is **how CDC consumers source events under per-schema tables** — candidates: a PG `PUBLICATION` across the per-tenant tables, logical replication, a per-tenant poller/stream, or an aggregating outbox. Each has real trade-offs. This needs design before implementation.

## Affected components

- Migrations `08_*`/`11_*`/`12_*` (contract table, capture-trigger fn, RLS) — installed per-schema instead of into `core`.
- `fraiseql generate capture-triggers` — emit triggers into the tenant schema.
- `TenantExecutorFactory` schema provisioning — install the change-log contract when a tenant schema is created.
- Poller + 3 NATS bridges — the fan-out sourcing question above.
- Server changelog HTTP handlers (`crates/fraiseql-server/src/observers/changelog_handlers/mod.rs`) + the `entity_change_logs` query.
- `fraiseql doctor` — the change-log RLS / contract-drift checks become per-schema.

## Out of scope / notes

- Default stays `shared` + RLS (#443). This is purely additive opt-in.
- Row-mode tenancy is unaffected (shared table is correct there).
- Not a security fix — F6 is already closed by #443. This is an isolation-model option for schema-per-tenant users who'd prefer structural isolation over RLS.

Refs #443, #437 (F6).

# DIVINE SHINE — HARVEY AI ACQUISITION PILOT
**Owner directive | Single engineering coordination issue | 2026-10-31 CT**
**Repository:** MikeSimmonsAI/advisorflow-web
**Drive project:** https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EZPZCGGtPJ7YOQ9NUccZxswTfDKHUj1Z
**Reference source:** https://github.com/ethanplusai/harvey (MIT; retain notices)

## Mission and boundary
Build one fully functional, polished, PRIVATE EvoSys Pro client-acquisition workspace for **Divine Shine Elite Cleaning**, owned by Ciara, serving Dallas–Fort Worth. The service is a **managed operation (Option A)**: EvoSys Pro researches prospects, operates eligible outreach, follows up, qualifies interested companies and books consultations or walkthroughs. Ciara sees appointments, prospect context, quotes and contract outcomes; she closes deals. **Do not expose campaign/Harvey internals to Ciara.** This is NOT Daniel's Commercial Cleaning Blueprint, and must not modify, share records with, or grant access to that product. No rollout to other tenants or brands.

## Success definition
- Free initial 30-day LIVE pilot, counting from verified activation of real operations, not software development.
- Target 3–5 genuinely qualified booked appointments, **not guaranteed**. Report appointments held, estimate/quote conversion, won recurring accounts and monthly contract value separately.
- Proposed discovery pool 750–1,000 DFW businesses and qualified pool 400–600 are hypotheses, subject to discovery accuracy and responsible sending volume.
- A 'qualified booked appointment' requires demonstrable customer interest in commercial/recurring cleaning and calendar-confirmed availability; scraped business names do not count.
- Free pilot, no automatic subscription/commission, no obligation beyond participation and honest feedback/outcome reporting. Prepare a concise pilot agreement, no invented commitments.

## Ciara's customer profile (from her own message)
Recurring commercial cleaning contracts in DFW. Targets: office buildings, medical and professional facilities, apartment complexes, property-management firms, short-term rental managers. Prioritize attainable smaller commercial clients; distinguish specialized medical cleaning from general offices. Capture her service capabilities, coverage, minimum job value, existing account exclusions, proof of insurance/certifications (only truthful verified claims), travel and appointment availability and quote-to-close feedback. Keep onboarding 8th-grader simple, and do not request personal account passwords.

## Architecture: ADAPT, DO NOT DUMP A SECOND APP
Review Harvey main: collectors/discover.py, collectors/profile.py, collectors/people.py, signals.py, agents/scout.py, writer.py, handler.py, analyst.py, gate.py, untrusted.py, state.py and integrations. Treat third-party content as untrusted. Retain MIT copyright/license notices in substantial reused code. Evaluate maturity/dependencies/security carefully.

Existing EvoSys Pro modules to inspect before designing:
- app/routers/lead_intelligence_router.py, app/models/lead_intel_models.py, app/services/qualification.py, app/services/lead_routing.py
- app/services/workforce/, app/jobs/run_ai_workforce_worker.py, app/services/ai_operations/, app/services/ai_gateway* 
- app/services/sales_suppression.py, app/routers/compliance_router.py, app/services/compliance_service.py, app/services/cadence_service.py, app/routers/auto_send_router.py
- app/services/tenant_scheduling.py, calendar providers, appointment models, existing sales workspace
- frontend React routes, Program Access card, God Mode and existing auth/RBAC
- render.yaml, service-role scheduling, database migrations, resource limits.
**Single EvoSys CRM/source of truth**, scoped to Divine Shine. Do not stand up Harvey's independent SQLite CRM/outbox/dashboard/sender as a competing source. Use bounded queued jobs; do not add a runaway 15-min daemon in the RAM-constrained Render backend. Do not rely on consumer Claude/Codex subscription credentials for a commercial customer SaaS model; evaluate compatible production AI gateway cost/rate limits. No exposure of credentials in GitHub/Drive artifacts.

## Mandatory two surfaces
1. **Owner/God Mode operations:** prospect discovery, evidence-based buying signals, search/provider cost estimate, provenance/confidence, DFW segmentation, verified contacts, dedupe, qualification, outreach drafts, mail health, reply inbox/classifications, appointment routing, AI worker health, spending, usage, job tracing, pause/resume/kill switches, outcome conversion dashboard. No fake numbers or placeholders in shipped operating screens.
2. **Divine Shine client workspace:** branded private Program Access card POST-LOGIN; simple dashboard for leads/interested prospects, appointments, prospect context, attendance/outcomes, quote values, recurring deals, notifications, feedback, profile and limited availability controls. No separate public login, tenant-wide access, or God Mode tools. Clean dark sidebar/light content consistent with approved EvoSys Sales Workspace, mobile-friendly, very easy to use.

## Data lifecycle
Discover business -> inspect/provenance -> dedupe -> score vs Divine Shine ICP -> eligible verified contact -> outreach staged -> deterministic pre-send checks + permissions -> authorized send -> reply intake/dedupe -> classify intent and opt-out -> qualified interest -> existing calendar availability checked live -> book in native scheduler -> Ciara notified -> consult held/no-show -> quote -> won/lost -> ROI.
Maintain auditable states and timestamps, company-level stop-on-reply where appropriate, retry/idempotency, confidence and evidence URL, no unsupported inference presented as verified fact.

## Operating constraints
- Strict single-tenant feature-flag and per-tenant authorization; no interaction with Daniel/SCI/Wholesale/Roofing/BookaBoost data or workflows.
- Practice mode and test fixtures isolated from real customers; no demo/sample data leaks.
- Channel eligibility and suppression checked at execution time; do not confuse lawful B2B email with permission for SMS or AI cold calling. Honor opt-outs; fail closed if eligibility unclear.
- AI does not autonomously choose calendar availability or override suppression. Respect current EvoSys kill switches, tenant budgets, global rate limits and approval configuration.
- No external outreach, customer account provisioning, billing, new paid provider spend, production migrations, or production deployment merely because this issue exists. Code can be developed/tested in isolated branch and PR. Get the existing owner's release/approval workflow satisfied before merge/deploy and controlled pilot activation.
- Store only non-sensitive diagrams/screenshots/docs in project Drive; real lead PII in restricted approved systems. Never post keys, addresses, contact exports or client secrets to public issue.

## Work phases and acceptance gates
**P0 — audit:** inspect current EvoSys and Harvey code, create source-to-target integration matrix; explain 'reuse vs rewrite', licensing, compatibility, email deliverability, data model, hosting/AI/prospect data costs, user roles, and risk list with exact paths and test plan.
**P1 — UX and onboarding:** functional Program Access card after login, approved org-scoped access, owner ops + Ciara simple app, business profile and availability, live truthful counts.
**P2 — discovery:** adapter(s), cost estimate, safe first sample cohort (no sends), signals, evidence, dedupe, qualification and tenant-safe pipeline.
**P3 — conversations:** integrate existing managed email/outreach, inbox/intent, guardrails, follow-ups, cost usage; dry run full state machine first. No silent live send.
**P4 — booking/outcomes:** existing calendar authority, qualified booked/held outcome tracking, notification, estimate/won/lost and reports.
**P5 — launch readiness:** security/RBAC, worker idempotency, memory/load, sending reputation, error/kill switch, real-browser tests, backup/rollback and clear pilot start gating.
**P6 — 30-day pilot:** only after launch approval, monitor verified contact-to-booking funnel and document outcomes; decide expand/no-expand AFTER evidence.

## Single-thread working protocol
Use THIS ISSUE as the permanent project ledger. Start by commenting an exact-time CT architecture audit, files inspected, risks, dependencies, proposed minimal implementation slices, and explicit P0 deliverables. Post timestamped progress and links to commits/PRs/test output/screenshots/Drive artifacts in THIS SAME issue. Avoid new handoff threads. Make a clean isolated branch and targeted PR when ready, with tests and accurate screenshots. Never claim 'live', 'done', or customer contacted without recorded evidence. Do not modify Daniel's blueprint. Keep Program Access simple and avoid 'Control Room' clutter. If unavailable external keys/accounts are needed, proceed with mocks and document the precise blocker rather than stalling the rest.

## Drive
Project: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EZPZCGGtPJ7YOQ9NUccZxswTfDKHUj1Z
- Scope: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1H9bigM_04Z1B-GWMlZ4koXqJ1G7LeMoG
- Screenshots: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1B3-GXxwcK3jhLlN6nTe0Mq_tvkkR7LrC
- Business profile: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gRrO01njtQco-1HTvd4zXofVDAGJbN3M
- Research: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qsABSz_MmeFxiaHXR__z_afGTGM7bVxa
- QA: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/15sjRR83nXZ3rCLSNmHYrJlQJlZbHoaC1

**Owner decision is to proceed with development of this single-company proof, not to enable customer contact or broaden distribution. Begin P0 audit, then P1 implementation within normal engineering gates.**

## User authorization
On 12 November 2026 the owner authorized an overnight release effort: create issues, have the relevant agents review them, apply approved after scope review, implement, independently review/rework PRs, and merge after review and CI pass. This standing delegation replaces earlier owner-only merging for this effort. It does not permit bypassing the approval label, the 15-reviewable-file limit, secrets, or uncertain production configuration.

## Product scope
Two businesses, each with a customer and admin Expo app, share an npm monorepo. Release web first, Android next, iOS after. Backend: Supabase Auth/Postgres/RLS/Realtime. Integrations: Google Analytics and Firebase Cloud Messaging. Ordering is restricted to Khed, Maharashtra by the server, not only a UI check.

## MVP assumptions
- Khed means Khed in Ratnagiri district (Konkan), not Khed/Pune. Service polygon must be verified/configured before live ordering is enabled; absent or unverified service area fails closed.
- Cash on delivery only for initial release; no invented payment gateway.
- Menu browsing, cart, authenticated checkout, address/contact, location eligibility, order history/live status; admin menu availability and order status management.
- Business and admin/customer access are enforced by Supabase, and totals/status transitions are server-authoritative.
- Analytics uses consent and excludes personal/contact/precise-location data. Messaging permission is contextual; in-app realtime and push are distinct.
- Public demo can browse seeded examples but must not fake successful real checkout.

## Release criteria
- [ ] Four app workspaces and shared UI/core/service packages.
- [ ] Cross-business/user/admin isolation and checkout/geofence/state transition tests.
- [ ] Customer and admin browser flows tested at desktop/mobile sizes.
- [ ] Clean installs, typechecks, web/native exports and GitHub CI.
- [ ] Reproducible Supabase migrations, seed, tests and Firebase function setup.
- [ ] EAS profiles, web artifacts/deployment workflow and release/configuration guide.
- [ ] Production blockers (accounts, keys, signing, verified boundary, real menu/prices, store review) explicitly reported rather than described as complete.

## Delivery process
Create bounded implementation subissues, review with relevant roles, then apply the exact approved label before implementation. Every PR <=15 reviewable files; .gitignore, README files and objectively generated lockfiles excluded. Correct feature/<app>-<issue>-<desc> branches; independent senior review for security/data/shared logic/CI, UX review for UI. Merge only the reviewed head after all required checks pass. Preserve original local main/screen/setup branches.

Related existing foundation: #1. This umbrella closes only after aggregate criteria are satisfied; child PRs close their own issues.

items.body:
> 🤖 Generated by the Agentic Engineer

Part of #6875. Depends on #6876, shared schema/plan #7512, the relevant catalogue verdicts in #6877, and existing Flux renderer parity bug #7511. Implementation and runtime proof remain pending.



## Problem and outcome

KSail currently chooses component versions from embedded source files and installs from external chart repositories. It has a Kustomize/Helm inspection renderer, provenance and degradation reporting, and safe scaffold helpers, but it does not have a complete built-in platform catalogue/render artifact shared by CLI and operator. The programme requires default configuration without cloning a reference/adopter repo, and a common base that #6878 can safely layer and hand off.

Implement the bounded content/render foundation: reviewed embedded catalogue/preset data, exact authenticated component render inputs and wiring templates, stable component/object identities, and deterministic final manifests or equivalent pinned controller artifact. Consume the resolved plan rather than re-defaulting it. Produce Flux and Argo adapters from the same component model. Keep generated base content and provenance separate from adopter-owned overlays. This feature starts default-off.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The off path preserves existing component/scaffold behavior and refuses selected new rendering/actuation paths before writing. On/off command and config gates are tested; later graduation is separate.
- [ ] A controlled catalogue with at least an existing component adapter and one clearly labeled composite test capability renders without reading the reference platform or an adopter repo. Instrumented acquisition controls prove exact inputs used and deny unplanned network source acquisition. An empty catalogue/output cannot pass.
- [ ] Every built-in chart/template input has a recorded version, authenticated content digest and source/license provenance. Corrupt/missing/mismatched inputs fail before render or delivery. An image digest does not stand in for the chart digest. Artifact pins and rendered pins agree.
- [ ] Equivalent plans yield deterministic complete resources/values, stable identities and provenance through both engine adapters, including required CRDs and wiring. Tests compare semantic manifests and the native engine value composition, not only counts/snapshots or whether controller CRs parse. Link values-precedence Bug #7511 and preserve its targetPath/literal controls.
- [ ] Rendered output is published under the #6876 generated-base layout or equivalent operator artifact. Existing content is verified before reuse; path traversal, unsafe symlinks, conflicting object identities and ambiguous/missing patch targets fail before write. Adopter overlay and unrelated workload files are never overwritten. Partial generation/delivery failure cannot publish a completed baseline.
- [ ] Built-in base and adopter overlay compose before delivery to the one active owner. A seed and a steady-state adapter consume identical effective values and exact release identities. Controlled clients verify rejected graphs/artifacts never mutate a cluster. Real bootstrap/handoff is still #6878/#6879 acceptance.
- [ ] Existing schema/policy/posture validation examines the complete rendered resources. Any unsupported render, unresolved non-optional values, missing schema/context, or incomplete child coverage remains a visible limitation and cannot certify complete platform policy coverage. Positive scope controls prevent an empty/wrong stream from passing.
- [ ] Exact input/content/plan/overlay digests and version differences are inspectable without resolved secret values. Updating built-ins is a reviewed source/pin change with rendered diffs, not runtime latest discovery.

- [ ] Complete source/template/rendered controls refuse forced replacement of persistent resources and conflicting overlays before writes, with positive non-destructive cases and intercepted-negative forcing, malformed/uninspectable and partial-output cases. Qualify Flux and Argo separately; retained prune policy and external ownership are preserved, and immutable stateful changes use an explicit migration/retention contract.

## Boundaries

This is shared rendering and delivery preparation, not #6878's real override/handoff/upgrade trial, #6879's real secret consumption/removal, #6880's two live presets, #6881's continuous reference evaluation, or #6882's hosted multi-target convergence. Do not add platform classes, tenancy/quota/auth, an air-gap guarantee, or an external reference service. Production catalogue content must be approved through #6877 and delivered by its capability child; test fixtures are not substitutes for those gates.

## Evidence

- [Current Cilium version source](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/blob/c4f3a6d4d348c8195c0e44a0ef9b84fb0408ad29/pkg/svc/installer/cni/cilium/version.go#L9) and [external chart specification](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/blob/c4f3a6d4d348c8195c0e44a0ef9b84fb0408ad29/pkg/svc/installer/cni/cilium/installer.go#L122).
- [Inspection provenance and degradation](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/blob/c4f3a6d4d348c8195c0e44a0ef9b84fb0408ad29/pkg/svc/gitops/render/render.go#L35) and [chart/value resolver](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/blob/c4f3a6d4d348c8195c0e44a0ef9b84fb0408ad29/pkg/svc/gitops/render/resolver.go#L154).
- [Scaffold entry point](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/blob/c4f3a6d4d348c8195c0e44a0ef9b84fb0408ad29/pkg/fsutil/scaffolder/scaffolder.go#L126) and [safe overlay generation](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/blob/c4f3a6d4d348c8195c0e44a0ef9b84fb0408ad29/pkg/svc/environment/reconcile_generate.go#L27).


## Stateful replacement safety from the current reference

The [completed catalogue decision](https://github.com/devantler-tech/ksail/issues/6877#issuecomment-5984361226) incorporates Platform `3f2764d78b0c5cad91354d21be12baaca28a14d7`: Flux layers and both Tenant templates use `force: false`; the obsolete PVC force annotation transformer is removed while existing prune protections remain. The [reference source validator](https://github.com/devantler-tech/platform/tree/3f2764d78b0c5cad91354d21be12baaca28a14d7/scripts/validate-flux-force-safety) rejects forcing Flux layers and force opt-ins on manifest-owned PVC/CNPG Clusters, including inspected templates and rendered patches. Its source census does not establish a universal Jobs-only guard, complete chart/operator-generated coverage, or equivalent Argo behavior.

The shared renderer must examine its own complete inputs and final output, preserve adopter ownership and retention, refuse conflicting replacement overlays before writes, and prove the corresponding Argo behavior independently. Immutable persistent-resource changes require an explicit reviewed migration/retention path; forced deletion/recreation and silently overwriting a user overlay are refused. Current reference prune/retirement policy remains in force; the future change tracked by [Platform #4444](https://github.com/devantler-tech/platform/issues/4444) needs its own merged implementation and deployment readback. Source/render acceptance does not prove live data retention or successful restore.

items.body:
### Affected area

Other

### Problem or use case

First off, thanks for TokenHub — the governance-first approach (project-scoped keys, routing policy, provider reconciliation) really fills a gap that most AI gateways skip.

I'd like to ask whether multi-tenancy is on the roadmap.

Context
We're evaluating TokenHub for a use case where a single deployment needs to serve multiple independent organizations (not just multiple teams inside one company). From reading the README and the three-role workspace design (User / Team Leader / Administrator), my understanding is that the current architecture is single-tenant by design:

Identity source is a single enterprise OAuth/OIDC.
The admin role is global to the deployment.
There's no tenant_id (or equivalent) concept that isolates users, projects, API keys, usage logs, and bills across independent organizations.
The PostgreSQL "multi-instance" note refers to horizontal scaling of replicas, not logical multi-tenancy.
Is that understanding correct?

Questions
Is multi-tenancy (in the SaaS sense — multiple independent organizations on one deployment) something you intend to support, or is it explicitly out of scope given the "private enterprise gateway" positioning?
If it's in scope, which isolation model are you leaning toward?
Shared DB + tenant_id column (with PostgreSQL RLS for enforcement)
Schema-per-tenant
Database-per-tenant (each tenant gets its own SQLite file / PG database)
If it's not on the roadmap, would you be open to a community PR that introduces a tenant_id layer? Specifically, are there architectural constraints (e.g. the project/team/admin role model, the provider abstraction, the reconciliation pipeline) that would make such a contribution difficult to merge?

items.body:
## Summary

Add built-in multi-tenancy support with automatic tenant resolution, context propagation, and query filtering.

## Motivation

- SaaS is the dominant application model in 2025
- Multi-tenancy is cross-cutting but lacks standardized CQRS patterns
- Finbuckle.MultiTenant is popular but doesn't integrate with CQRS pipelines
- Encina already has `TenantId` in `IRequestContext` but no resolution/filtering

## Proposed Solution

### Tenant Resolution

```csharp
public interface ITenantResolver
{
    Task<string?> ResolveAsync(HttpContext context);
}

// Built-in resolvers
public class HeaderTenantResolver : ITenantResolver { }      // X-Tenant-Id header
public class SubdomainTenantResolver : ITenantResolver { }   // tenant.myapp.com
public class ClaimsTenantResolver : ITenantResolver { }      // From JWT claims
public class RouteTenantResolver : ITenantResolver { }       // /api/{tenant}/...
```

### Context Enrichment

```csharp
// Extend existing RequestContext
public record RequestContext(
    Guid CorrelationId,
    string? UserId,
    string? TenantId,      // Now automatically populated
    string? IdempotencyKey,
    TenantInfo? Tenant     // Full tenant details
) : IRequestContext;

public record TenantInfo(
    string Id,
    string Name,
    string ConnectionString,  // For database-per-tenant
    string Schema,            // For schema-per-tenant
    IDictionary<string, object> Metadata
);
```

### Automatic Query Filtering

```csharp
// Mark entities as tenant-scoped
public interface ITenantEntity
{
    string TenantId { get; }
}

// EF Core automatic filtering
public class TenantQueryFilterInterceptor : IQueryInterceptor
{
    // Automatically adds WHERE TenantId = @currentTenant
}

// Or explicit in handler
public class GetOrdersHandler : IQueryHandler<GetOrdersQuery, List<OrderDto>>
{
    public async Task<Either<EncinaError, List<OrderDto>>> Handle(
        GetOrdersQuery query, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var tenantId = _context.TenantId; // From IRequestContext
        return await _db.Orders
            .ForTenant(tenantId)  // Extension method
            .ToListAsync(ct);
    }
}
```

### Tenant-Aware Behaviors

```csharp
public class TenantValidationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
{
    // Validates tenant exists and is active
    // Returns EncinaErrors.TenantNotFound or EncinaErrors.TenantSuspended
}

public class TenantIsolationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
{
    // Ensures cross-tenant access is prevented
    // Logs/alerts on tenant boundary violations
}
```

### Features

1. **Tenant Resolution Strategies**
   - Header-based (`X-Tenant-Id`)
   - Subdomain-based (`tenant.app.com`)
   - Path-based (`/api/{tenant}/...`)
   - Claims-based (JWT token)
   - Custom resolver support

2. **Data Isolation Patterns**
   - Database-per-tenant
   - Schema-per-tenant
   - Row-level security (shared database)

3. **Integration Points**
   - `IRequestContext.TenantId` auto-populated
   - EF Core query filters
   - Cache key prefixing by tenant
   - Message correlation with tenant

4. **Configuration**
   ```csharp
   services.AddEncina(config => {
       config.UseMultiTenancy(options => {
           options.TenantResolver = new HeaderTenantResolver();
           options.TenantStore = new DatabaseTenantStore();
           options.EnableQueryFiltering = true;
           options.CacheKeyPrefix = true;  // tenant:{tenantId}:key
       });
   });
   ```

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Finbuckle.MultiTenant without CQRS integration**: Finbuckle provides excellent tenant resolution and context management, but it operates at the middleware level. Integration with the CQRS pipeline provides validation, isolation enforcement, and consistent context propagation.

2. **Manual TenantId in all requests**: Requiring developers to pass TenantId as a parameter to every command/query, but this is error-prone and doesn't provide automatic query filtering or isolation validation.

3. **Separate application instances per tenant**: Deploying isolated instances eliminates complexity but dramatically increases infrastructure costs and operational burden for many-tenant scenarios.

## Affected Packages

- [x] Encina (core)
- [x] Encina.AspNetCore
- [x] Encina.EntityFrameworkCore
- [x] Encina.Dapper.*
- [x] Encina.ADO.*
- [x] Encina.MongoDB
- [ ] Encina.Messaging
- [x] Encina.Caching.*
- [x] Other: `Encina.MultiTenancy` (new package)

## Additional Context

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ITenantResolver` interface with built-in implementations
- [ ] `TenantInfo` record with connection/schema info
- [ ] `TenantResolutionMiddleware` for ASP.NET Core
- [ ] `IRequestContext` extension with tenant details
- [ ] `TenantValidationBehavior` for tenant validation
- [ ] EF Core `ITenantEntity` and query filter support
- [ ] Cache key tenant prefixing integration
- [ ] OpenTelemetry tags for tenant correlation
- [ ] Documentation with patterns for each isolation level

### References

- [Finbuckle.MultiTenant](https://www.finbuckle.com/multitenant)
- [Multi-Tenant Data Patterns on Azure](https://developersvoice.com/blog/azure/azure-multi-tenant-data-patterns-implementation-guide/)

items.title: [Cosmos] Remove ephemeral-tenant provisioning from fixed-account live-test lanes

labels.name: Client
labels.description: This issue points to a problem in the data-plane of the library.

items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

PR #48459 moves the Python Cosmos key-auth live tests onto fixed, team-owned accounts and proves that the selected accounts work across the live matrix. However, the shared Python live-test stage still deploys and removes a temporary Cosmos account for every matrix leg before the fixed credentials are reapplied.

As a result, the migrated key-auth tests still authenticate through the ephemeral live-test tenant during ARM deployment. A tenant rotation or broken service connection can therefore fail the job before pytest reaches the fixed account. This is the final gap between the current Python implementation and Java's no-provisioning fixed-account model.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Separate the live matrix by resource-lifecycle requirements and make the fixed-account lane independent of ephemeral-tenant provisioning.

- [ ] Split the 12 fixed key-auth jobs and the already-fixed GSI job from the 7 AAD jobs that require a tenant-scoped Cosmos data-plane role assignment.
- [ ] Run the fixed-account jobs through a Cosmos-owned stage or job that resolves credentials from the shared versioned JSON secret but does not invoke `build-test-resource-config.yml`, `deploy-test-resources.yml`, or `remove-test-resources.yml`.
- [ ] Ensure the fixed-account jobs do not require the `azure-sdk-tests-cosmos` service connection or any authentication against the ephemeral tenant.
- [ ] Keep the AAD jobs on the existing provisioned-resource path so `test-resources.bicep` can create their tenant-specific `sqlRoleAssignment`.
- [ ] Move values currently supplied only as Bicep outputs into the fixed-account matrix. In particular, set `AZURE_COSMOS_ENABLE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER=True` on the applicable circuit-breaker jobs.
- [ ] Remove the transitional post-deployment credential reapplication once fixed-account jobs no longer deploy resources; the resolver pre-step should become their sole source of `ACCOUNT_HOST` and `ACCOUNT_KEY`.
- [ ] Add best-effort cleanup for databases left by cancelled or aborted runs. Cleanup must be limited to stale `PythonSDKTest-*` databases owned by Python and must run across each fixed account without affecting Java or concurrent Python runs.
- [ ] Document ownership for Java's shared account provisioning/reconciliation script and the shared JSON secret update procedure, including a smoke test after account or key rotation.
- [ ] Validate overlapping fixed-account runs and prove they remain runnable when ephemeral-tenant deployment credentials are unavailable.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

1. Keep the current transitional deployment followed by credential override. This is already proven by PR #48459, but it does not remove the tenant dependency.
2. Move AAD tests onto the fixed accounts and refresh their role assignments after every tenant rotation. This preserves one matrix but requires cross-subscription permissions and additional identity lifecycle work.
3. Add a per-leg deployment condition to shared `eng` templates. This is generic, but changes monorepo-wide infrastructure for a Cosmos-specific requirement.
4. Register a separate AAD pipeline while keeping the fixed-account pipeline Cosmos-owned. This is fully service-local but adds another Azure DevOps pipeline definition to maintain.

**Additional context**

PR #48459 already supplies the prerequisites for this work:

- A cross-platform PowerShell resolver compatible with Java's shared JSON-secret schema.
- Stable-account selectors for all 12 key-auth matrix jobs; GSI already uses dedicated fixed credentials.
- Run-scoped `PythonSDKTest-*` database naming, bounded control-plane retries, scoped normal cleanup, and test isolation needed for concurrent use.
- Early resolver validation through `PreSteps` and a Cosmos-local post-deployment hook used during the transitional rollout.
- Successful live verification of the fixed-account query, split, multi-region, and circuit-breaker coverage.

Related tracking issue: #48236. Java reference: Azure/azure-sdk-for-java#49735.

items.title: Security: Supabase RLS policies allow public writes to current_pipeline and shared_analyses via the anon key
items.body:
## Problem
`app/src/lib/supabase.ts:4-8` creates the app's `supabase` client with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` — a key that ships in the browser bundle by design. Several tables' Row Level Security policies do not restrict writes on that anon role, so anyone holding the public anon key (i.e. anyone who loads the site) can write directly to Postgres via the Supabase REST API, bypassing the Next.js app entirely.

## Evidence
- `app/supabase/migrations/006_create_current_pipeline.sql:26-28`:
  ```sql
  CREATE POLICY "Allow public upsert" ON current_pipeline
      FOR ALL WITH CHECK (id = 'current');
  ```
  No `USING` clause — this policy has no auth/role restriction at all, only a value check on `id`. Any client can `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` the singleton pipeline row.
- `app/supabase/migrations/002_create_shared_analyses.sql:26-32` — `FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (true)` and `FOR UPDATE USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)`, i.e. unrestricted insert/update for `shared_analyses`.
- `app/supabase/migrations/009_afbp_schema_migration.sql:213-221` — the same permissive pattern repeated for the `afbp` schema's `pipeline_current` table.
- This is reachable independent of the app-layer routes: the `current_pipeline`/`shared_analyses` tables are exposed over PostgREST directly, so see #3 does not need to be fixed for this to be exploitable.

## Impact
Any visitor can overwrite the current pipeline singleton (corrupting what every other user sees) or flood `shared_analyses` with junk rows, without going through the Next.js server at all — a Supabase REST call with the public anon key and URL is enough.

## Recommendation
Add `USING` clauses restricting `SELECT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` to `auth.role() = 'service_role'` (or an authenticated admin claim), and restrict `INSERT`/`UPDATE` `WITH CHECK` similarly. Public writes should only happen through server code holding the service-role key, never through the anon-key client.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `current_pipeline` and `shared_analyses` (and their `afbp`-schema equivalents) reject writes from the anon role
- [ ] A follow-up migration adds proper `USING`/`WITH CHECK` policies scoped to `service_role` for writes

---

items.title: [Spec] P2 — Managed runtime and MCP
items.body:
# P2 — Managed runtime and MCP

Parent specification and coordination: https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/5

Status: ready for manager decomposition after assignment. No implementation, paid experiments or rollout dispatched by this issue.

## Problem Statement

A smart model cannot by itself preserve decisions, enforce authority or reliably resume management work. Separate UI and assistant implementations could fork plans or bypass checks.

## Solution

Run bounded management tasks over Relay's existing authenticated services, durable plans and execution records. Expose the same governed operations to the native experience and MCP.

## User Stories

1. As an artist, I want to have my goals and explicit preferences remembered, so that I do not repeat my brief every session.
2. As an artist, I want to inspect and correct inferred preferences, so that Relay does not silently impose assumptions.
3. As an artist, I want to resume a manager task after interruption, so that my previous decisions remain intact.
4. As an artist, I want to use an external assistant on the same plan, so that I do not create conflicting schedules.
5. As an artist, I want to receive a truthful limited result during model failure, so that I can distinguish saved work from unfinished reasoning.
6. As an artist, I want to cancel a manager task, so that it stops preparing new work within my revoked scope.
7. As an artist, I want to have permission checked on every action, so that a prompt cannot grant access to another account.
8. As an operator, I want to bound calls, time and spend per task, so that background work cannot run indefinitely.
9. As an operator, I want to identify the model configuration and evidence for a plan, so that I can investigate problems and roll back changes.
10. As a manager agent, I want to reuse established plan and execution authorities, so that parallel implementation does not create competing state.

## Implementation Decisions

- Own runtime orchestration, brief persistence semantics, authenticated management operations and the MCP adapter. Experience owns presentation; execution owns delivery; evidence owns metric calculations.
- Inventory general AI, gallery-editor and conversational-planning provider paths before selecting existing ownership. Reuse Goal Cycle and conversational-plan revisions/checkpoints rather than create another plan engine.
- Use bounded fact loading, gap handling, proposal, validation, review, execution delegation and assessment with durable stopping/error states. Scheduled triggers initiate bounded runs; the process need not remain continuously reasoning.
- Define a versioned context/result envelope with creator identity, brief, asset references, capabilities, evidence, plan revision, allowed result types, cancellation and budget. Application identity and approval evidence cannot be supplied as trusted model assertions.
- MCP remains a thin authenticated adapter over the same operations. Verify scoped reads as well as writes. Planning approval must not grant external publishing authority.
- Keep imported text and tool content untrusted. Avoid credentials and unnecessary raw patron/source content in model context or traces.
- Recheck current revision, authorization and cancellation before mutations. Replay returns saved results; retries do not regenerate approved payloads.
- Configuration promotion is explicit and reversible after P3 evidence; old evaluation budgets or provider choices do not authorize new paid runs.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary seam: authenticated management operations through real services and isolated database state, including prepare, revise, preview, approval, cancellation and resumed status.
- Reuse conversational-planning API restart/replay/concurrency and tenant-isolation cases, Goal Cycle checkpoints and gallery-editor stale-change/budget tests.
- Thin native/MCP parity tests prove equivalent authorization and resulting records; arbitrary MCP requests cannot bypass service rules.
- Provider-adapter tests cover budget exhaustion, timeout, malformed output, injection attempts and cancellation without fabricated completion.

## Out of Scope

A second scheduler/library/permission ledger, custom model training, general-purpose agent framework, unauthenticated MCP access, unattended publishing permissions inferred from chat, production model activation.

## Further Notes

Owns the shared envelope baseline with other contract owners and integrates accepted P3 candidate configurations. Can build against versioned P1/P4/P5 doubles. Exit: native and MCP clients can operate one saved plan with equivalent authority, survive restart, and truthfully expose completion or limitation.

The parent issue defines shared contract ownership, parallel waves, integration acceptance and shared-file serialization. Test boundaries were confirmed by the user: shared authenticated application operations, with focused connector and AI-quality evaluation seams. Preserve existing safety, approval and release requirements; reconcile older conflicting priorities with the current artist-manager direction.

Related pipelines: [P1](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/6) · [P3](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/8) · [P4](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/9) · [P5](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/10) · [P6](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/11). Integration dependencies are described above; these links do not make all work wait for other pipelines to finish.

items.title: No way to offboard a repo or team: its chunks, graph, memory, tasks and audit rows stay forever
items.body:
Part of #2365.

### No repo/team/tenant offboarding: nothing removes an onboarded repo's chunks, trace graph, memory, tasks or audit rows, and the graph retention reap only runs on that repo's next ingest

'Remove repo X' or 'remove team Y' has no code path. Disabling a repo leaves its {schema}.chunks embeddings, its Dgraph trace graph (which nothing reaps once ingests stop), repo-scoped memories, facts, entities and edges, pipeline.tasks descriptions and context_bundle, assembly/station runs, pipeline.audit_log, digest_posts and plans in place. 'Remove tenant X' is a whole-deployment teardown. Even that leaves the GCP Secret Manager containers (prevent_destroy), up to 30 days of DB backups, the Dgraph PV and any Slack messages already posted (a trash-can reaction can delete single bot posts: webhook-slack-events.ts:72-113). There is no checklist for it.

**Evidence**
- `grep 'method: "DELETE"' in apps/lore-api/src/transport/routes: only agent-definitions and plans; no repo, team or chunk-schema removal; grep offboard|removeRepo|deleteRepo = 0 hits`
- `libs/shared/src/outbound/project/settings/settings-pg.ts:101 (the only DELETE FROM lore.repos, used when merging a renamed repo)`
- `apps/lore-api/src/work/chunks/prune-orphans.ts:53 + libs/shared/src/outbound/project/chunks/chunks-pg.ts:70 (chunks are deleted per file path for a repo that is still ingesting, never per repo)`
- `apps/stations/src/work/ingest/ingest.ts:117-140 + libs/shared/src/work/spec-trace/graph-retention.ts:8,22-37 (Dgraph reap is per repo, overlays/failures only, triggered by an ingest of that repo, so an offboarded repo is never reaped and its specs/tests/coverage nodes stay)`
- `memory.entities.repo / memories.repo / pipeline.tasks.target_repo rows have no repo-scoped delete`
- `explore:governance-evidence: tenant = whole deployment; secrets.tf prevent_destroy; db_backups bucket 30d`

**Proposed change**
Decide what offboarding means (soft disable versus full purge, and how long audit is retained). Then add an admin 'offboard repo' job: DELETE {schema}.chunks WHERE repo, a Dgraph drop of every node with repo==X, memory purge WHERE repo (using the ordered purge from the first finding), task/run rows anonymised or deleted per policy, and lore.repos last, with a dry-run count report first. Write runbooks/offboard-tenant.md for whole-deployment teardown that covers backups, PVs, the Secret Manager containers and Slack.


_Found in a codebase audit on 2026-10-01 (main @ 0fabcf525); each point was checked against the code by a second reviewer._

<!-- lore-backlog-reconciled: 3971/full-review-v1 -->

## Backlog reconciliation

Reviewed against main at `3cb0d923c43d05e3ba03adb67b73c3acc61bce2d` using independent Codex review. Assessment: **missing**.

No admin offboard job, multi-store dry run or tenant offboarding runbook was found. Current memory deletion is soft, so removing a repo/settings row alone cannot satisfy the requested erasure across chunks, graph, memory, tasks/runs, digests and plans.

### Remaining work

Define disable-versus-purge/audit policy and implement the ordered multi-store repo/team purge with dry-run counts and lore.repos last; document tenant teardown including backups/PVs/secrets/Slack and current external stores.

### Evidence

- [libs/server-core/src/work/memory/memory-read.ts:84–96](https://github.com/re-cinq/lore/blob/3cb0d923c43d05e3ba03adb67b73c3acc61bce2d/libs/server-core/src/work/memory/memory-read.ts#L84-L96)

Source review is not a claim of successful behavioral or production verification.
