items.title: Milestone 1: Foundations (auth, Workspaces, RBAC, API contract pipeline, UI shell)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

Tessle has no working foundation. A person cannot sign in, create or join a Workspace, or see an App list, and the frontend and backend are separate scaffolds with no shared API contract. Every later milestone (data sources, forms, reports, pages, AI) depends on identity, tenant isolation and a typed contract existing first.

## Solution

Deliver the platform foundation: email-OTP and Google sign-in with cookie-based sessions, Workspaces with Memberships and roles, an App list per Workspace, strict Workspace isolation, and a typed OpenAPI to Hey API pipeline with a CI drift check. The frontend is a Next.js shell offering sign-in, a Workspace switcher, a members page and an App list. Both projects live in one monorepo with CI. See `docs/architecture.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs 0001 to 0004.

## User Stories

1. As a visitor, I want to enter my email and receive a one-time code, so that I can sign in without a password
2. As a visitor, I want to enter the 6-digit code, so that I am signed in
3. As a visitor, I want a new code to invalidate the previous one, so that old codes cannot be reused
4. As a visitor, I want codes to expire after 10 minutes, so that leaked codes are short-lived
5. As a visitor, I want a code locked after 5 wrong attempts, so that guessing is impractical
6. As a visitor, I want the sign-in response identical whether or not my email is known, so that accounts cannot be discovered
7. As a visitor, I want to sign in with Google, so that I can skip the code
8. As a User, I want my first sign-in to create my account, so that no separate registration is needed
9. As a User, I want to stay signed in via a refresh token for up to 7 days, so that I am not prompted constantly
10. As a User, I want my session to renew silently, so that short access tokens do not interrupt me
11. As a User, I want to sign out, so that my session ends immediately on this device
12. As a User, I want to sign out everywhere, so that I can end all sessions if a device is lost
13. As a User, I want a reused old refresh token to revoke the whole session family, so that a stolen token is contained
14. As a User, I want tokens stored only in HttpOnly cookies, so that scripts cannot read them
15. As a User, I want state-changing requests protected by a CSRF token, so that other sites cannot act as me
16. As a User, I want to create a Workspace, so that my team has a space of its own
17. As a Workspace owner, I want to be its owner automatically, so that I can administer it
18. As an owner or admin, I want to invite someone by email, so that they can join the Workspace
19. As an invitee, I want the invitation sent by real email, so that I actually receive it
20. As an invitee, I want to accept an invitation after signing in, so that I gain a Membership
21. As an owner or admin, I want to assign a role (owner, admin, builder, editor, viewer) to a Membership, so that access matches responsibility
22. As an owner or admin, I want to remove a Membership, so that former members lose access
23. As a demoted member, I want my reduced access to apply immediately, so that stale permissions do not linger
24. As a User in several Workspaces, I want to switch the active Workspace, so that I work in the right context
25. As a User, I want to see only Workspaces I belong to, so that other organizations stay invisible
26. As a builder or above, I want to create an App in a Workspace, so that I can later group Definitions
27. As any member, I want to see the Apps I may access, so that I can open them
28. As a viewer, I want to be unable to create or change Apps, so that roles are enforced
29. As a member of Workspace A, I want to be unable to read Workspace B's data even through a missing filter, so that tenant isolation holds
30. As an owner, I want the last owner of a Workspace protected from removal or demotion, so that a Workspace is never orphaned
31. As a developer, I want the frontend client and React Query hooks generated from the OpenAPI spec, so that I never hand-write API calls
32. As a developer, I want CI to fail when generated client code differs from the committed one, so that the contract cannot drift
33. As a developer, I want sign-in emails sent by a queue consumer with retries and a dead-letter queue, so that mail failures do not break requests
34. As a developer, I want a trace id carried from the HTTP request into queued jobs, so that I can follow a request end to end
35. As a developer, I want one command to start Postgres, Redis (AOF on) and RabbitMQ locally, so that setup is quick
36. As a developer, I want a monorepo with one CI pipeline, so that frontend and backend changes are verified together
37. As an admin, I want repeated sign-in or code requests rate limited, so that email bombing and brute force are blocked

## Implementation Decisions

- Monorepo at the repo root with separate backend, frontend and schemas areas, on JDK 25; remove the Mongo starters and the MySQL, Oracle and SQL Server drivers from the platform module.
- Modules: identity (Users, OTP, tokens, Google sign-in), workspace (Workspaces, Memberships, roles, Apps), mail (queue consumer), plus API and security configuration.
- Tenancy (ADR 0001): shared Postgres schema, `workspace_id` on tenant-owned rows, row-level security driven by a per-transaction active Workspace setting, failing closed when unset. Flyway owns migrations; JPA for platform metadata.
- Tokens (ADR 0004): access JWT 10 minutes and refresh JWT 7 days in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookies; refresh cookie path scoped to the refresh endpoint. The access token carries user id and active Workspace id only. Refresh token hashes live in Redis, rotate on every use, with reuse revoking the family. Membership role is read per request through a short-TTL Redis cache. Redis runs with AOF.
- OTP: 6-digit code stored hashed in Postgres, 10 minute expiry, 5 attempts, per-email send limit, uniform responses.
- CSRF: double-submit token on state-changing requests. The browser reaches the backend through a same-site `/api` rewrite in Next.js.
- Rate limiting in Redis on sign-in and code endpoints.
- Mail: RabbitMQ consumer calling `JavaMailSender` against Resend SMTP; credentials from environment variables in a git-ignored env file; one global sender. Idempotent consumer, backoff retries, dead-letter queue. Sending only to your own account is possible until a domain is verified in Resend.
- Roles: owner, admin, builder, editor, viewer. Only owner and admin manage Memberships; builder and above create Apps; viewer is read-only. At least one owner must remain.
- Contract: springdoc-openapi (Boot 4 line) produces the spec; `@hey-api/openapi-ts` (pinned exactly, with the TanStack Query plugin) generates the client; an npm script regenerates it and CI fails on diff. Definition JSON Schemas folder is created but empty in M1.
- Frontend: Next.js App Router shell with sign-in, Workspace switcher, members and roles page, and App list. Read the bundled Next.js docs before writing code. Visual design goes through the impeccable plugin.
- Compose provides Postgres, Redis (AOF) and RabbitMQ. No mail catcher.
- Versions as listed in `docs/architecture.md`.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests exercise external behavior through the HTTP API and assert observable outcomes (status codes, cookies, persisted state visible through the API), never internals.
- Primary seam: the backend HTTP API, tested with Testcontainers against real Postgres, Redis and RabbitMQ. Covers the OTP flow (expiry, attempts, invalidation, uniform responses), cookie token lifecycle (rotation, reuse revocation, sign-out everywhere), Workspace and Membership operations and role enforcement, last-owner protection, immediate effect of role changes, and cross-Workspace isolation including a query that omits its filter, proving RLS holds.
- Mail is verified by asserting the consumer invokes the mail sender interface through a fake; SMTP itself is not tested.
- Second seam: the OpenAPI to Hey API drift check, run in CI on every PR. Frontend gets a smoke test only.
- No prior art exists in the codebase; only a generated context-load test.

## Out of Scope

Data sources, the query compiler, Forms, Reports, Pages and the AI builder; messaging; workflows; SSO (OIDC/SAML); API keys and webhooks; per-Workspace branding or sender addresses; the four-database CI matrix; sandboxed custom code; app export/import.

## Further Notes

A Resend account with a verified domain is needed before invitation and OTP emails reach people other than the account owner. Redis 8 is tri-licensed; Valkey is a drop-in alternative. Hey API does not yet list TypeScript 7 as a supported peer, so expect warnings or pin TypeScript 6. The repo root currently contains a stray `node_modules`, `package.json` and `bun.lock` that should be reviewed during the monorepo cleanup.

items.title: [CONN-CRM-003] Add a qualified HubSpot inbound adapter for the SMB relationship import
items.body:
Todo-ID: CONN-CRM-003
State: OPEN

## Outcome
Add a HubSpot-specific inbound adapter that feeds the proposed SMB-CRM-007 mapped and provenanced relationship import/export workflow. A company admin connects one HubSpot account, confirms the provider portal identity, binds it to one HCM company, chooses the supported company/contact projection, maps fields, previews the exact import outcomes, and activates a recoverable inbound sync. HubSpot remains the source for its CRM objects and pipeline activity. This ticket adds no second generic import engine and does not claim a production HubSpot connector or business-party registry already exists.

## Workflow, field authority, and shared owners
From Admin → Integrations (proposed provider detail extension), the admin enters the proposed HubSpot connection flow, reviews requested scopes and distribution status, confirms the returned portal/account identifier, and binds it to one HCM company. The exact current-platform authorization flow must be established in the test portal before production activation. The supported object/field matrix is explicit and versioned. HubSpot owns external record IDs, its pipeline/activity state, and fields the tenant marks HubSpot-authoritative. HCM owns business-party roles/sites, contact affiliations, local access and review decisions. The initial direction is inbound observation or staging into the SMB-CRM-007 target. No automatic email/name matching, merge, contact deletion, or outbound field write is allowed. A later outbound action must be separately authorized against field ownership and current revision.

Reuse `internal/connectivity/application/installation.go` for connection lifecycle, `internal/connectivity/mapping` and `mappingprofile` for field maps, `syncjob` for checkpoints, `providerreceipt`/`observe` for source evidence, and `operation`, reconciliation, capacity, and health owners for transport outcomes. The relationship import target is SMB-CRM-007 (#3527); it owns generic mapping, provenance, preview, row recovery, and import/export semantics. This ticket owns HubSpot portal binding, provider descriptors and object/field fixtures, supported pagination or event-to-observation translation, and account-specific authorization diagnostics. Existing `internal/domains/crm` is recruiting/talent CRM and must not be repurposed as the customer registry. Shared connector authentication, schema, mapping, webhook, cursor, replay, and health engines remain shared prerequisites.

## Qualification and interaction
Use the current HubSpot Developer Platform app path and minimum required scopes only after verifying them in a test portal. The linked official page documents the legacy public-app path and is historical context, not instructions for new app setup. Verify current OAuth installation, scope classification, allowlisted or Marketplace distribution, and review/unverified-install behavior directly before enabling a tenant. Before activation, qualify current platform registration, OAuth and refresh behavior, exact company/contact endpoints and scopes, API quota/retry semantics, app review/distribution, target account eligibility, and schema/version change behavior using a test portal. If the installed app is unverified or the account lacks a required feature, show a qualification hold and do not imply production support.

The proposed flow shows Connect, verified portal identity, Bind company, Select objects, Map, Preview, Activate, Health, Reconnect, and Disconnect. Preview identifies creates, updates, unchanged rows, ambiguous records, forbidden fields, and source revisions. Loading, empty schema, denied scope, wrong portal/company, revoked auth, stale schema, rate limiting, conflicting revision, duplicate event, and expired cursor each have an explicit state and recovery action. Cursor expiry requires snapshot reconciliation before resume. Disconnect fences new sync and keeps pending operations inspectable. Reuse existing Admin integration/operations pages and shared forms, tables, alerts, and dialogs; add a provider detail extension only where needed. Keep keyboard order and focus visible, associate errors with inputs, announce async state, support en-US/de-DE/RTL, and fit narrow responsive layouts.

## Acceptance and rollout
Tests prove a wrong portal cannot bind to another company; repeated provider record/event identity and revision does not create duplicate parties; ambiguous email/name matches require review; API permission failure does not advance the cursor; revoked access pauses before external calls; and stale schema/cursor requires repair or reconciliation instead of silently skipping data. Cross-company external IDs cannot be resolved by guessing a tenant. Require SMB-CORE-002 and SMB-CRM-001/003/007, plus the shared connection, schema, mapping, observation/sync, and health prerequisites before activation. Roll out as an allowlisted pilot with read-only probes, a kill switch, and explicit support matrix. No HubSpot CRM replacement, marketing campaign/sender, consent-law engine, automatic merge, broad bidirectional sync, or plan-independent eligibility claim is included.

Source: https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/apps/legacy-apps/public-apps/overview

## Delivery verification
Add `TestTodo_CONN_CRM_003` as the primary contract test, plus named integration, security, recovery and served-browser cases for the acceptance criteria above. Qualification-only work must prove fail-closed enablement and preserve an explicit go/no-go result. Record exact packages, commands and results in the canonical TODO evidence. Inspect the served setup and health surfaces at desktop, 390 px and 320 px, in en-US, de-DE and Arabic RTL, using existing light/dark themes, keyboard navigation, focus restoration and announced errors. Render-only tests do not replace this browser evidence.

items.body:
**Stable key:** PP-09B
**Owner role:** Creative and fulfillment — production maintainer; named implementer and accountable reviewer recorded at kickoff.
**Priority:** P0 — A bundle must prove exactly which approved inputs and output files it contains
**Required for v1:** Yes. **Implementation state:** Planned.

## Current evidence
Live inspection 2026-10-10: main is [24fb18a](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/tree/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd). The complete tracked tree is [README](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/blob/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd/README.md), [OWNERSHIP](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/blob/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd/docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP.md), and [ACCEPTANCE](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/blob/24fb18a1fc54d34ce71e99a2162d62ebca3a52cd/docs/architecture/ACCEPTANCE.md). No AGENTS.md, source, runtime/package manifest, tests or CI exist. #1 is the original WP06 work package; merged [PR #2](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/print-production/pull/2) added architecture documentation only. This issue is planned implementation work, not completion evidence.

The [shared catalog](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/blob/main/docs/contract-catalog.md) names ProductionBundle; [shared-contracts #24](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/24) is planned. No canonical executable schema, manifest writer or bundle evidence exists here.

## Scope / non-goals
Build exportArtifactBundle orchestration and getArtifactManifestStatus using canonical ProductionBundle. Join immutable source/template/spec/renderer/font/approval/personalization references, reports and file hashes into the final bundle; atomically publish through storage. Do not invent ProductionArtifactSet or copy shared schemas.

Production owns composition, exact layout/text, templates, personalization, preflight, output storage and manifests. It consumes external approvals and immutable creative/event inputs. Customer identity/order/payment/approval authority, research, GPT Image generation, supplier ordering, pricing and the authoritative ledger remain outside this repository. No paid provider work is authorized.

## Acceptance IDs and expected outcome
Global ART-04 (all files and hashes), ART-05 (asset provenance/approval), with local PP-09B lineage and hashing rules; shared-contracts owns CON-01 schemas.
[Master acceptance definitions](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/ff1f6d2df816ebbff34742f51be728fcb5c28cb5/planning/acceptance-checklist.md) and [JSON evidence tracker](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/integration-evals/blob/ff1f6d2df816ebbff34742f51be728fcb5c28cb5/planning/acceptance-checklist.json) retain their existing global IDs, priorities and owner roles. This run does not change that tracker.

- [ ] PP-09B.1: Manifest carries schema and bundle ID/revision, tenant/project-safe scope, design/artwork/approval/fact refs and hashes, composition revision, product/template/spec identity, renderer/tool/font versions, exact formatting/repair policy, source lineage and personalization row/batch scope. Preserve privacy through scoped refs/digests rather than unneeded raw attendee values.
- [ ] PP-09B.2: List every shipped file with safe relative path, media type, byte length, SHA-256, dimensions/units/DPI/profile and raster/vector characteristics. Include final preflight rule/report refs, warnings/errors/information and explicit passed/failed/unsupported/unknown state; presence of files alone is not readiness.
- [ ] PP-09B.3: Hash protocol is unambiguous: hash payload files first; canonicalize manifest without its own digest or final ZIP hash; compute detached manifest digest; package payloads plus manifest; compute final ZIP digest in detached metadata/status. No self-hash recursion or omitted/unlisted payloads. Canonical shared hashing rules win after review.
- [ ] PP-09B.4: Keep source-artwork, preview, composed-output, manifest and bundle hashes distinct. Changed composition/personalization/spec produces a new identity and cannot reuse an unrelated approval or downstream purchase authorization.
- [ ] PP-09B.5: Only complete output sets with passing mandatory checks and current permission applicability are published eligible. Retrieval distinguishes processing/failed/partial/completed and readiness; validate every stored reference and hash without starting new exports.
- [ ] PP-09B.6: Provide a verification command that consumes an existing bundle/manifest, validates canonical schema, recomputes all hashes, rejects extra/missing/tampered files and reports typed errors. Read-only verification cannot count as a new production attempt.

## Approach and migration implications
Consume accepted schema/types from PP-01B and SC-07C. Assemble file hashes after export, produce canonical manifest bytes, ask PP-09A's packager for ZIP, then publish via PP-10A. Cross-reference exact operation/trace/evidence IDs without pricing or authority claims. Maintain supported-old-schema read fixtures and explicit migrations that preserve old immutable manifests.

## Relationships
**Parent:** #1 (WP06 / PP-EPIC).
**Blocked by:** #10 (storage), #15 (exporters); [shared-contracts #24](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/24), [#8](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/8)
**Blocks:** #3 (PP-12 release gate); downstream edges are maintained in #1's dependency and coverage map.
**Related:** [fulfillment-connectors #1](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/1), [shared-contracts #29](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/shared-contracts/issues/29).

## Executable validation
Required implementation commands; these do not exist and were not run during backlog triage. PP-01A must establish the dispatcher and fail on unknown/missing suites. Run in a clean pinned checkout with no provider credentials.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm run verify -- --suite manifests --mode offline --evidence-dir out/evidence
```

Produce a complete bundle, validate shared schema, unpack it and recompute every file/manifest/ZIP hash with an independent verifier. Alter/remove/add one file, change product units/spec and present stale approval; assert failures. Fetch completed status twice and prove identical immutable refs with no new render/export attempt.

## Required evidence for closure
Attach canonical contract pin, sample manifest/bundle/detached metadata, hash-protocol specification, lineage graph and independent pass/tamper/missing/extra-file verification reports. Include merged implementation SHA, exact runtime/dependency/shared-contracts pins, fixture digests, command/exit-code logs and sanitized durable evidence links. Record limitations and reviewer sign-off. No unchecked criterion or missing dependency evidence is complete; documentation/mocks alone do not verify global end-to-end criteria.


## Production & commerce cross-repository audit correction — 2026-10-10

**Single accountable artifact owner:** PP-09B / this issue (#16) owns the published canonical ProductionBundle and the all-file/manifest/bundle hash evidence for ART-04. PP-07 (#11) owns preflight findings and PP-09A (#15) owns renderer/export file production; both feed their verified results and files into this issue. PP-12F (#19) owns integration-corpus orchestration, not ART-04 acceptance ownership. No artifact is eligible for handoff until this issue publishes and independently verifies the actual canonical bundle.

**Required downstream dependency chain:** print-production #11 and #15 → this issue (#16) publishes the actual ProductionBundle → [fulfillment-connectors #10](https://github.com/Jevelopers-neatHack-2026/fulfillment-connectors/issues/10) validates that actual bundle and unchanged hashes with its real offline consumer validator → print-production #19 runs the pinned integration fixtures against that accepted validator result → print-production #3 applies the release gate. A proposed manifest, local mock, or absent validator is a blocker; fulfillment sandbox/live order evidence remains separately owned and is not required by the offline production gate.

**PP-09B closure evidence:** close #16 when this producer has attached the actual published canonical ProductionBundle and manifest with pinned source/schema/tool revisions, complete payload and manifest hash inventory, PP-09B command and exit logs, independent pass/tamper/missing/extra-file verification output, and reviewer sign-off. The fulfillment-connectors #10 unchanged-hash offline consumer result is downstream evidence: PP-12F #19 collects and pins it, and PP-12 #3 assesses it. That downstream validator result is not a prerequisite for closing this producer issue.

**Audit state:** backlog prepared only; PP-09B implementation and its own closure evidence remain pending. Keep #16 open until its producer evidence above is attached. The deliverable sequence remains actual #16 bundle → fulfillment #10 real offline validator → PP #19 → PP #3.

items.title: [Spec] P1 — Intake and reusable library
items.body:
# P1 — Intake and reusable library

Parent specification and coordination: https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/5

Status: ready for manager decomposition after assignment. No implementation, paid experiments or rollout dispatched by this issue.

## Problem Statement

Artists cannot conveniently reuse work if uploads lose context, recovery requires repeated transfers, or imported and new assets behave differently. Partial recovery can also be mistaken for a complete backup.

## Solution

Make artist-controlled imports and direct uploads converge on a private, reusable catalogue with stable asset identity, preserved source contexts, visible readiness and retry-safe recovery.

## User Stories

1. As an artist, I want to upload new work once and reuse it, so that subsequent releases do not require another transfer.
2. As an artist, I want to resume interrupted intake, so that completed work is preserved.
3. As an artist, I want to retry a lost upload confirmation safely, so that I receive the same usable asset.
4. As an artist, I want to recognize filenames and source labels after reload, so that I can find the right work.
5. As an artist, I want to import selected or recent posts before the entire archive, so that I can prepare a release immediately.
6. As an artist, I want to retain distinct source publications for shared media, so that captions and publication history are not lost.
7. As an artist, I want to keep previews and originals distinct, so that a similar image is not mistaken for an interchangeable asset.
8. As an artist, I want to see unavailable or partial media clearly, so that I know which work needs repair.
9. As an artist, I want to export retained files with their available context, so that I can recover them independently.
10. As an artist, I want to retain convenient Patreon intake through credential changes, so that security improvements do not create a manual reupload chain.

## Implementation Decisions

- Own asset readiness, source/version association, durable intake metadata and recovery. Reuse existing MediaAsset, canonical shared-media history, gallery SHA suppression and export services; their existence does not mean intake-wide replay and association are complete.
- Preserve direct presigned private tenant-scoped object storage. Revalidate commits against stored bytes and ownership. A repeated successful commit should return its saved result without silently accepting a different payload.
- Preserve source snapshots separately from Relay-owned presentation and reuse state. Exact-byte reuse must not expose another creator's assets or erase distinct source contexts; similarity is not authority to merge variants.
- Publish the reusable-asset contract with identity, source revision, readiness, retained rendition/original status, labels, audience classification and permitted retrieval. Consumer references must remain stable across retries.
- Make useful selected work available while broader history continues. Preserve current Patreon repair, reconciliation and live access guards; do not change release evidence or restart its queue.
- Inventory current branch behavior before slicing filename, batching, recovery, limits and staging issues; active workspace changes may already address some earlier findings.
- Before changing credential custody, document parity for existing imports, new posts, restricted media, browser closed/offline behavior, retries and user actions. If parity fails, harden the current approach rather than force migration.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary seam: authenticated intake and Library reads with isolated database state and a controlled object-store adapter.
- Prove lost-response replay, reload/restart recovery, missing bytes, mismatched commit data, expired presigns, wrong creator, preserved source contexts and distinct variants.
- Prove imported work enters preparation without public Relay publication or download/reupload, and private intake leaves patron permission behavior unchanged.
- Prior art: upload route/storage tests, private staging access, canonical shared-media integration, SHA duplicate suppression and Patreon media-repair tests.

## Out of Scope

New fan entitlement services, new external sources without a scoped demand/capability case, replacing the storage architecture, global cross-tenant deduplication, publication approval, full backup claims without restoration proof.

## Further Notes

Can start inventory, failure fixtures and upload/recovery slices independently. Supplies asset/provenance contract to P2/P4/P5/P6. Integrates after the shared contract gate; preserves the current Patreon acceptance gates. Exit: one uploaded and one imported item remain privately usable with context across retry/restart and prepare a release without retransferring bytes.

The parent issue defines shared contract ownership, parallel waves, integration acceptance and shared-file serialization. Test boundaries were confirmed by the user: shared authenticated application operations, with focused connector and AI-quality evaluation seams. Preserve existing safety, approval and release requirements; reconcile older conflicting priorities with the current artist-manager direction.

Related pipelines: [P2](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/7) · [P3](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/8) · [P4](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/9) · [P5](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/10) · [P6](https://github.com/JTBAZ/relay/issues/11). Integration dependencies are described above; these links do not make all work wait for other pipelines to finish.

items.title: Noisy-neighbour protection (per-tenant rate limits & quotas)

milestone.title: Later
milestone.description: Unscheduled. Pulled into an R milestone when a customer or a regulation needs it. Holds the open remainder of M0-M2, M6-M9 and MVP 1 (MVP 1 items keep the release:MVP 1 label).

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

The platform runs a shared-schema, shared-runtime deployment: one Kubernetes footprint, one PostgreSQL 16 cluster, one Redis, one NATS JetStream, serving every hospital tenant in a country region. There are no per-tenant limits of any kind today. Any tenant's behaviour is therefore every tenant's problem.

The realistic triggers are mundane, not malicious. A hospital runs a one-off migration and fires 400,000 patient-record writes through the API in an afternoon. A tenant's badly-written integration polls the appointment list every second from forty terminals. A LabConnect analyser bridge retries a failing upload in a tight loop. A tenant enables an export that generates a full-history report per patient. Any of these saturates connection-pool slots, Redis memory or JetStream consumer capacity, and every other hospital on the deployment sees timeouts.

The consequence is not uniform across products. If MediCore's OPD queue is slow, clinics run late. If EmergencyConnect is slow, an ambulance dispatch or a pre-alert to the receiving ED is delayed — that is a patient-safety event, and this platform's reliability position is explicit that EmergencyConnect gets its own capacity headroom. A tenant whose ward nurses cannot chart because another hospital is running a bulk import has a legitimate service-credit claim and, if it recurs, a reason to leave.

Affected roles: every clinical user of every co-tenant, the ambulance crew and dispatcher on the life-critical path, the platform SRE with no lever short of blocking a tenant entirely, and the hospital admin whose own integration is the cause and who currently gets no warning that they are approaching a limit.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** platform operator running a shared multi-tenant clinical deployment
**I want** per-tenant rate limits, concurrency caps and resource quotas, tier-configurable, with a protected reservation for life-critical traffic and clear feedback to the tenant approaching a limit
**So that** no single hospital's workload can degrade another hospital's clinical service, and EmergencyConnect retains guaranteed headroom under any load condition.

### Scope

**In scope**

* Per-tenant request rate limiting at the API edge, keyed by tenant and by route class (read, write, bulk, export, integration), implemented as a token bucket with burst allowance.
* Per-tenant concurrency caps on expensive operations: report generation, bulk import, data export, FHIR bundle assembly, analytics extracts.
* Per-tenant database resource control: a bounded share of connection-pool slots and a statement-timeout profile per route class, so a single tenant cannot occupy the pool.
* Per-tenant NATS JetStream consumer limits and per-tenant Redis memory accounting with key-prefix quotas.
* A protected reservation: EmergencyConnect routes are served from a separate limiter pool and a separate connection-pool partition that other products' limits cannot consume, and are exempt from tenant-level throttling for dispatch-critical operations.
* Tier-driven configuration through the subscription/entitlement model, with per-tenant overrides and a documented default for each tier.
* Standards-compliant client feedback: `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`, `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` headers, plus a machine-readable error code so the offline-first mobile clients can back off intelligently rather than hammering.
* Soft-limit warnings at 80% of quota surfaced to the hospital admin in the console and via `TenantQuotaWarning`, so the tenant can act before being throttled.
* Fail-open behaviour if the limiter's own backing store is unavailable — availability of a clinical system outranks quota enforcement, with an alert.

**Out of scope**

* Autoscaling and cluster capacity planning (KEDA/HPA policy) — owned by the Infrastructure epic; this issue bounds demand, it does not add supply.
* Detection and scoring of tenant degradation — issue #33 provides the signals and health view; this issue enforces limits and publishes quota events into it.
* Usage metering for subscription billing — the Subscriptions epic; billing counters have different accuracy and retention requirements and must not be derived from limiter counters.
* Per-user or per-device abuse controls and bot mitigation — owned by the Security epic at the Cloudflare/Istio layer.
* Tenant isolation correctness — issue #32; a throttled request must still be a correctly isolated request, and #32's suite covers that.

---

## Recommended Solution

Enforce at two layers, deliberately: a coarse edge limiter and a fine application limiter. The edge (Istio/Envoy with a Redis-backed rate-limit service) sheds obviously excessive load before it consumes Go worker capacity; the application limiter in Gin middleware understands route class, tenant tier and the EmergencyConnect reservation, which the edge cannot express.

**Algorithm.** Token bucket in Redis via a Lua script so check-and-decrement is atomic across replicas:

```lua
-- KEYS[1] = ratelimit:{tenant}:{class}
-- ARGV = capacity, refill_per_sec, now_ms, cost
-- returns {allowed, remaining, reset_ms}
```

Token bucket rather than fixed window because clinical traffic is bursty by nature — a ward round produces twenty writes in ten seconds and then nothing for an hour, and a fixed window would reject legitimate bursts while permitting sustained abuse.

**Configuration** is resolved from the entitlement model, never compiled in:

```yaml
tiers:
  standard:
    read:        { rate: 200/s,  burst: 400 }
    write:       { rate: 50/s,   burst: 100 }
    bulk:        { rate: 5/s,    burst: 10, max_concurrent: 2 }
    export:      { max_concurrent: 1, max_per_day: 20 }
    integration: { rate: 100/s,  burst: 200 }
    db_pool_share: 0.15
  enterprise:
    read:        { rate: 800/s,  burst: 1600 }
    ...
reservations:
  emergencyconnect:
    pool_partition: dedicated
    exempt_routes: [ "POST /api/v1/ambulance/dispatch",
                     "POST /api/v1/ambulance/{id}/handover",
                     "POST /api/v1/emergency/pre-alert" ]
```

**Database protection.** A per-tenant semaphore in front of the pgx pool caps a tenant's concurrent checkouts at `db_pool_share × pool_size`, with a bounded wait and a fast `503 TENANT_DB_SATURATED` rather than an unbounded queue that manifests as an eight-second timeout. Statement timeouts are set per route class via `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` inside the same transaction that sets `app.tenant_id`, so a runaway report query is killed at 30 seconds rather than holding a slot indefinitely. EmergencyConnect uses a physically separate pgx pool so its slots cannot be exhausted by any other product's tenants.

Data model:

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenant_quota (
  tenant_id      UUID NOT NULL,
  route_class    TEXT NOT NULL,
  rate_per_sec   INT,
  burst          INT,
  max_concurrent INT,
  max_per_day    INT,
  db_pool_share  NUMERIC(3,2),
  source         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (source IN ('tier_default','override')),
  effective_from TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, route_class)
);

CREATE TABLE tenant_quota_event (
  id          UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id   UUID NOT NULL,
  route_class TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('warned','throttled','saturated')),
  observed    NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  limit_value NUMERIC NOT NULL,
  window_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  window_end   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);
```

API surface:

* `GET /api/v1/tenant/quota` — the tenant's own limits and current consumption (hospital admin can self-diagnose).
* `GET /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/quota`
* `PUT /api/v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/quota` — override, requires an expiry so temporary uplifts for a migration do not become permanent.
* `GET /api/v1/admin/quota/top-consumers?window=1h` — operator triage view.

Events: publishes `TenantQuotaWarning` (80% sustained), `TenantThrottled` and `TenantDbSaturated` on NATS JetStream; consumed by issue #33's health evaluator (a throttled tenant is a degraded tenant) and by the alerting router. `TenantDbSaturated` for any tenant pages the platform on-call, because it indicates the shared pool sizing is wrong, not merely that one tenant is busy.

OpenFGA:

```
type tenant_quota
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define self_viewer: admin from tenant     # sees own limits and usage only
    define operator_viewer: sre from platform
    define overrider: sre from platform
```

Sequencing: depends on the tenant-scoped middleware (tenant identity must be resolved before the limiter can key on it), on the subscription/entitlement model for tier defaults, and on the EmergencyConnect dispatch routes existing so the reservation list is real. Should land before the first multi-tenant production deployment carrying more than one live hospital. Issue #33 consumes its events.

Risks and mitigations. (1) *Throttling a clinical write during an emergency.* Mitigated by the exempt-route reservation, by writes carrying a higher cost weighting but a generous burst, and by never throttling an authenticated single-record clinical write below a floor that a human being could plausibly exceed — limits target machine traffic, and the route classes make that distinction explicit. (2) *Redis failure taking the platform down.* Mitigated by fail-open: if the limiter store is unreachable, requests pass and `ratelimit_fail_open_total` alerts immediately. (3) *Offline-first mobile clients retrying a 429 into a storm on reconnection.* Mitigated by honouring `Retry-After` in the shared Flutter/React Native sync client with exponential backoff and jitter, tested explicitly. (4) *A legitimate migration being blocked.* Mitigated by time-boxed operator overrides with a mandatory expiry, and by the 80% warning giving the hospital admin advance notice to request one.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a standard-tier tenant whose bulk route class is limited to 5 requests/second with a burst of 10
**When** their integration submits 200 bulk write requests in one second
**Then** 10 are accepted, the remainder receive `429` with `Retry-After` and accurate `RateLimit-*` headers, no other tenant's p95 latency on any route rises by more than 10% during the burst, a `TenantThrottled` event is published, and the tenant's own `GET /api/v1/tenant/quota` reflects the exhausted bucket.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a tenant has fully exhausted its rate limit and its database pool share during a runaway import
**When** an ambulance dispatcher at that same tenant submits `POST /api/v1/ambulance/dispatch`
**Then** the request is served from the EmergencyConnect reservation — a separate limiter pool and a separate connection-pool partition — completes within its normal p95 latency budget, is never throttled, and the dispatch proceeds; the exemption is recorded so it can be audited rather than silently applied.

### Edge Cases

* The Redis limiter store becomes unreachable — the limiter fails open, all requests pass, `ratelimit_fail_open_total` increments and pages on-call; no clinical request is rejected because the quota system is unhealthy.
* A tenant sits at exactly 80% of quota for a sustained window — a single `TenantQuotaWarning` is emitted with hysteresis, not one per request, and the console shows an actionable message naming the route class.
* A hospital admin requests a temporary uplift for a data migration — the override is applied with a mandatory expiry, is visible in the operator view, and reverts automatically without a follow-up ticket.
* An offline-first mobile client reconnects after six hours with 300 queued writes — the sync client paces submission against `RateLimit-Remaining`, and the queue drains without a single 429-induced retry storm.
* Two API replicas process requests for the same tenant simultaneously at the bucket boundary — the Lua check-and-decrement is atomic, so the combined accepted count never exceeds the configured burst.
* A tenant is upgraded from standard to enterprise mid-day — new limits take effect on the next request without dropping in-flight requests or resetting buckets punitively.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team's agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.

items.title: Dedicated storage paths

milestone.title: Later
milestone.description: Unscheduled. Pulled into an R milestone when a customer or a regulation needs it. Holds the open remainder of M0-M2, M6-M9 and MVP 1 (MVP 1 items keep the release:MVP 1 label).

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

The platform stores a large volume of binary clinical and operational content outside PostgreSQL: scanned referral letters and consent forms, DICOM-adjacent imaging exports, LabConnect analyser result PDFs, pathologist-signed DiagnosticReport renders, PharmaConnect batch photographs and recall notices, FacilityConnect asset nameplate photos and permit-to-work scans, SafetyConnect drill evidence, and e-invoices carrying GSTIN detail.

Today there is no object-storage layout at all — this is a greenfield platform, and the working assumption in early service code is "write to a bucket with a UUID key". That assumption is not survivable. A flat keyspace means tenant separation exists only in the database row that happens to point at the object; anyone who obtains or guesses an object key, or any service bug that mixes up a foreign key, reads another hospital's PHI directly from storage with no row-level security in the path. It also makes the enterprise tier impossible to sell: hospitals demanding physical separation, and the isolated-backup and per-tenant-key work in this epic, both need storage that is already partitioned by tenant before they can be layered on.

Affected roles are broad — a ward nurse uploading a wound photograph, a pathologist attaching a stained-slide image, a biomedical technician photographing a failed medical-gas manifold, and the hospital admin and DPO who must answer a DPDP Act 2023 data-principal access or erasure request. Erasure in particular is unworkable against a flat keyspace: the DPO cannot demonstrate that every object belonging to a data principal has been located and destroyed. CERT-In log-retention obligations similarly require that access logs be attributable to a tenant and a country.

Data residency is a hard boundary in this platform: Indian PHI must never leave an India region. A storage layout that does not encode country makes residency a matter of deployment convention rather than an enforceable invariant.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** platform engineer operating the HMS storage layer
**I want** every stored object to live under a deterministic, tenant- and country-scoped path served exclusively through short-lived signed URLs issued by a tenant-aware broker
**So that** no object can be read, listed or enumerated across a tenant boundary, and per-tenant retention, erasure and residency become mechanically enforceable.

### Scope

**In scope**

* A canonical object-key scheme: `{country}/{tenant_id}/{product}/{domain}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{object_id}` with `object_id` a ULID, plus a written specification that all services follow.
* A shared Go storage-broker package that is the only permitted way to read or write objects; direct SDK use is forbidden by lint rule and code review.
* Tenant and country derived from the request context (the same context that sets the RLS `app.tenant_id` GUC), never from a caller-supplied parameter.
* Per-tenant bucket prefixes with IAM/bucket policy conditions restricting each workload identity to its country prefix, so a service misconfiguration cannot cross a residency boundary.
* Signed, time-limited download and upload URLs (default 10 minutes download, 15 minutes upload) with content-type and max-size constraints bound into the signature.
* An `object_ref` table recording every object with its tenant, owning entity, classification (PHI / financial / facility / non-sensitive) and retention class.
* Deny-by-default on `List` operations for application service accounts; enumeration is available only to the retention and backup workers.

**Out of scope**

* Per-tenant customer-managed encryption keys — issue #30 owns key material and envelope encryption; this issue only guarantees the path layout keys will be applied to.
* Tenant-isolated backup and restore of these objects — issue #31.
* Dedicated bucket-per-tenant for the enterprise tier — a later premium-tier story; this scheme must be forward-compatible with it, and the broker must resolve a bucket per tenant rather than a constant.
* Retention and legal-hold policy enforcement (the actual expiry job) — owned by the Data Lifecycle epic; this issue supplies the retention-class column it reads.
* Virus/malware scanning of uploads — owned by the Security epic.

---

## Recommended Solution

Implement a `pkg/storage` broker in the Go modular monolith. It exposes only `PutSigned`, `GetSigned`, `Delete` and `Copy`, all of which take a `context.Context` and derive tenancy from it:

```go
type Ref struct {
    ObjectID   ulid.ULID
    TenantID   uuid.UUID
    Country    string // ISO-3166-1 alpha-2, from the country profile
    Product    string // medicore | labconnect | pharmaconnect | facilityconnect | ...
    Domain     string // consent | diagnostic-report | permit | invoice | ...
    Class      Classification
}

func (b *Broker) GetSigned(ctx context.Context, id ulid.ULID, ttl time.Duration) (string, error)
```

`GetSigned` loads the `object_ref` row inside the tenant-scoped GORM session, so PostgreSQL RLS rejects a cross-tenant lookup before any storage call is made. The broker then re-checks that the row's `tenant_id` equals the context tenant — a deliberate belt-and-braces check that catches an RLS misconfiguration rather than trusting it silently.

Data model:

```sql
CREATE TABLE object_ref (
  object_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,              -- ULID
  tenant_id      UUID NOT NULL,
  country_code   CHAR(2) NOT NULL,
  storage_key    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  bucket         TEXT NOT NULL,
  product        TEXT NOT NULL,
  domain         TEXT NOT NULL,
  classification TEXT NOT NULL
      CHECK (classification IN ('phi','financial','facility','non_sensitive')),
  retention_class TEXT NOT NULL,
  owner_entity   TEXT,        -- e.g. 'encounter', 'work_order'
  owner_id       UUID,
  content_type   TEXT NOT NULL,
  size_bytes     BIGINT NOT NULL,
  sha256         BYTEA NOT NULL,
  created_by     UUID NOT NULL,
  created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  deleted_at     TIMESTAMPTZ
);
ALTER TABLE object_ref ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY object_ref_tenant ON object_ref
  USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid);
CREATE INDEX ON object_ref (tenant_id, owner_entity, owner_id);
```

`storage_key` is generated, never accepted from a caller. A `CHECK` constraint asserts the key begins with `country_code || '/' || tenant_id || '/'`, so a malformed key cannot be persisted even if broker logic regresses.

API surface (console and mobile clients never touch storage directly):

* `POST /api/v1/objects:presign-upload` → `{product, domain, content_type, size_bytes, owner_entity, owner_id}` returns a signed PUT URL and `object_id`.
* `POST /api/v1/objects/{object_id}:confirm` → verifies size and SHA-256 against the stored object, flips the ref to `active`.
* `GET  /api/v1/objects/{object_id}/url` → returns a short-lived signed GET URL.
* `DELETE /api/v1/objects/{object_id}` → soft-deletes the ref and schedules destruction.

Events on NATS JetStream: `ObjectStored` and `ObjectDeleted` (subject `hms.{country}.{tenant}.storage.*`) carrying `object_id`, classification and retention class — consumed by the audit writer and, later, by the backup worker in #31.

Authorisation uses OpenFGA rather than a role check alone, because object access follows the owning clinical entity:

```
type object
  relations
    define owner_entity: [encounter, work_order, diagnostic_report]
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define viewer: viewer from owner_entity
    define deleter: admin from tenant
```

A signed URL is only minted after an OpenFGA `check(user, viewer, object:<id>)` succeeds, so a clinician who cannot see the encounter cannot see its attachments.

Sequencing: depends on the tenant context and RLS data-access layer (Multi-Tenancy epic, tenant-scoped session work) and on the country-profile registry that supplies `country_code` and the regional bucket. Issues #30 and #31 both consume this scheme and should not start before the key layout is frozen.

Risks. The main one is that a service bypasses the broker; mitigated by a CI `forbidigo` rule banning direct cloud-storage SDK imports outside `pkg/storage`, plus an IAM policy that grants object permissions only to the broker's workload identity. Second, signed URLs leak once issued — mitigated by short TTLs, binding the URL to the requester's IP where the client supports it, and recording every mint in the tamper-evident audit log so a leak is investigable. Third, ULID keys are time-sortable and therefore mildly enumerable within a prefix; mitigated by denying `List` to application identities and by the fact that a guessed key still fails the `object_ref` RLS lookup before a URL is minted.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a ward nurse authenticated to tenant A with a care relationship to encounter E
**When** she uploads a wound photograph against encounter E and then requests it back
**Then** the object is written to `IN/{tenantA}/medicore/clinical-image/2026/07/{ulid}`, an `object_ref` row exists with `tenant_id = A` and `classification = 'phi'`, an `ObjectStored` event is published, and a signed GET URL valid for 10 minutes is returned.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a records clerk authenticated to tenant B who has obtained a valid `object_id` belonging to tenant A
**When** they call `GET /api/v1/objects/{object_id}/url`
**Then** the request returns `404 Not Found` (not `403`, so existence is not confirmed), no signed URL is minted, no storage call is made, and a `cross_tenant_object_access_denied` audit record is written with the caller's subject, tenant and source IP.

### Edge Cases

* Presign issued, client never uploads — the orphaned `object_ref` in `pending` state is reaped after 24 hours and does not appear in any clinical view.
* Client uploads content larger than the signed `size_bytes` or with a different content type — the confirm step fails on SHA-256/size mismatch and the object is deleted rather than left half-attached to the encounter.
* The same lab report is confirmed twice (mobile retry on a flaky rural connection) — confirm is idempotent on `object_id` and does not create a duplicate ref or a second `ObjectStored` event.
* A tenant is migrated from the shared-schema tier to a dedicated bucket — existing refs continue to resolve because the broker resolves the bucket per tenant at read time rather than from a constant.
* An object is requested after its owning encounter has been erased under a DPDP data-principal erasure request — the ref is soft-deleted, the URL request returns `410 Gone`, and the underlying object is confirmed destroyed.
* A signed URL is presented after expiry — storage rejects it; the console surfaces a re-request rather than a raw storage error page.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team's agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** every binary object in the platform is addressable only through a tenant- and country-scoped key, retrievable only via a short-lived signed URL minted after an RLS lookup and an OpenFGA check.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** the enterprise physical-separation tier, per-tenant keys (#30), isolated backups (#31) and DPDP erasure all become implementable; residency is enforced by IAM policy rather than convention.
* **Success metric or validation method:** 100% of objects written in a staging soak carry a conforming `storage_key` (validated by a nightly scanner reporting zero non-conforming keys); the adversarial cross-tenant suite from #32 achieves zero successful cross-tenant object reads across at least 500 generated attempts; p95 presign latency under 80 ms and p95 signed-GET mint latency under 50 ms.
* **Monitoring period:** 30 days post-deployment, tracking `storage_key_nonconforming_total` (must remain 0), `cross_tenant_object_denied_total` and signed-URL mint latency in OpenTelemetry.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — keyboard navigation, accessible names and WCAG level.
**Reason:** This story delivers a backend storage broker and API; it introduces no user interface. The upload and viewer components that consume it are delivered by the MediCore records and LabConnect report-viewer stories, which carry the accessibility guardrails.
**Alternative validation:** The presign/confirm/download journey is validated end-to-end through an API contract test and through the existing document-upload Playwright journey once a consuming UI lands; error responses use stable machine-readable codes so consuming UIs can render accessible messages.
**Residual risk:** Low — a consuming UI could surface raw storage errors; mitigated by specifying the error contract (`OBJECT_EXPIRED`, `OBJECT_GONE`, `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`) in the API documentation.
**Approved by:** Platform Team lead.
