items.title: [UI-056] Recover invalid creative plans without freezing conversational design
items.body:
## Problem and observed failure
During intake the site build stopped with:
`creative direction returned an invalid experience plan: brand_behavior_system.utility_behaviors[0].meaning is required`.
This is an internal generated-plan contract failure, not missing owner input. The conversation should shape the design without making the owner debug a JSON schema or repeat intake.

## Required outcome
Keep conversational design content flexible while making the producer/consumer contract explicit, coherent and recoverable. Behaviors, their meaning, scenes, page structure and visual direction must adapt to confirmed conversation and evidence; do not impose a fixed creative template to satisfy validation.

## Bounded implementation
1. Trace the actual deployed creative-direction path, raw failing response and validation boundary. Verify whether the field is absent, aliased, or represented elsewhere; do not assume the local source proves the exact deployed cause.
2. Audit nested behavior-record requirements, especially `utility_behaviors[].meaning`. Decide whether each required field provides necessary downstream semantics or duplicates an already-authoritative field. Record that rationale. Retain useful requirements; simplify genuinely redundant requirements coherently across producer, consumer, fixtures and contract versions where needed.
3. Align every creative-direction producer with the authoritative typed contract, including nested required fields. Prefer shared schema generation/structured output when supported; avoid manually maintained prompt/schema copies drifting apart. Requiredness must not depend on which prompt path happened to run.
4. Add a bounded, budget-aware correction attempt for recoverable generated-plan validation errors, feeding back precise field paths and constraints. Preserve the frozen brief/context, owner confirmations, artifact hashes and valid creative decisions. Never invent missing design semantics, silently insert filler `meaning`, bypass validation, or retry indefinitely.
5. Resume from the failed planning stage rather than repeating intake or an already-started build. If repair is exhausted, preserve inputs and report a clear, actionable failure with a retry/recovery path and diagnostic evidence. Do not expose raw schema errors as the sole owner-facing explanation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Reproduce the missing `utility_behaviors[0].meaning` failure in regression coverage.
- Cover other named behavior arrays and every creative-direction producer so the fix is not one-field/one-prompt-only.
- A corrected valid response proceeds; invalid output remains rejected after the bounded repair limit.
- If a redundant-field contract change is justified, prove existing persisted/supported plans remain readable or have an explicit versioned migration path.
- Different confirmed conversations can produce materially different valid behavior systems; optional arrays can remain empty when semantically appropriate. No mandatory generic effects or fixed scene/behavior counts are added.
- Repair does not change frozen context identity, confirmed revision, copy/asset bindings or authorization and budget gates, and cannot trigger duplicate paid builds.
- Cover success after correction, exhausted correction, budget rejection, preserved context/hashes and no duplicate build startup.
- Deploy through the canonical release pipeline and record the exact deployed SHA plus a disposable intake run proving planning can recover and continue. Keep Merged separate from live verification.

## Starting points
`src/site_agent/hands/opencode_runner.py` (creative-direction prompt and plan parsing),
`src/site_agent/core/design_contracts.py` (`_named_records`, `BrandBehaviorSystem`),
`src/site_agent/application/design_orchestration.py` (other creative-direction prompt/contract path).

## Scope and dependencies
No prerequisite on removing the redundant intake button (#455). Coordinate overlapping edits with active workers. Scope is generated-plan contracts, producers, bounded recovery and focused tests; not a redesign of intake or removal of existing safety gates.

items.title: API contracts: security invariants, response coverage, limits and fault detection
items.body:
<!-- restmail-consolidation:20261026:current -->
## Current outcome and ownership

Security, limits and fault checks prove the API fails safely. The detailed acceptance below remains required.

Shared named-pair/example work is owned once by #625 and PR #1171. Behavior changes and their regression tests stay in focused fix PRs. Earlier prose that asks to mix the two is superseded by the owner’s 2026-10-26 split. Closing source issues is consolidation, not implementation completion.

Decisions remain decisions: preserve current API behavior where #622, #625, #646, #661 or #672 has no explicit answer. Independent fixes and tests can proceed; a scoped decision does not block unrelated work.

---

Part of #623; design and owner decisions remain in #622.

This is the implementation topic for the related work below. Complete every remaining requirement in the linked source bodies and comments. Those requirements are incorporated into this issue; the source issues remain the detailed acceptance and evidence records. Consolidation is not completion.

Work in substantial related batches, with a single PR covering multiple compatible tasks where practical. Do not create one PR or issue per operation or response status.

## Source issues and acceptance

- [ ] [#654: API contract: prove the contract run catches faults (fault injection)](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/654): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#655: API contract: every response a handler can give is reached by the contract run](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/655): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#657: API contract: no account reaches another account's or domain's objects (cross-account phase)](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/657): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#659: API contract: browser sessions (cookies + CSRF), cookie attributes and security headers](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/659): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#660: API contract: every limit holds (rate limits, body caps, recipients, send rate, streams, page size)](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/660): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#661: Each feature works as REST Mail wires and configures it (configuration matrix)](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/661): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#674: Declare and check the security headers, cookies and Retry-After on every response](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/674): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#386: Contract tests: make each documented error response reachable](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/386): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.
- [ ] [#388: Contract tests: what vertrag found (spec mismatches, missing validation)](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/388): all remaining body and comment requirements, existing findings, and validation evidence.

## Owner decisions remain open

- [#661](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/661): The contract for configuration-dependent routes must be decided in #622; keep this decision record open while configuration wiring is grouped.
- [#388](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/388): Historical createBan protocol/default compatibility questions in the comments must be checked against an explicit later decision before changing behavior. The latest acceptance audit supersedes the old unmerged-fix inventory.
- [#672](https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/issues/672): Cross-account 403/404 and invalid-input 400/422 remain owner decisions. No policy change is implied by grouping.

Only Decided work may be implemented. Keep the blocked parts visible while progressing independent work.

## Detailed work retained from the source issues

<details><summary>#654: API contract: prove the contract run catches faults (fault injection)</summary>

Part of #623; decided by the owner on 2026-10-23.

A green contract run can mean nothing was tested. Vertrag's own `doctor` catches configuration that reaches nothing, but not a run that reaches everything and checks too little. A schema that allows every value, an exclusion that is too broad, or a principal that is not what it claims all pass silently.

## Do

A CI job, nightly and on demand, that breaks the server on purpose in known ways and requires the contract run to fail for each one. Each fault is a small patch applied to a throwaway build, or a build tag that switches it on. The first set comes from the faults that matter most:

- **Authorization:**
  - a route's capability check removed;
  - a domain-scoped check turned into a check at `*`;
  - a handler's account-reach check (`mayReach`) skipped;
  - CSRF skipped for cookie sessions.
- **Shape:**
  - a response field renamed;
  - a field's type changed;
  - a list sent as `null`;
  - a field added that the type does not declare (a leaked `storage_ref`).
- **Status:**
  - 200 where 404 is right;
  - 201 where 200 is right;
  - a 422 validation removed.
- **Limits:**
  - a rate limit turned off;
  - the body cap removed.
- **Secrets:** a password or key echoed in a response.

Each fault names the phase expected to catch it: examples, coverage, authorization, the cross-account phase (#657), the leak checks (#658) or the limits suite (#660). A fault that no phase catches is a gap in the proof, filed as such.

## Done when

- Every fault in the set turns the contract run red, in the phase it names.
- The job runs nightly, and a fault that stops being caught fails it.
- Adding a fault is a documented one-file change.


</details>

<details><summary>#655: API contract: every response a handler can give is reached by the contract run</summary>

Part of #623; decided by the owner on 2026-10-23.

"100%" today means every *documented* response passed (`surface.require: 100` in `vertrag.yml`). An operation that documents 3 statuses while its handler writes 9 counts as fully covered. #376 planned to build the API with `-cover` during the contract run and collect `GOCOVERDIR`, but it was never built: `e2e-suite.yml` collects no coverage.

## Do

- **Coverage receipts:** the E2E topology's API runs a `-cover` build during the contract run, and `GOCOVERDIR` is collected per phase. The report shows which handler code the contract run reached.
- **Response-site coverage:** every place a handler writes a response (`respond.*`, `WriteHeader`, `http.Error`, `ServeContent`, following helpers) is a site.
  - The scanner that mapped the API for the area issues lists all of them: 935 across 171 handlers, 761 of them not 500s.
  - The gate: every non-500 site is reached by some example pair (#625) or probe, or is listed as unreachable with a reason.
  - That turns "every operation passed" into "every answer the code can give was given and checked".
- **The site list** comes from the API scanner committed in #664 (`tools/apimap`), the same tool that keeps the area issues current.
- **The report** is part of the HTML report a person reads (#627): operation, site, status, code, reached by which example, or why it is unreachable.

## Done when

- The contract run produces Go coverage for the API.
- Every non-500 response site is reached or listed as unreachable with a reason, and CI fails on a new site that is neither.


</details>

<details><summary>#657: API contract: no account reaches another account's or domain's objects (cross-account phase)</summary>

Part of #623; decided by the owner on 2026-10-23.

Vertrag's authorization phase checks roles: whether a principal holding a capability is allowed, and whether one without it is refused (#376). The commonest way into an API is different: using *another* account's or *another domain's* ids with a credential that is perfectly entitled to the operation (OWASP API1, broken object-level authorization). The document's security roles cannot express "only on your own objects", so no phase tests it today. vertrag#81 also notes that the authorization phase sends example ids literally.

In REST Mail, access to an id is checked in many different places:
- in handlers: `mayReach`, `verifyMessageOwnership`, `managedAccount`;
- in route middleware scoped to the domain or mailbox an `{id}` names: `needsOnDomain`, `needsOnMailbox`, and `needsOnAlias` and `needsOnList` from #619.

A mistake in any one of them leaks another tenant's mail.

## Do

- **Two tenants in the fixtures (#662),** each with:
  - a domain and two accounts;
  - an app password;
  - a domain-scoped admin;
  - mail, contacts, a Sieve script, aliases, pipelines and the other objects the routes take ids for.
- **A cross-account phase:** every operation that takes an id (path or body, about 100 of the 172) is sent by each of tenant B's principals with tenant A's ids, and must be refused. The phase is run by Vertrag (antimatter-studios/vertrag#82), or by hooks generated from the registry until Vertrag has it.
- **One refusal everywhere:** 403 or 404 for an object that exists but is not yours, as decided in the conventions (#656). A refusal that confirms another tenant's id exists is a finding of its own.
- **Lists too:** a list filtered by `domain_id`, or one that lists everything the caller reaches, never contains tenant A's rows when tenant B asks.

## Done when

- Every id-taking operation has been sent by every tenant-B principal with tenant A's ids, and refused, in CI.
- A fault that removes any one ownership check turns the run red (#654).


</details>

<details><summary>#659: API contract: browser sessions (cookies + CSRF), cookie attributes and security headers</summary>

Part of #623; decided by the owner on 2026-10-23.

The whole contract run signs in with `client: "native"` and sends a bearer token. The webmail and the admin UI use the other path: httpOnly cookies plus a CSRF header. That path is never exercised by the contract run:

- `middleware.CSRF` refusing a cookie session's unsafe request without the `X-CSRF-Token` header (403 `csrf_failed`);
- login's cookie shape: `restmail_access` and `restmail_refresh` `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`, and `restmail_csrf` readable (`handlers/auth.go:287-361`);
- logout clearing all three;
- refresh from the cookie;
- the event stream authenticating from the cookie.

The response headers every route carries (HSTS, `nosniff`, frame denial, referrer policy, CSP from `middleware.SecurityHeaders`, and CORS with credentials) are not checked either. Vertrag's `header-schema` check is off.

## Do

- **Cookie principals** in the authorization phase: a cookie session with the CSRF header, and the same session without it. The second must get 403 `csrf_failed` on every unsafe method and succeed on every safe one. Vertrag already supports cookie credentials (`auth` with `cookie:`).
- **Document and check the cookies:** login, refresh, recover and reset declare their `Set-Cookie` headers (antimatter-studios/go-oapifly#18), and a check verifies the attributes (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path`), and that logout expires them.
- **Headers on every response:** turn on `checks.header-schema`, and declare the security headers once for every operation (a middleware describing itself, antimatter-studios/go-oapifly#25). Check CORS against an allowed origin and a refused one.

## Done when

- The contract run includes cookie principals with and without CSRF, and every unsafe operation refuses the latter.
- The cookie attributes and security headers are declared and checked on every response.
- A fault that skips CSRF turns the run red (#654).


</details>

<details><summary>#660: API contract: every limit holds (rate limits, body caps, recipients, send rate, streams, page size)</summary>

Part of #623; decided by the owner on 2026-10-23.

The limits are part of the contract: they are what keeps the API from being used as a password oracle or a spam cannon. Nothing proves they hold, and the fuzz phase avoids them on purpose. The limits, with their defaults:

| Limit | Where | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in and credential checks (login, refresh, reset, recover, password change, link, 2FA, app-password creation, grant escalation, protocol sign-in) | `authThrottle`, per IP | 1/s, burst 15 |
| Refused HTTP Basic credentials | `BasicCredentials`, per credential/address | login's rate |
| Recovery failures | `FailureBudget`, per address | 5, then 1 per 15 min |
| Owner endpoints and `GET /api/v1/server` | `ownerThrottle`, per IP | login's rate, own bucket |
| TLS-RPT ingestion | `tlsrptThrottle`, per IP | 1/s, burst 10 |
| Pipeline and filter tests | `pipelineTestThrottle`, per IP | 2/s, burst 10 |
| Request body | `MaxBodyBytes` | 2 × the SMTP max message size + 1 MiB |
| Delivery body (internal deliver, RESTMAIL) | `deliverBodyLimit` | from the SMTP max message size |
| TLS-RPT body and policies | handler | 512 KiB, 100 policies |
| Recipients per message | send path | 100 |
| Sends per account | send path | 20/min, 100/h |
| Event streams per account | SSE broker | 8 |
| Page size | `limit` | 200 (lists), 100 (messages, clamped) |

## Do

A limits suite of its own, run in CI after the contract phases, on a fresh topology so its buckets are its own. For each limit, it spends the allowance and checks:
- the next request gets the documented 429 with `Retry-After`, or the 413 or 422;
- the allowance comes back after `Retry-After`;
- a different key (another IP, address or account) is unaffected.

Each limit is declared in its route's registration (antimatter-studios/go-oapifly#25 describes the 429 and its header), so the suite is generated from the registry rather than kept by hand.

## Done when

- Every limit in the table (and any added later) is hit in CI and answers as declared.
- A fault that turns a limit off fails the suite (#654).


</details>

<details><summary>#661: Each feature works as REST Mail wires and configures it (configuration matrix)</summary>

Part of #623. The owner's rule (2026-10-23):

> Some parts of the system test themselves, and if they pass all their tests they can be used and relied upon; we don't need to double-check that code as part of rest-mail-server. However, how a feature is implemented in REST Mail needs tests to make sure it's installed and operating correctly, so we catch errors from configuring a component incorrectly.

So this issue does not re-test the components: the go-* libraries (#374), go-smtp, Vertrag, rspamd, ClamAV and the ACME CA have their own suites. It tests that **each feature, as REST Mail wires and configures it, is installed and works**, in every configuration REST Mail supports. Today one contract run on one configuration stands for all of them.

## The features whose presence or behaviour depends on configuration

| Feature | Configuration | What "installed correctly" means |
|---|---|---|
| Push devices | APNs credentials | the `/api/v1/devices` routes exist and register with a (stub) APNs; without credentials, they answer 404 |
| ACME | ACME on | `/.well-known/acme-challenge/*` answers an order's token; off, it is absent |
| Internal listener | `INTERNAL_MTLS_ENABLED` | deliver and check-address are only on the mTLS listener and refuse without a client certificate (Vertrag's `transport.cert`); off, they are on the public router |
| Two-factor | `TOTP2FAEnabled`, master key | enroll answers 403 when off and 503 without a master key; otherwise the lifecycle works |
| Production lock | `ENVIRONMENT` production-like | all seven test endpoints answer 403 even for `*` |
| Security headers | `SECURITY_HEADERS_ENABLED` | on every response, or on none |
| Rate limits | `*_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | on (#660), or off |
| RESTMAIL delivery auth | strict mode, trusted CIDRs, tarpit | a trusted peer delivers, an untrusted unsigned one is refused, negative lookups slow down |
| RESTMAIL discovery | `GATEWAY_HOSTNAME` | answers the endpoint; 503 when unset |
| JavaScript filters | sidecar URL and token | validate and test work; a wrong token gives the 503 with its message |
| Content scanners | rspamd and ClamAV URLs, HMAC secret | a verdict is accepted only with a valid HMAC; an unreachable scanner defers |
| Sieve redirect policy | allow-external, allowed domains | an external redirect is refused or allowed as configured |
| ARC sealers | trusted sealer list | a passing ARC chain overrides DMARC only for a listed sealer |
| Metrics allowlist and trusted proxies | CIDRs | `/metrics` 404s outside them, and `X-Forwarded-For` counts only from a trusted proxy |
| Attachments | S3 settings | attachments are stored and served from the bucket |
| Owner and status keys | key lists | the owner endpoints answer as #633 describes; 409 without keys |

## Do

- **A CI matrix of named configurations,** each a small overlay on the E2E topology: `default`, `internal-mtls`, `production`, `push` (stub APNs), `minimal` (no master key, no sidecar, no scanners, 2FA off). In each one, Vertrag's examples phase and a feature check run.
- **Feature checks:** one per row, testing REST Mail's wiring end to end, not the component. For example, "a message through a pipeline with `rspamd` and a bad HMAC is deferred", not "rspamd classifies spam".
- **Decide what the served document describes:** only the routes this server has in its configuration (the document is generated on demand), or every route with a note. The contract run in each configuration then reads that configuration's document.

## Done when

- Every row has a check that fails when the feature is wired or configured wrong, and runs in the configurations it applies to.
- The decision on configuration-dependent routes is in #622.


</details>

<details><summary>#674: Declare and check the security headers, cookies and Retry-After on every response</summary>

Split out of #659. #659 keeps the cookie-and-CSRF principals and the cookie-attribute checks, which can run now. Declaring headers in the document needs the generator to describe them (antimatter-studios/go-oapifly#18), and middleware to describe what it adds (#25).

- Declare the security headers once, for every operation, through the middleware that sets them: HSTS, `nosniff`, frame denial, referrer policy and CSP (`middleware.SecurityHeaders`).
- Declare `Set-Cookie` on login, refresh, recover and reset, `Retry-After` on every 429, and the download headers on attachments.
- Turn on Vertrag's `checks.header-schema`, so every response's headers are checked against what is declared.
- Check CORS with an allowed origin and a refused one.

## Done when

- Every response's headers are declared and checked in CI.


</details>

<details><summary>#386: Contract tests: make each documented error response reachable</summary>

Follow-up to #376 (vertrag contract tests).

The examples phase now sends every operation's success response, and each authenticated operation's `401` (with no credential). The other documented error responses are excluded by pattern in `vertrag.yml` (`exclude-matching`) because the spec has no request that provokes them: vertrag pairs a request with a response by example name, and an unnamed request pairs with every response, so a `422` transaction sends the valid request and fails.

## Do

For each documented error response, give the operation a **named** request example and the response a matching **named** example (OpenAPI `examples`, same key on both sides), so vertrag sends the request that provokes it:

- [ ] `422`: an invalid body (a required field missing, a value out of range) — 23 operations.
- [ ] `404`: a path parameter that names nothing — needs a parameter example per named example, or a hook.
- [ ] `409`: a create repeated (the conflict needs the first create to run first: order it with a link).
- [ ] `400`: malformed input.
- [ ] `401` on the sign-in operations (`login`, `refresh`, `reset`, `owner/*`): a wrong credential.

Then drop each pattern from `exclude-matching` as its responses become reachable.

Not here: `403` (needs a principal without the capability: vertrag's authorization phase, antimatter-studios/vertrag#71, using the principals the E2E fixture already makes) and `429`/`503` (rate limits, an unavailable sidecar).


</details>

<details><summary>#388: Contract tests: what vertrag found (spec mismatches, missing validation)</summary>

Found by the vertrag contract tests (#376), E2E run https://github.com/rest-mail/rest-mail-server/actions/runs/39027682625 (report: the run's `e2e-container-logs` artifact, `examples.xml` and `contract.log`). Branch: `feat/vertrag-contract-tests`.

## The server and its spec disagree (examples phase)

Each is either a wrong spec (correct it) or a small server bug (fix it):

- [x] `Message.headers` arrives as an array; the spec says object (`listMessages`, `searchMessages`).
- [x] `Message.recipients_to` items arrive as strings; the spec says objects (`sendMessage`, `saveDraft`), so every link from a sent message is skipped.
- [x] `PUT /api/v1/accounts/{id}/sieve` answers `201` when it creates the script; the spec documents only `200`.
- [x] `POST /api/v1/accounts/{id}/contacts/block` answers `201`; the spec documents `200`.
- [x] `GET /api/v1/admin/queue`: the body has none of `items`, `total`, `limit`, `offset`; the documented shape is wrong.
- [x] `GET /api/v1/admin/grants` and `/grants/mine`: `granted_by.kind` has a value outside the documented enum (`admin`, `system`).
- [x] `POST /api/v1/admin/pipelines/test`: `data.steps` is `null` (spec: array); a nil slice in the handler.
- [x] `GET /api/v1/admin/pipelines/analytics`: `data.funnel.top_reject_reasons` is `null` (spec: array); a nil slice.
- [x] `GET /api/v1/attachments/{id}` answers with the attachment's own type (`text/plain`); the spec promises only `application/octet-stream`.

## Requests the spec cannot produce yet

The documented (or schema-generated) request is refused, so each needs a request example, or a hook for fixture state: `PATCH /admin/mailboxes/{id}` (422), `POST /admin/pipelines/test-filter` (422), `POST /admin/custom-filters` (422), `POST /admin/custom-filters/validate` (422), `POST /admin/domains/{id}/allowlist` and `/blocklist` (422), `POST /.well-known/smtp-tlsrpt` (422), `POST /autodiscover/autodiscover.xml` (400), `POST /restmail/messages` (422), `GET /.well-known/mta-sts.txt` (404: needs the Host of a domain with a policy), `POST /auth/protocol-sign-in` and `POST /auth/refresh` (hook fixes pushed, unverified).

## Coverage phase: boundaries not refused

190 probes on 65 operations got a 2xx (or a 5xx) where a value outside the schema needs a 4xx, or a 4xx for a value inside it. Each is either a validation the server is missing or a schema that is looser or stricter than the handler. By operation (count of probes):

- /api/v1/accounts > Create an account > 201 > application/json 4
- /api/v1/accounts/{id} > Get an account this one may read > 200 > application/json 1
- /api/v1/accounts/{id}/credentials > List an account's app passwords > 200 > application/json 1
- /api/v1/accounts/{id}/folders > List folders for an account > 200 > application/json 2
- /api/v1/accounts/{id}/folders > Create a new folder > 201 > application/json 3
- /api/v1/accounts/{id}/folders/{folder}/messages > List messages in a folder with cursor pagination > 4
- /api/v1/messages/{id} > Get a single message by ID > 200 > application/json 1
- /api/v1/messages/{id} > Update message flags or move to another folder > 200 > application/json 1

- /api/v1/messages/send > Compose and send a new message > 201 > application/json 9
- /api/v1/messages/{id}/raw > Get the raw RFC 2822 message source > 200 > text/plain 1
- /api/v1/messages/{id}/forward > Forward a message > 201 > application/json 5
- /api/v1/messages/draft > Save a new draft > 201 > application/json 10
- /api/v1/accounts/{id}/threads/{threadID} > Get all messages in a thread > 200 > application/json 2
- /api/v1/accounts/{id}/quota > Get mailbox quota usage > 200 > application/json 2

</details>


## Consolidation audit

Original bodies, comments, completed checkboxes and existing PR evidence remain available through every source link. Source closure with reason `not_planned` means work moved here; it does not mean that work shipped.

items.title: [Agent 1/8] Platform Foundation, AWS EC2 Deployment, Authentication & Shared Contracts
items.body:
## Mission
Build the secure, deployable foundation for the **complete SomaLoom educational content platform**. All other agents depend on your initial repository structure and interface conventions. Deployment target: **AWS EC2 + Docker Compose**, with Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL/pgvector, Redis, HTTPS and durable storage.

## Ownership / boundaries
- **Own:** repository bootstrap and root config; `infra/**`, `docker/**`, `contracts/**`, `apps/api/app/core/**`, `apps/api/app/auth/**`, `db/migrations/**`, deployment workflows and project documentation.
- Create the minimal `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `services` workspace structure without implementing other agents' features.
- **Do not** write the other agents' ingestion, parsing, retrieval, authoring, assessment, or web UI implementations.

## Implementation guide
1. **Bootstrap first**: initialize `main` with a coherent monorepo, README, .gitignore, env examples, formatting/linting/tests, Docker Compose, shared type/schema conventions. Commit this early so seven feature branches can start.
2. Establish **versioned contracts** (OpenAPI + JSON Schema/Pydantic): `Resource`, `ResourceVersion`, `Extraction`, `ContentBlock`, `VisualAsset`, `Equation`, `CurriculumOutcome`, `EvidenceLink`, `GenerationJob`, `GeneratedDocument`, `Export`. Identifiers: UUIDs; UTC timestamps; tenant/school ID; source/license/provenance fields. Publish placeholder endpoints and working mock fixtures.
3. FastAPI `/api/v1` app: standardized responses/errors, typed validation, `/health`, `/ready`, OpenAPI, request IDs, pagination, job-status convention; auth with secure password hashing and roles `platform_admin`, `school_admin`, `teacher`, `reviewer`. All school-owned records must enforce tenant isolation server-side.
4. PostgreSQL + `pgvector`, Redis queue, transactional migrations, audit events, object/file abstraction backed by encrypted EBS for MVP; introduce S3-compatible storage interface for migration/backup. Never keep documents only in ephemeral containers.
5. Configure EC2 deployment: Docker Compose services for nginx/TLS, web, API, worker, Postgres, Redis; restrictive security groups (public 80/443 only; SSH restricted or Session Manager), non-root containers, secrets outside Git, IAM least privilege, HTTPS, secure headers, health/restart policy.
6. CI: test/lint/build on PR; staging deploy, backup/restore scripts, safe migrations, rollback instructions, logs/metrics, disk/capacity alerts, rate limits. Capture AWS and domain prerequisites in README; never commit keys.

## Shared API/data contract for all agents
- REST prefix `/api/v1`; authenticated operations; stable pagination `{items, page, page_size, total}`; async jobs `{id,status,progress,error,created_at,finished_at}`.
- Central schema reference in `contracts/`; feature agents own implementations in their own directories, **not** the contract source. Contract changes need a PR or documented agreement.
- DB migration ownership stays here: feature agents submit additive migration specs in `db/proposals/agent-N-*.sql` or ORM model proposals, which you integrate; no competing edits to migration head.
- Document pipeline: `Resource -> Extraction -> Indexed Evidence -> Generation -> Review -> Export`. Every object must retain tenant and provenance information.
- Branch convention: `agent/01-platform` etc; one PR per workstream to `main`; never force push another agent's branch. Do not publish production credentials or enable shell-access endpoints.

## Definition of done — final product
- [ ] One-command reproducible local setup; working authenticated web/API integration.
- [ ] EC2 HTTPS deployment, correct service lifecycle, database migrations and environment documentation.
- [ ] Tenant/role authorization tested including denial of cross-school access.
- [ ] Upload and generation job status can be tracked through common contracts.
- [ ] Working encrypted durable data storage and verified off-instance backup **and restore**.
- [ ] CI passes tests, secrets checks and deployment health tests; clear observability, recovery and rollback runbook.
- [ ] No open critical/high security issues at public launch.

## 48-hour checkpoint (26–28 October 2026)
**First 2 hours:** bootstrap commit + contracts + env examples; unblock agents. **By beta:** EC2 reachable behind HTTPS, basic authentication, Postgres/Redis, worker and app health checks. Hardening/scale work remains tracked here until final acceptance.

## Coordination
Act as the integration owner. Review contract-changing PRs quickly; publish stable mock payloads. Agent 8 owns the user-facing UI and end-to-end acceptance; you own reliable deployment and security. Related: agents 2–8.

items.title: GET /api/schemas answers a stale key with the Default tenant's type list, and deploy probes ride the same path
items.body:
`GET /api/schemas` is the last surviving route of the deprecated legacy surface (api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex:2966-2971). Its scope is `pipe_through([:api, BarkparkWeb.Plugs.LegacyDeprecation])`, and LegacyDeprecation is a header-stamper with no gate at all - `put_resp_header` three times and return (api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/legacy_deprecation.ex:7-13). So the effective mount is the bare shared pipeline, and the schema list a caller receives is chosen by `AssignDefaultScope`, not by the credential the caller sent.

RELATION TO THE PARENT: mechanism-sibling of task-46872cadcfc50c5f, not a copy of it. The parent's in-flight remedy (`strict_on_presented` on OptionalToken, PR #14318) attaches to `pipeline :api_grant_read`, which is layered on the single scope `/v1/data` at router.ex:1917. Verified on origin/main @ fdb04d57d5: that pipeline (router.ex:112-121) is `ResolveTokenOwner`, `AssignGrantScope`, `PublicRead` and this legacy scope pipes through none of the three. The remedy is route-local; this route retains the behaviour.

--- CHAIN ---

`LegacyController.schemas/2` (api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/legacy_controller.ex:179-208) calls:

    schemas =
      @dataset
      |> Content.list_schemas(scope_opts(conn))
      |> Enum.filter(&Schema.public_schema?/1)

`scope_opts/1` (api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/scope_helpers.ex) reads `assigns.current_workspace` and `assigns.current_project` verbatim and emits them as the WHERE terms. With no verified credential those assigns were placed by `AssignDefaultScope` (api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/assign_default_scope.ex), because `OptionalToken`'s failed-verification arm (api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/optional_token.ex:26-44) never assigns `:api_token` and `DeriveWorkspaceFromToken` (api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/derive_workspace_from_token.ex) consequently no-ops. The path carries no `/w/:workspace_slug/p/:project_slug` segment, so no resolver ever competes for the assign.

Result: a caller holding an expired or revoked workspace-B token is handed the seeded Default tenant's public schema list, at 200, with deprecation headers attached and nothing indicating the credential was rejected.

--- CEILING ON THE HARM ---

The route is deliberately ungated - the comment above it (router.ex:2960-2965) records that w15-E over-gated it and the gate was removed on purpose - and the controller comment at legacy_controller.ex:180-191 records that the response is already narrowed to explicitly-public schemas through `Schema.public_schema?/1`, the same predicate the query route and the anonymous search allowlist use. A caller sending no Authorization header receives byte-identical output. Nothing is exposed that was not already world-readable.

Classify as integrity/mislead, and as the LOWEST-severity member of this sweep's family. It is not a confidentiality finding.

The residual harm is a wrong answer to an identity question: an integrator pointing a build at the flat legacy endpoint with a dead workspace-B key sees a schema list, concludes the credential works and the types are those, and is wrong on both counts. The route is also probed as a liveness check by deploy.sh, the docker-compose healthcheck and cloud/support.go (named in the controller comment) - all of which test parse-ability, so a wrong tenant's list still reads as healthy to them.

--- CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMEDY, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW EXISTS SEPARATELY ---

This route is the reason the widening decision cannot be made purely on severity. It is the cheapest hit in the family and simultaneously the one with real deployment blast radius: if the strict-on-presented clamp is attached to the shared pipeline, any deployed prober still sending a stale key begins receiving a refusal here, on the endpoint several deploy scripts use to decide whether the box is up. That trade belongs in the decision record alongside the media surfaces, not discovered afterwards.

<!-- barkpark:acceptance:start -->
### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] LegacyDeprecation is confirmed by content to be a header-stamper with no gate, so the effective mount of GET /api/schemas is the bare shared pipeline.
- [ ] The derivation is confirmed on origin/main: legacy_controller.ex:179-208 passes scope_opts(conn) to Content.list_schemas/2, and with no verified credential those assigns came from AssignDefaultScope.
- [ ] The finding is recorded as the lowest-severity member of this family and explicitly as integrity rather than confidentiality, on the evidence that Schema.public_schema?/1 already narrows the response and a header-less caller receives byte-identical output.
- [ ] The deployment blast radius is recorded in the widening decision: deploy.sh, the docker-compose healthcheck and cloud/support.go probe this path, so a strict clamp on the shared pipeline changes what a stale-keyed prober sees on a liveness endpoint.
<!-- barkpark:acceptance:end -->

items.title: EWP-2: ingestion-cache store Connection-scoped refactor (#482b-ingestion)
items.body:
# Migration 3 — ingestion-cache → EWP-1 envelope (Option A)

**Corrected (2026-11-01):** ingestion-cache is **Cassandra-backed** (`CqlSession`), not JDBC. There is no `DataSource`/`JdbcTemplate`, so the `JdbcEventOutbox` + 3-arg `OutboxEventPublisher` same-transaction-JDBC pattern does **not** apply, and no store needs Connection-scoping. (This supersedes the original "Connection-scoped refactor" title.)

The Cassandra outbox already has LWT atomicity (`insertSourceVersionAndOutboxIfAbsent`), dead-letter (5 attempts), retry classification, exponential backoff, and per-aggregate ordering (`orderingBlocked`). Migration 3 **adapts its event envelope to EWP-1**, keeping the Cassandra store + `KafkaProducer`.

## In scope

- **`EventEnvelopeBuilder` extraction** into `eventing-outbox`: shared wire-shape validation (tenant scope, registered type-version, replay-class match) with **no JDBC dependency** — used by `OutboxEventPublisher` and the Cassandra path. This is the shared contract; `EventOutbox`/`JdbcEventOutbox` remain the JDBC storage impl.
- **Cassandra schema additions**: `schema_version`, `correlation_id`, `causation_id`, `replay_class`, `security_metadata` columns in `source_versions`/`source_tombstones` (+ manifest outbox).
- **SecurityMetadata propagation**: classification/actor from the ingestion pipeline must reach each event.
- **Typed payloads + registry**: `SourcePublished`, `SourceTombstoned`, manifest-transition types; `SourcePublished` = `REPLAY_SAFE` (fact); `SourceTombstoned` inherits Hazard H-1 (pin in #394).
- **Config fail-startup gate**: fail if `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS` is blank and dispatcher mode is not explicitly demo (same discipline as topology).

## Out of scope (explicit)

`EventOutbox`, `JdbcEventOutbox`, `OutboxEventPublisher`, `KafkaOutboxDispatcher`, `OutboxReader`, and reimplementing the Cassandra dead-letter/retry/ordering (those stay as-is).

## Preserved unchanged

`insertSourceVersionAndOutboxIfAbsent` (LWT), retry classification, dead-letter, backoff, `listUnpublishedSourceOutbox` + `orderingBlocked`, `replaySourceOutbox`, `listTenantIds()` / `tenant_registry` enumeration.

## Dependency

Blocked on the "outbox production readiness" PR (dispatcher gating + `EventEnvelopeBuilder` extraction + fixes).

items.title: adr-fleet hardcodes docs/knowledge/decisions/, so its cross-check, number pre-allocation, and VERIFY gate all fail silently in any repo using a different ADR store

labels.name: route:roadmap-fleet
labels.description: issue-fleet route: owned by roadmap-fleet (build stage)

items.body:
`adr-fleet`'s SKILL.md hardcodes `docs/knowledge/decisions/` as the ADR store in eight places, including its VERIFY gate. In a consuming repo that keeps ADRs anywhere else, every step that depends on that path silently finds nothing.

Observed during a `fleet-command` run today (harness CLI **12.2.0**) against a repo whose ADR store is `docs/adr/`, holding 41 sequentially-numbered records with a `README.md` stating the convention.

## What breaks, in order of severity

**1. The cross-check finds nothing, so every decided ADR is misclassified as novel.**

SKILL.md:60 — "For every candidate, search `docs/knowledge/decisions/` for an ADR that already records it. A candidate whose decision is already documented is **already-decided** — flag it for closure with a citation, not a re-draft."

The directory does not exist, so the search returns empty and all 41 already-decided architectures read as novel. The skill's own anti-pattern table (SKILL.md:193) names this outcome precisely: *"An already-decided point re-drafted is duplicate work and a conflicting ADR."* The skill becomes a duplicate-ADR generator in any repo not using the hardcoded path.

**2. Number pre-allocation collides.**

SKILL.md:64 — "Scan `docs/knowledge/decisions/` for the highest existing number and assign each confirmed candidate the next sequential number." Scanning a non-existent directory yields a highest-existing of none, so pre-allocation starts at 0001 and collides with the entire existing 0001–0041 range. Pre-allocation is described as the mechanism that *prevents* collisions when N subagents draft concurrently, so this defeats it at the source rather than in a race.

**3. VERIFY rejects every conforming draft.**

SKILL.md:115 and :168 — a draft is required at `docs/knowledge/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md`, and SKILL.md:168 states "A branch lacking a valid `docs/knowledge/decisions/NNNN-<slug>.md` at `status: proposed` did not run the real advisor pipeline. It is rejected or retried — never carried into the sign-off pass, no matter what the subagent claimed."

So a subagent that correctly writes to the repo's real ADR directory is rejected as not having run the pipeline. The gate cannot be satisfied and cannot be honestly passed.

## Why this is not the same as #2145

#2145 covers `manage_adr` ignoring its `path` argument, and its third defect covers ADR *file format* (missing `# ADR NNNN` heading, markdownlint directive, bold `**Status:**`/`**Date:**` lines). Notably it cites "the consuming repo's `docs/knowledge/decisions/README.md`" — i.e. that repo does use the hardcoded path, which is likely why this has not surfaced before. This issue is about the *directory* being a literal rather than resolved, which is orthogonal and survives a `manage_adr` fix.

## Suggested direction

Resolve the ADR directory rather than hardcoding it — a `harness.config.json` key, or discovery (`docs/adr/`, `docs/decisions/`, `docs/knowledge/decisions/`, first one present), with the resolved path echoed in SELECT's output so a wrong resolution is visible rather than silent. Note that `harness.config.json` already has `docsDir`, but no ADR-specific key, and the entropy config's `forwardLookingPaths` default list contains both `docs/decisions/` and `docs/adr/` — so the CLI already knows both conventions exist.

Until then a conductor must pass the real path in the lane's dispatch prompt, which is a per-run workaround that every consuming repo has to rediscover.

## Detection note

This was caught only because the probe reported it rather than returning a plausible number. A cross-check that finds zero existing ADRs and concludes "all candidates are novel" is a zero denominator reported as a result — the queue looks healthy and large precisely when the lookup has failed completely.

items.title: P0 — Fondations & décisions d'architecture
items.body:
## Contexte

Première phase : trancher les choix structurants de la plateforme SaaS Dudalo avant tout développement. Rien ne peut démarrer proprement sans décisions actées (tenancy, stack, socle de données) et un pipeline en place. Fondation de tout le backlog.

Réf. : audit `migration/audit-migration-dudalo.md` (espace Cabane).

## Acceptance Criteria

```gherkin

Feature: Fondations techniques et décisions d'architecture validées

  Scenario: Stratégie de tenancy tranchée et documentée
    Given l'équipe doit choisir le modèle d'isolation des données
    When la décision est prise et consignée dans un ADR
    Then la stratégie retenue (shared DB + tenant_id / schéma par tenant / DB par tenant) est actée
    And ses implications de sécurité et de coût d'exploitation sont documentées

  Scenario: Monorepo et CI/CD opérationnels
    Given aucun socle projet n'existe encore
    When le monorepo et le pipeline CI/CD sont initialisés
    Then un push sur main déclenche automatiquement build + tests + lint
    And les environnements dev / staging / prod sont provisionnés

  Scenario: Modèle de données socle validé
    Given les entités identité / tenant / souscription doivent être modélisées
    When le schéma socle est revu et approuvé
    Then il couvre users, tenants, memberships, souscriptions, entitlements et audit

```

## Definition of Done

- [ ] ADR "stratégie de tenancy" publié
- [ ] Monorepo + CI/CD (build/test/lint) verts sur main
- [ ] Environnements dev / staging / prod provisionnés
- [ ] Modèle de données socle validé et versionné
- [ ] Décision *strangler pattern* vs réécriture actée
- [ ] Conventions de sécurité documentées (secrets, chiffrement, politique MDP)

items.title: New repo: refuge-demo, a neutral sales-demo app (circle.so competitor) built on the refuge package

labels.name: video_call
labels.description: Video calling feature (GetStream preview, guest join)

items.body:
## Goal
Create a **completely separate repository** for a demo app built on the Refuge platform. It's used for sales demos and screenshots and positioned as a **circle.so competitor**:
- community spaces, posts, DMs and profiles
- Zoom-style video calls with guest invite links
- event and call signups (Signup Genius style)
- courses (coming soon)

It must have **nothing to do with church, religion or autism**. Use neutral branding, neutral seed content (e.g. a "Maker Collective" or "Remote Founders Club" community) and neutral copy.

## Must not interfere with Belong
- Separate repo, its own Firebase project, its own Stream app and keys, and its own Supabase (or a separate schema/project).
- No shared production data or credentials with Belong. Belong production stays untouched.
- Consumes the reusable `refuge` package from #924, as its second tenant after Belong. That proves the package is generic.

## Suggested small slices
1. Decide the repo name and visibility, and pick a neutral brand, palette and icon.
2. Scaffold a Flutter app that depends on `refuge`. Use a git or path dependency until #924 publishes the package.
3. Set up its own Firebase, Stream and Supabase. Keep secrets server-side only; no secrets in dart-defines or the APK.
4. Seed script for demo data (members, spaces, posts, an upcoming call), plus a periodic reset.
5. Demo hosting: a web build on its own Firebase Hosting site, plus an Android APK via App Distribution.
6. A screenshot and marketing-image pipeline (Maestro/marionette) for sales decks.
7. Optional guest-only "try it" mode so prospects can join a demo call from a link.

## Relationship
- Supersedes and expands #910 (the earlier in-repo `FLAVOR=demo` idea). This issue covers a separate repo.
- Depends on #924 for the reusable package. It can start with a vendored copy and switch later.

items.title: paige_social_posts: operator-vs-tenant schema conflict leaves two Solo Social surfaces non-functional on prod (§9 product decision)
items.body:
Surfaced by the §5 compliance pass on PR #1159 (the #1155 fresh-replay repair). Filed as an out-of-scope finding per the standing directive ("park unrelated findings with exact evidence") — it is **not** fixed by #1159, which deliberately only unbreaks fresh replay without making the operator-vs-tenant decision.

## The conflict
`public.paige_social_posts` is defined twice, with two incompatible schemas under one name:

- **Operator schema (LIVE on prod)** — `20260627193825_*.sql`: `platform`/`caption`/`posted_at`/`status(enum)`, **no `tenant_id`**; RLS `is_platform_owner()` (operator-only, set in `20260721053737:82`). The live writer `supabase/functions/meta-schedule-post/index.ts:75` inserts exactly this schema (platform-wide, single `META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN`), and `20261210000000:30-36` explicitly warns that a tenant-scoped read of this table would "publish every workspace's post to one shared page — a §9 breach."
- **Tenant schema (intended, never applied to prod)** — `20270117000000_social_operations.sql`: `tenant_id NOT NULL`/`content`/`targets`/`job_attempt_id`/`published_at`, tenant RLS. Its `create table if not exists` no-ops against the pre-existing operator table, so this schema never materialized. (The migration has never applied to prod — `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` has no `paige_social_accounts` type. #1159 unblocks the migration's *other* objects but intentionally keeps `paige_social_posts` on the operator schema.)

## Impact — two wired-but-non-functional Solo surfaces on prod
- `src/solo/social-studio.tsx:466` — reads/writes the **tenant** schema (`.content`/`.targets`/`.content_type`, writes `{content}`). On the live operator table these columns don't exist and tenant RLS returns 0 rows → **non-functional on prod** (a §70 "wired but a human can't complete it" surface).
- `src/solo/settings-integrations-social.tsx:57` — reads `paige_social_accounts`, which does not exist on prod yet (created net-new when #1159's migration finally applies, then empty under tenant RLS).

Both are reachable (via `growth2.tsx` / `settings-integrations.tsx`) but cannot complete their flow today. This is pre-existing, not caused by #1159.

## The decision to make
Reconcile to ONE schema for `paige_social_posts`:
- **Operator-only** (drop the tenant pipeline ambition; fix/retire the two Solo surfaces), or
- **Tenant-scoped** (requires per-tenant OAuth — provider app review + per-tenant tokens — because the current platform-wide `META_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN` path cannot be tenant-scoped without the §9 breach above; and `meta-schedule-post` would need to move off the operator insert). Making the live table `tenant_id NOT NULL` without this **breaks `meta-schedule-post`**.

## Also noted (pre-existing, same file)
`20270117000000`'s header advertises five `social.*` Spine capabilities (`social.accounts_read/.post_draft/.post_schedule/.post_publish/.analytics_read`) but only `social.post_publish` is ever registered (the others are never inserted into `registry.ts`/`paige_action_kinds`). Reconcile the header when the pipeline is actually built.

## Related
- #1155 (fresh-replay repair — the guard that made this visible; PR #1159)
- #1154 (`social_post` edge fn non-functional — `paige-social/index.ts` references undefined `content`)
- Harness Completion Map §5.7 (`docs/delivery/harness-completion-map.md`) records this as the Social domain's next-phase product decision.

items.title: platform 7: the store — tables with a tenant column, row-level security, blob store for raw artifacts

labels.name: platform
labels.description: Platformization: turning the CLI into a multi-tenant API

items.body:
## Why
With every read and write behind the run handle, swapping what sits behind it is one job in one place. Listing runs by alert, status, or date is what forces a real store: trivial against a table, painful against a directory tree.

## Design
- Tables: `tenant`, `environment`, `alert`, `run`, `episode`, `finding`, `lesson` (metadata + approval state; the prose stays in git per the lessons-store issue). Sibling worlds are rows in `run` with `parent_run_id` and `fork_turn`. The chain run → episode → finding → lesson is the provenance story; each link is a foreign key.
- **Tenant column on every table**, with row-level security so a query without tenant context returns nothing. The run handle carries its tenant and the store refuses any operation that doesn't come through a tenant-bound handle — isolation enforced in the data layer, not by business logic remembering the filter. Start with one shared database; per-schema or per-database isolation is an upgrade for a contract that demands it.
- **Blob + record** for loosely-shaped inputs: the raw alert stored untouched as an immutable blob under a per-tenant prefix with its own access policy, plus a small fixed record (signature, source, host, timestamp, severity, environment) filled via the environment's alert mapping. Schemas belong to the tenant; only the mapping is ours. Same pattern for raw gather payloads (large, opaque, read whole).
- The leads and queries tables become real tables (they are filtered on by the judge and the lead-author). The investigation log stays an opaque artifact unless the learning loop needs to query inside it — decide then.
- Second implementation of the run handle against this store; the file-backed one becomes the test double.

## Done when
- The e2e replay passes against both backends.
- A cross-tenant read attempted through a handle bound to the wrong tenant returns nothing, covered by a test.
- Run listing by alert / status / date exists on the store interface.

Depends on: run handle, environment record, lessons store, job model. Decide the cross-tenant lessons question (see the lessons-store issue) before keying the `lesson` table.

items.title: Per-tenant Greptime trace tables with tenant-level TTLs and no default partitioning
items.body:
Today we write traces into a shared Greptime table, `opentelemetry_traces`, and read them back from that same table in the API. We want to move to one trace table per tenant so retention can be configured per tenant/table instead of globally.

Greptime supports overriding the target trace table via the `X-Greptime-Trace-Table-Name` header, and its default trace table model applies a 16-way `trace_id` partition rule. That default is fine for a small number of shared trace tables, but it does not scale if we create one table per tenant. With tenant tables, default partitioning would multiply into too many partitions overall, so partitioning should no longer be the default.

We can keep partitioned tenant trace tables as a future/pro-tier option with migration via the repartition feature.

**Required changes**
- Introduce one Greptime traces table per tenant, with a stable naming convention derived from tenant/organization ID.
- Provision tenant tables explicitly with the Greptime trace data model and tenant-specific TTL.
- Stop relying on Greptime’s default trace-table creation shape for tenant tables, since that shape includes default `trace_id` partitioning.
- Update trace ingestion so writes are routed to the tenant’s table instead of always landing in shared `opentelemetry_traces`.
- Update the trace read path in the API to resolve the tenant table dynamically instead of hard-coding `opentelemetry_traces`.
- Update schema introspection and caching in the trace service so it is table-aware rather than assuming a single shared table.
- Cache discovered `metadataColumns` and optional trace column presence per tenant table in [service.ts](/Users/h/Documents/hebo-platform/apps/api/src/modules/traces/service.ts), instead of using one global cache entry. This avoids repeated `information_schema.columns` lookups while keeping trace queries correct for each tenant table.
- Define fallback behavior for spans that do not have tenant context. Either:
  - keep them in a shared non-tenant table, or
  - scope this change to gateway gen-AI traces only.

**Conceptual OTLP exporter change**
The current exporter setup is effectively process-wide and uses static headers. To support multiple tables, replace the single trace exporter with a tenant-aware exporter/multiplexer:

- Resolve the tenant from span attributes already attached during request handling, e.g. `hebo.organization.id`.
- Map tenant ID to a Greptime table name.
- Group exported spans by resolved table name.
- For each table group, send the batch with the normal Greptime trace pipeline header plus `X-Greptime-Trace-Table-Name: <tenant_table>`.
- Cache delegate exporters/clients per table so we do not recreate an exporter on every batch.
- Keep table provisioning separate from normal export flow so TTL and table options are controlled explicitly, rather than depending on first-write auto-creation.

**Non-goals**
- No migration or backfill of existing traces.
- No partitioning by default for tenant tables.
- No UI change expected in console; this should remain an API/storage concern.

**Acceptance criteria**
- New traces for a tenant are written to that tenant’s own Greptime trace table.
- Each tenant table can have its own TTL.
- Tenant trace tables are created without default `trace_id` partitioning.
- API trace list/detail queries work against the correct tenant table.
- Trace schema discovery is cached per tenant table rather than globally.
- There is no migration/backfill requirement for existing shared-table traces.
- Partitioned tenant trace tables, if supported later, are explicitly opt-in rather than the default.

**References**
- Greptime OTLP traces docs: https://docs.greptime.com/user-guide/ingest-data/for-observability/opentelemetry/
- Greptime trace data model docs: https://docs.greptime.com/user-guide/traces/data-model/
- Greptime manage data docs: https://docs.greptime.com/user-guide/manage-data/overview/#manage-data-retention-with-ttl-policies
- Greptime repartition docs: https://docs.greptime.com/user-guide/deployments-administration/manage-data/repartition/

items.title: [Onboarding] Define the minimum usable-tenant baseline and readiness checklist
items.body:
## Parent

- #1999

## Context

The new identity onboarding flow deliberately creates an **empty root tenant**. It is immediately sign-in capable, but it is not yet a usable PGR tenant: application masters, boundaries, workflow, employees, and UI configuration are still absent.

We need one canonical, implementation-oriented document that answers: **what must exist before a newly created tenant is usable?**

## Goal

Document the smallest PGR-ready tenant baseline, map each requirement to its owning DIGIT service/store and configurator phase, and provide a checklist that can be run against every freshly onboarded tenant.

## Decisions / invariants

- The organization maps directly to a **root tenant**. Do not generate or preserve a synthetic `.city` child tenant.
- Do not clone arbitrary demo data, complaints, boundaries, or employees from `pg`/another tenant.
- Keycloak owns authentication, organizations, memberships, and organization-scoped identity roles.
- DIGIT continues to own application authorization and application data. The managed DIGIT employee account is necessary for a DIGIT token, but does **not** by itself create the HRMS employee/jurisdiction data needed to operate PGR.
- The BFF's responsibility ends at an **identity-ready tenant**. The configurator/onboarding layer owns application readiness.
- All setup operations must be tenant-scoped, idempotent, resumable, and safe to rerun after a partial failure.
- `tenant.citymodule` is an existing DIGIT schema name; using it must not imply that a child city tenant exists.

## Readiness levels

### 0. Identity-ready — created by the BFF

- [ ] Root `tenant.tenants` schema/record exists for the new tenant code and organization name.
- [ ] Tenant encryption key exists.
- [ ] Keycloak organization exists and maps to the root tenant.
- [ ] Tenant-admin membership and organization-scoped roles exist in Keycloak.
- [ ] Managed DIGIT employee account can be created/refreshed and a tenant-scoped DIGIT token can be issued.
- [ ] Tenant appears in `GET /identity/v1/tenants` for the member.

Passing this level means **the tenant can be selected and signed into**, not that PGR is configured.

### 1. Configurator-ready — minimum shared platform configuration

- [ ] Required MDMS v2 schema definitions exist at the root tenant.
- [ ] `tenant.citymodule` enables only the modules intended for v1 (at minimum the employee shell/configurator and PGR dependencies).
- [ ] `ACCESSCONTROL-ROLES.roles`, actions, and role-action mappings contain the tenant-admin/configurator permissions required by the deployed stack.
- [ ] The selected-country `common-masters.MobileNumberValidation` schema and default record exist before the managed DIGIT account is created.
- [ ] Deployment has installed and smoke-tested every platform-provisioner access action required by Level 0, including `POST /mdms-v2/v2/_create/common-masters.MobileNumberValidation`; these grants are deployment prerequisites, not records discovered during signup.
- [ ] Data-security encryption, decryption, masking, and security-policy records exist.
- [ ] Required Level 1 common masters exist: `StateInfo`, `GenderType`, and tenant branding/theme defaults where consumed. Mobile-number validation is a Level 0 prerequisite and is deliberately not deferred here.
- [ ] `common-masters.IdFormat` has the formats required by PGR and HRMS.
- [ ] Baseline localizations exist for tenant name, navigation, common UI, enabled modules, and supported locales.
- [ ] Tenant admin can open the configurator against the root tenant without missing-schema, access-control, or localization failures.

### 2. PGR-ready — minimum tenant-specific operating data

- [ ] Boundary hierarchy definition exists.
- [ ] At least one valid boundary chain and assignable leaf boundary exists; relationships and materialized paths are valid.
- [ ] At least one department exists.
- [ ] At least one designation exists and references a valid department where required.
- [ ] Complaint hierarchy definition exists.
- [ ] At least one active complaint leaf/service code exists with a valid department and SLA. Use `RAINMAKER-PGR.ComplaintHierarchyDefinition` + `ComplaintHierarchy` on the current stack; document compatibility only if a deployed environment still reads legacy `ServiceDefs`.
- [ ] PGR workflow/business service exists with valid start, assignment, resolution, rejection/reopen, and terminal transitions for the supported flow.
- [ ] PGR roles and action mappings exist (`GRO`, `DGRO`, `PGR_LME`, etc., limited to roles actually used by the configured workflow).
- [ ] At least one HRMS employee exists with a valid DIGIT user, department, designation, jurisdiction, and workflow role so a complaint can be processed. Do not confuse this with the BFF-managed DIGIT account.
- [ ] Localizations exist for boundaries, departments, designations, complaint hierarchy nodes/leaves, workflow states/actions, and PGR UI labels.
- [ ] A citizen can create a test complaint against the root tenant and selected leaf boundary/service code.
- [ ] An authorized employee can find, assign, and resolve it; the citizen can view and complete the supported post-resolution action.

### 3. Operational enhancements — not a blocker for the first usable tenant

- [ ] Notification templates/channels.
- [ ] Escalation configuration beyond the minimum workflow SLA.
- [ ] Dashboard/KPI/indexer configuration and historical analytics.
- [ ] Real boundary polygons/map configuration.
- [ ] Additional locales and full translated catalogs.
- [ ] Additional employees, departments, complaint types, and sample/demo content.

## Existing configurator mapping

- **Phase 1:** tenant identity/branding and select existing root tenant.
- **Phase 2:** boundary hierarchy, boundaries, relationships, and optional geometry.
- **Phase 3:** departments, designations, complaint hierarchy definition, and complaint leaves.
- **Phase 4:** HRMS employees, roles, and jurisdictions.

The document must identify gaps not currently covered by these phases, especially module enablement, access-control data, ID formats, security policies, workflow, and baseline localization.

## Deliverable

Add `docs/onboarding/usable-tenant-baseline.md` containing:

1. the readiness levels above;
2. a matrix for every required artifact: owner service/store, tenant scope, schema/API, source (platform default vs user input), configurator phase, rerun behavior, and verification query;
3. a copy/paste operator checklist for a fresh tenant;
4. a clear handoff point between BFF identity onboarding and configurator/application onboarding;
5. an explicit list of optional items so they are not allowed to block v1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The document is merged and linked from the onboarding/BFF architecture docs.
- [ ] Every required item has a named owner and a concrete verification method; no generic “bootstrap tenant” step remains.
- [ ] Checklist is run against one newly created empty root tenant and records pass/fail evidence, including tenant-local mobile-policy visibility before user creation and a provisioner authorization smoke test for every Level-0 write.
- [ ] Missing items are split into implementation issues rather than silently copied from a demo tenant.
- [ ] A tenant that passes Levels 0–2 can sign in, load the configurator/employee shell, submit one complaint, and process it through the configured workflow.
- [ ] No `.city` child tenant or unrelated demo data is created.

items.title: Standalone Trader Intelligence — public third-party trade analysis, provenance and chart overlays
items.body:
# Standalone trader-activity intelligence and external-trade analysis

**Normative boundary:** tester is entirely independent. NO integration or runtime dependency on Unified, Grid, Strattester, Math, MetaAnalyse, Terminan or their Gateway. Only tester's own PostgreSQL, ingestion, analytics, strategy/backtest, local terminal, Codex Control Plane.

Goal: ingest permitted public trader-specific transactions/positions where truly available, compare with market history, visualize actual observed entry/exit points and clearly labeled inferred hypotheses, and let Codex analyze through tester's typed read-only research API.

## Source and legal gates
- Source registry with official API/documentation URL, dataset category, terms/access requirements, auth needs, rate limits, redistribution/privacy restrictions, update cadence, availability window, provenance and source confidence. Verify actual public access; no assumed public per-trader histories, no unauthorized scraping, bypass, leaked/private IDs, or keys for trading.
- Distinguish (A) anonymous public market trades (execution prints: price/size/taker side, NO trader identity), (B) opt-in/public trader activity (leaderboard/copy-trading/verified shared portfolio), (C) self-provided user-authorized CSV/export, (D) inferred strategies/positions. Never join A into named trader identity without independently verified linkage.
- For B, record published trader alias/pseudonymous source identifier, disclosed execution/position, timestamps, side, size, leverage if actually provided, PnL and fees if actually provided; do not infer absent fields as factual. Respect source terms, remove sensitive personal data, deletion/revocation and retention controls.

## Canonical data and uncertainty
- Tables: trader_sources, trader_profiles (pseudonymous), disclosed_trades, disclosed_positions, trade_events, trade_observations, reconstruction_hypotheses, analysis_runs, chart_artifacts, evidence_links; use B migrations/schema and typed Decimal strings. Stable scoped identity (source, trader_id, trade_id), exact source precision, UTC event/observed/published times, delayed disclosures, revision history, source evidence/hash and validity/coverage/availability. Distinguish source revisions/corrections and late reporting.
- Entry/exit matching ONLY when disclosed or deterministically reconcilable from verified events; ambiguous partial closes, fees, funding, average cost, transfers, liquidations and position mode yield explicit UNKNOWN. Reconstruction has confidence/evidence and is never tagged observed. Source claims of profitability are not audited realized PnL unless verifiable.
- Market context at decision time: price, OHLCV, volume, taker delta/CVD, footprint, OI/funding, VWAP, POC, volatility, support/resistance, liquidity proxies where available; never pretend historical L2/L3 book exists.

## Analytics
- Cohort performance: realized/unrealized distinctions, gross/net, win rate, profit factor, expectancy, drawdown, exposure, holding time, leverage, risk, fees, funding, survivorship and selection bias, delayed publication and hindsight bias. Avoid ranking on unverified outcomes. Compare observed trader actions vs reproducible baseline and benchmark with uncertainty. No assumption copy trading is profitable.
- Replay/strategy inference: infer candidate rules from disclosed behavior, show counterexamples, time split train/test, avoid lookahead and curve fitting; feed only explicitly approved hypotheses to F's simulation engine, not automatic trading.

## User experience and Codex
- Trader explorer, filters by source/trader/instrument/date/confidence; overlays actual disclosed entries/exits and inferred hypotheses with different shapes/colors and evidence tooltip; link position legs and market context; show unknown and disclosure lag. Timeframe pan/zoom and provenance overlays. Click event -> Codex analysis plan, inspect why, compare peers, simulate rule, produce signed/digest-backed artifact; chart updates through typed local control API. Natural-language query -> plan preview -> approved read-only research/backtest job -> verified artifact; no direct SQL/shell, no real orders.
- Add bounded APIs /api/trader-sources, /api/traders, /api/traders/{id}/events, /api/trader-analysis, /api/trader-overlays with authenticated scope, cursor, UTC ranges, dataset revision and evidence. Do not expose nonpublic data.

## Acceptance
- Anonymous trade cannot become named trader; missing SL/TP/fees not fabricated; source delay/revision; partial close, netting/hedge; conflicting events; no public source; opt-in import/revoke; idempotent retry, pagination evidence; market alignment with no future data; result provenance; 10 instrument stress, PG memory/disk; chart overlays match recorded events; Codex denied unsafe request; tests and independent review. Synthetic fixtures separate from real public data. Source-specific availability research must precede promises.
- Draft PR and contract tests only, no merge/deploy, no other repos. Coordinate B storage, A source adapters, C metrics, D UI, E API, F backtest, G Codex, MASTER oversight.

items.title: P0: Coordinate parallel multi-chat dataset ingestion (source owners, branches, QA and merge gates)
items.body:
## Purpose

Run **multiple independent source-ingestion ChatGPT conversations in parallel**, without conflicting edits, duplicate source work, or false Source Health claims. GitHub issues/branches/PRs are the *only shared coordination system*; separate chats do **not** automatically see or message one another. The user can start separate sessions and direct each to this issue.

**Product scope: all industries and all facility types**, not FDA/life-sciences-only. Source identities are not automatically verified physical facilities, and no absent observation means zero risk.

## Snapshot at setup (2026-10-23; verify against latest main before working)

- EPA FRS national source identity index: 5,354,716; durable private serving remains outstanding, [#39](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/39) and [#3](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/3).
- NOAA Storm Events: source ingestion implemented in recent merged work; verify live/deployed freshness and browser visibility before marking fully production ready.
- NOAA OR&R IncidentNews: work in progress; [PR #72](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/pull/72) open for browser regression/status; **do not independently reimplement** this lane.
- FDA device/drug, Canada NPRI, Ireland EPA: already represented as distinct source registries; confirm published counts/metadata; avoid reingestion without a scoped fix.
- Foundational [#4](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/4) covers verified all-industry hazard, incidents, insurance and interruption findings.

## Parallel lanes (one separate chat/branch/PR per lane)

| Lane | Source focus | Boundary / distinct deliverable | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A: Flood & wildfire** | FEMA NFHL and official US wildfire layers, plus source-vintage/geometry QA | Geospatial hazard importers, staged tiles/shapes/point-in-polygon **only at corroborated site coords**; do not edit NOAA IncidentNews or FRS registry ingestion | P0 |
| **B: Environmental compliance** | EPA ECHO plus facility-level TRI/RCRA/RMP where permitted | Live download/import + stable program IDs, normalized findings, distinct source identities; never equate a compliance record with a physical insured property | P0 |
| **C: Industrial events** | USCG NRC, CSB, PHMSA | Independent incident parsers, dates, location uncertainty, severity context, **unverified report** flags, matching candidates, outcome corroboration | P0 |
| **D: Reliability & BI** | Public utility/provider mapping, EIA-861 context, outage datasets where available, public financial event reports | Contextual reliability and independently grounded interruption evidence; EIA-861 is not a facility-specific outage/claims database | P1 |
| **E: Registry/operations & integration (coordinator)** | [#39](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/39), shared provenance/manifest, private serving, canonical review-only crosswalk, report wiring, QA and deployment | **Sole owner** of shared schemas/UI/shared Source Health files and final merges; do not reimplement source importers already owned by A–D | P0 |

Additional future lanes can include other countries/global all-industry registries, earthquakes/wind, supply-chain routes, and outcome/claims validation. Create one issue/branch per source before touching shared code.

## Cross-chat synchronization rule

1. Each chat reads **latest main**, this coordination issue, [#3](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/3), [#4](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/4), [#39](https://github.com/jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest/issues/39), and open PRs **before implementing**.
2. Each lane claims its ownership in a comment on this issue (lane, sources, branch name, linked PR, status, blockers). Do not duplicate a lane already claimed by active work.
3. Use `ingest/<source-or-lane>-<distinct-suffix>` from fresh main; no direct pushes to main; no changes outside owned importer/tests/source metadata except via coordinator.
4. Provide an isolated importer module, reproducible run command, tested source licenses/API requirements, deterministic transforms, source-specific fixtures, schema/identifier/duplicate/null/coordinate tests, and provenance+freshness manifest.
5. Record actual **data counts and evidentiary state**, not just HTTP test: NOT_TESTED -> PROBED -> DOWNLOADED -> STAGED -> NORMALIZED -> INDEXED -> VERIFIED -> DEPLOYED. Record latest run, published vintage, accepted/rejected rows, source IDs, coverage, null coordinates, checksum, failure modes, and known geographic bounds. VERIFIED requires content-level checks; DEPLOYED requires live app/backend verification.
6. Preserve original source keys and raw records separately from review-only candidate facility linkage. Use actual source-reported geometry/addresses and confidence; **never infer one facility = one source record**. Never represent external risk observations as insured losses or policy coverage.
7. Open focused PR with test evidence and deployment impact. Coordinator rebases/merges PRs one at a time, reruns full suite and live browser checks, checks Source Health statuses, publishes count/freshness ledger. No PR should declare another lane's status.
8. Hosting constraint: GitHub Pages is static; multi-GB indexes, private APIs, ingestion schedules and auth require a durable backend. CI artifacts are staging, not persistent production. Do not claim source availability if only CI artifacts exist.

## Per-lane definition of done

- [ ] Official source access and data-use constraints verified
- [ ] Real download/ingestion run completed (not simulation-only)
- [ ] Raw rows and accepted/rejected rows reconciled with checksums
- [ ] Source-specific IDs and geospatial limitations documented
- [ ] Transform, QA, and failure-mode regression tests pass in CI
- [ ] No unreviewed canonical physical-site auto-merges
- [ ] Query/storage integration and source health manifest are verified
- [ ] Deployment runtime/app shows **accurate** state and count; unreleased work remains labeled staging

## Copy/paste for each worker chat

> Work on **Lane [A/B/C/D]** in `jhennessy-pharm3r/FacilityTest`. First read the master parallel-ingestion coordination issue and current open PRs. Claim the lane there with your branch and source list. Ingest real public source data, implement a reproducible pipeline with source-identity preservation and QA, and open a focused PR. Do not touch other lanes or shared registry/UI except through the coordinator; do not merge your own PR. Report actual downloaded, normalized, indexed, and deployed counts separately. All industries and facility types are in scope. Continue implementation and verification until your lane meets the explicit gate or document any hard blocker.
