items.title: Tenant deployment orchestrator: versioned releases, migrations, and control-plane reconciliation

milestone.description: Everything that must ship before the authhero 1.0 release. Anything that can wait goes in a later milestone.

items.body:
## Context

WFP dispatch namespaces version user Workers internally but expose no versions API — no list, fetch, deploy-specific, or rollback ([confirmed in CF docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-for-platforms/workers-for-platforms/reference/limits/): "Gradual Deployments is not supported yet for user Workers. Changes made to user Workers create a new version that deployed all-at-once to 100% of traffic"). The public surface is script get/put/delete, content, settings, secrets, bindings, tags. "Changing a version" for a tenant means re-PUTting the bundle we want. Therefore we own the release registry, and per-tenant version management becomes a control-plane feature — which is also a product differentiator (per-tenant pinning / maintenance windows, something Auth0 doesn't offer).

Prior art reviewed: Atlas (atlasgo) database-per-tenant guides (target groups, drift detection, plan/apply, content-hashed migration dirs) and Turso Multi-DB Schemas (since deprecated). No off-the-shelf tool covers WFP code-version orchestration — every WFP platform builds its own control plane.

## Relationship to #1026 (already shipped)

This is **the next phase on the existing tenant-operations engine**, not a new system. Shipped via PRs #1037–#1040, #1042:

- `tenant_operations` + `tenant_operation_events` + `rollouts` control-plane tables (`packages/drizzle/src/schema/control-plane/`), with `target_worker_version` / `target_database_version`, canary tenant ids, wave size
- Executor adapter (`inline` | `cloudflare-workflows`), row-first enqueue, idempotent steps
- `createWfpProvisionerSteps` (packages/cloudflare): DB create → migrations → script PUT → secrets → seed → verify → mark-ready, already schema-first
- Tenant columns: `deployment_type`, `storage_kind`, `bundle_configuration`, `worker_version`, `database_version`, `worker_script_name`, `d1_database_id`
- Per-tenant D1 migration tracking table `_authhero_provisioner_migrations` (name + applied_at, legacy backfill handling)

**Genuinely new in this issue:** release registry (R2 + `releases`/`channels` tables), build-time `requires_schema` derivation, the `upgrade` operation steps (kind exists in the enum, no executor steps yet), drift detection, write-freeze, and the reconciliation loop.

## Design

**Model: desired state + reconciliation** (operator pattern). Directory DB holds desired state per tenant; controllers diff against observed state and converge. Every fleet operation produces a reviewable plan before apply (canary tenants first via `rollouts`, fail-fast per tenant).

**Release registry**
- CI publishes immutable artifacts to R2: `releases/{project}/{semver}/worker.mjs` + `manifest.json`
- Release version = the consuming project's semver (the deployable artifact), with authhero package versions recorded in the manifest as provenance
- Manifest also carries bindings, compatibility_date, compatibility_flags — a code rollback re-PUTs matching config, not just matching JS
- `requires_schema` derived at build time from the bundled adapter's Drizzle migration journal head — no manual bookkeeping (same derivation as today's `database_version` = last migration name)
- Everything content-hashed; verify before apply

**Directory schema (control plane)**
- `releases` (version, r2_key, git_sha, schema_head, channel, created_at) — new
- `channels` (stable/beta → version) — new
- tenant rows: reuse existing `deployment_type` (pooled/shared vs dedicated/wfp) and `storage_kind` (engine); add `channel` + optional `pinned_version` (two columns, not one polymorphic ref) + write-freeze flag. `worker_version` / `database_version` remain the observed state.
- Per-migration observability: reuse `tenant_operation_events` (step = migration name) rather than a new `migration_attempts` table

**Deploy sequence per tenant (durable workflow — extends `createWfpProvisionerSteps` into the `upgrade` operation)**
1. Resolve desired release (pin or channel)
2. Check `requires_schema` vs tenant `database_version`
3. Apply pending migrations via D1 HTTP batch — **migration SQL and its `_authhero_provisioner_migrations` insert in the same batch** (today they're separate calls; a crash between them re-runs non-idempotent DDL), one migration per batch; record attempts as operation events
4. PUT worker bundle + metadata (bindings/flags from manifest) to dispatch namespace script; secrets re-synced (upgrade must not drop them)
5. Mirror state onto script tags (`version:x.y.z`, `channel:stable`, `tenant:id`) as out-of-band drift check (8-tag limit per script; 2 already used by the provisioner)
6. Post-deploy verify step (health check against the tenant) before marking succeeded
7. Update directory

**Rules**
- Schema first, code second. Forward-only migrations, expand/contract discipline (every migration backward-compatible with the **oldest supported pinned version**, not just the previous release; destructive cleanup ships N releases later). Rollback = code only, never schema.
- **Version-skew policy**: pinning is bounded by a support window (max N releases behind the channel head). Pins older than the window block destructive migrations fleet-wide, so pins need expiry/escalation. Pinned tenants' schemas advance only when their deployed release's `requires_schema` demands it.
- **Per-tenant single-flight**: at most one running operation per tenant (lease or conditional status transition on `tenant_operations`). The current engine's idempotent steps don't prevent a rollout wave and a reconciler converging the same tenant concurrently.
- One migration system owns any given database. Pooled plane = Kysely/PlanetScale (single shared DB, single migration run). Dedicated plane = Drizzle/D1, tracked via `_authhero_provisioner_migrations` (the Drizzle journal is a build-time input only — no second tracking table on tenant DBs).
- Feature parity enforced via the shared adapter conformance suite, not schema identity.
- Worker schema-compatibility check: primary enforcement is the post-deploy verify step in the workflow. The runtime check is a cached backstop that serves a maintenance response — **not** a cold-start crash loop (that turns a control-plane mistake into a hard tenant outage and adds a D1 read per cold start).
- Write-freeze enforcement mechanism must be explicit (request-time check against pushed config, not just a directory flag).

**Drift detection**: background scan comparing script tags, `_authhero_provisioner_migrations`, and config hashes against directory; flag (not auto-fix) anything changed outside the pipeline. Directory is truth; tags are a hint (a PUT can succeed while the tag update fails). Drizzle's per-migration snapshots give schema-drift diffing nearly free.

**Future controllers on the same engine** (same desired/observed/plan/apply contract): config push (config lives in tenant DB, controller pushes diffs), backup policy (check D1 Time Travel first; build long-retention R2 export on top), log routing config (reconcile the routing, not the stream — logs stay on the tail-worker/OTLP path). Pool→dedicated extraction workflow (filter by tenant_id, transform MySQL→SQLite, verify hashes, flip routing, delete from pool) as a later controller — sessions/refresh tokens must migrate or tenant users get logged out.

## Open decisions

- [ ] WFP-per-tenant vs cell Workers: per-tenant version pinning is the strongest argument for WFP; partly pre-decided by the shipped `deployment_type` column — revisit explicitly before adding `releases`/`channels` columns
- [ ] Pooled plane: permanent standard tier vs transitional (determines whether we invest in extraction workflow or in dual-schema authoring ergonomics)
- [ ] Version-skew window size (how many releases behind a pin may fall) and pin expiry/escalation policy
- [ ] Verify email/collation semantics in the D1 Drizzle schema before migrating real tenants (MySQL CI collation vs SQLite case sensitivity — login-lookup risk)
- [ ] Confirm D1 Time Travel coverage before building backup exports

## Non-goals (for now)
- Down migrations across the fleet
- Generic framework / UI — one workflow engine, controllers added when a real task exists
- Gradual (percentage) rollout within a single tenant (not supported by WFP user Workers anyway)

- `.engineering/DECISIONS-LEDGER.md` D-153 and `.engineering/IMPLEMENTATION-SEQUENCE.md` order 6: versioned Spryxel DNA + Asset core is next NECESSARY increment after Identity/Tenancy, Projects, durable Job and Credit Ledger/CostGuard foundations.
- No authorization to leapfrog G0/G1/G2 website/brand/legal decisions or expand V1 scope. This planning issue does not modify the canonical source authority.

## Candidate mission / functionality, subject to owner review
1. **Project DNA v1:** project/tenant-scoped, versioned structured DNA document/profile with validation and deterministic immutable version identifiers; explicit draft/published lifecycle, lineage, provenance and restore/fork semantics. Avoid rewriting historical versions.
2. **Asset Core v1:** canonical metadata record + provenance/lineage links, versioned asset identity, project association, content digest/checksum, S3-compatible object reference with tenant scoped authorization and status. No need to implement full image inference, models/GPU, 2.5D/3D, public sharing, video, billing purchase, export pack, QA service or generation UX in WO-010.
3. **Security and cost:** enforce application auth, membership/role, project ownership, FORCE RLS where required, object-storage path authorization, immutable audit evidence, denied cross-tenant reads/writes, fail-closed CostGuard/ledger controls. No economic purchase/balance activation. Separate developer fixture/local tests from production auth.
4. **Data integrity:** schema and migration candidates, contracts and ports for persistence/object storage, idempotency and replay safety, bounded upload/metadata mutations, validation for content types/sizes/hash and threat model for storage URLs. Favor existing app/provider abstraction rather than new paid service.
5. **API/web scope:** only read/write surface explicitly granted by future admitted WO; document potential product route and UX needs, do not assume redesign of public frontend or alter AuthKit/Jobs/Credit Ledger.
6. **Observability:** audit records linking identity, tenant, project, asset/DNA version, storage operation and provenance without exposing user secrets or token strings.

## Candidate deliverables to PREPARE, not implement
- [ ] `WO-010-DRAFT.md` with complete statement of work, path allowlist, scope/non-goals, admission prerequisites, ownership, budgets, exit/stop condition.
- [ ] Schema/data model v1 and contract sketches: DNA v1, Asset v1, lineage/provenance, storage metadata, version validity and state graph; reversible migration strategy.
- [ ] API/port and tenant ACL/RLS / object storage threat-model plan, with security-focused negative test matrix.
- [ ] E2E/worker/integration/credit guard acceptance matrix with PostgreSQL/Redis/SeaweedFS local infrastructure + explicit NOT_RUN if unavailable.
- [ ] Context Lock **CANDIDATE** only, generated against *current* main exact SHA and canonical fingerprints, to be **formally admitted later** by authority. Never reuse WO-009 or previous lock.
- [ ] Independent HIGH_ASSURANCE review and owner signoff checklist; no documents marked CANONICAL/APPROVED prematurely.
- [ ] Dependencies and draft sequencing for next bounded inference and QA/export increments, not implementation.

## Entry/exit gates
**Entry to implementation NOT SATISFIED:** objective Source Pack/DoD/GEF review, explicit owner WO admission, fresh Context Lock, precise file ownership and SHA, high-assurance boundary/audit signoff. Prior approval of frontend #89 is a separate scope and does not automatically control DNA admission.

**Expected later proof:** unit/typecheck/lint/build, database FORCE RLS tenant-negative integration, object-store ACL and checksum tests, idempotency/version/lineage invariants, failure/rollback behavior, worker/job/CostGuard nonregression, GEF exact-head checks, independent security review, main protected merge only after fresh permission. Record EXECUTED / OBSERVED / NOT_RUN, no assumed local Docker proof.

**Current STOP:** `SPRYXEL_WO010_DNA_ASSET_CORE_PROPOSAL_READY_FOR_OWNER_SCOPE_REVIEW_NOT_ADMITTED`.

items.title: MVP: Flat monorepo + working backend/frontend/docs/data + central schema
items.body:
## Goal
Ship a **hackathon-honest MVP** of Klima with a **flat** monorepo (complYaigent-style) and working surfaces for **backend, frontend, docs, and data**, plus a **central schema** shared across packages.

## Target layout
```text
klima/
├── mobile/      # Flutter (keep)
├── backend/     # FastAPI (was web/api)
├── frontend/    # Next LGU dashboard (was web/dashboard)
├── docs/        # VitePress (was web/docs)
├── data/        # ETL + DuckDB assets (canonical pipeline home)
└── schema/      # central contracts (Pydantic / OpenAPI / JSON Schema)
```

Reference flat layout: https://github.com/liitkud/complyaigent (`backend/`, `frontend/`, `docs/`).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Layout is flat (no `web/` nesting)
- [ ] `backend` boots; health + mobile contract endpoints work
- [ ] `frontend` talks to live backend (not mock-only stub page)
- [ ] `docs` site builds with getting-started + API overview
- [ ] `data` owns ETL; bronze ingest runnable via documented command
- [ ] `schema/` is single source of truth for hazard/report/safezone/community models
- [ ] README + STATUS match reality
- [ ] Each workstream has a handoff under `docs/handoffs/`

## Non-goals (post-MVP)
- Production Auth0/Keycloak multi-tenant RBAC
- Full silver/gold medallion orchestration + schedulers
- Channel bots (Messenger/Telegram/Viber)
- Perfect offline sync on mobile

## Children
- #3 Flatten
- #4 Central schema
- #5 Backend
- #6 Frontend
- #7 Docs
- #8 Data

**Branch:** `docs/mvp-handoffs` — [mvp plan](https://github.com/Signal-No-5/klima/blob/docs/mvp-handoffs/docs/mvp/README.md)

items.title: Dedicated database option

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

Issue #27 gives the platform the ability to *route* a tenant to a dedicated PostgreSQL database. It does not give us the ability to sell one. There is no entitlement that grants it, no way to provision a CloudNativePG cluster for a specific customer, and — most importantly — no way to move a hospital that is already live on the shared database onto its own without downtime that a hospital cannot accept. A hospital's clinical systems cannot be offline for a data migration; the emergency department does not close for a maintenance window.

That gap matters commercially. Large hospital groups, trust-run institutions and government tenders frequently make physical database separation a mandatory requirement, and the customers who ask for it are the largest ones. They also ask what follows from it: a separate backup lineage they can point an auditor at, restore testing on their own data, and a defined RPO and RTO for their cluster rather than a platform-wide average. Under NABH information-management expectations and DPDP 2023 accountability obligations, a Data Fiduciary being able to describe exactly where its records live and how they are recovered is a real requirement, not a preference.

Affected: the hospital admin and CIO at an enterprise tenant, the DPO who must document the storage location and processor arrangements, platform operations who will run these clusters, and finance, since a dedicated cluster carries real infrastructure cost that must be recovered by the subscription tier rather than absorbed.

The hard part of this issue is not provisioning. It is the live cutover from shared to dedicated with no data loss and a cutover window measured in seconds.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As an** enterprise hospital group with a contractual physical-separation requirement
**I want** my tenant's data to live in a dedicated PostgreSQL cluster with its own backup lineage, restore testing and documented RPO/RTO, provisioned and migrated without clinical downtime
**So that** I can satisfy my own information-security, accreditation and procurement obligations while receiving identical product behaviour.

### Scope

**In scope**

* A `dedicated_database` subscription entitlement, priced as a tier add-on, that gates the ability to request the mode.
* Provisioning: a Temporal workflow that creates a CloudNativePG cluster via ArgoCD/GitOps, applies the full schema to the platform's current version, registers credentials in the vault and registers the target in the `tenant_storage` catalogue from #27.
* Live cutover from shared schema to the dedicated cluster: bulk copy of the tenant's rows, change capture during copy, verification, brief read-only freeze, tail application, catalogue switch, resume — with an abort path at every step.
* Verification: row counts and per-table content checksums compared between source and target before cutover is permitted, and a post-cutover reconciliation report retained as evidence.
* Rollback: the source data is retained read-only for a configurable retention window (default 14 days) so cutover can be reversed within that period.
* Dedicated backup lineage per cluster with its own retention, encryption, defined RPO/RTO and scheduled restore verification into an isolated namespace.
* Source-data purge after the retention window, executed as an explicit, authorised, audited operation — never automatic and silent.
* AdminConnect visibility for the tenant: isolation mode, region, cluster reference, last successful backup, last verified restore, RPO/RTO commitments.

**Out of scope**

* The routing framework, catalogue and pool management — issue #27; this issue consumes it.
* Row-level security — issue #26; RLS remains enabled inside the dedicated database.
* Dedicated schema mode — available through #27 without this issue's cutover machinery for new tenants.
* Object storage path separation and per-tenant encryption keys — the Data Isolation storage and key-management stories.
* Cross-region residency moves — the Country Profile epic; this issue moves a tenant within its existing region only.

---

## Recommended Solution

Provisioning and cutover are two Temporal workflows. Nothing in this path is a script an engineer runs by hand, because a partially completed migration of clinical data is the worst possible outcome.

**Provisioning** (`DedicatedClusterProvisioningWorkflow`): assert entitlement → render CloudNativePG `Cluster` manifest into the GitOps repository with tenant-derived naming, region pinned to the tenant's residency region → wait for ArgoCD sync and cluster readiness → create roles (`hms_app`, `hms_migrator`, `hms_platform` per #26) → apply schema to current version → write credentials to vault → insert `tenant_storage` row with `status = provisioning`. Idempotent at every step and safe to retry.

**Cutover** (`TenantCutoverWorkflow`) uses logical replication rather than dump/restore, because it is the only approach that keeps the freeze short:

```
1. snapshot     – record source LSN; create publication filtered to this tenant's rows
2. bulk copy    – COPY each table WHERE tenant_id = $tenant into target (parallel, batched)
3. tail         – logical replication applies changes from the snapshot LSN forward
4. verify       – per-table row counts + md5 of ordered row digests, source vs target
5. freeze       – catalogue status -> 'migrating'; writes rejected with ErrTenantReadOnly (#27)
6. drain        – wait until replication lag = 0, re-verify checksums
7. switch       – tenant_storage.isolation_mode = 'dedicated_database'; publish
                  platform.tenant_storage.changed; resolver caches invalidate
8. resume       – status -> 'active'; writes accepted against the dedicated cluster
9. quarantine   – source rows marked read-only, retained 14 days, then purged on approval
```

Only steps 5–8 are user-visible, and the target is under 60 seconds. Steps 1–4 run for as long as they need against a live system. Failure before step 7 aborts cleanly: drop the subscription, delete the target data, leave the tenant untouched on shared. Failure after step 7 rolls forward, not back — the reverse path is the same workflow run in the opposite direction using the retained source, which is why the retention window exists.

Verification uses ordered digests rather than row counts alone, because a count match with content divergence is exactly the failure that would otherwise reach a clinician:

```sql
SELECT md5(string_agg(t.digest, '' ORDER BY t.digest)) FROM (
  SELECT md5(row(x.*)::text) AS digest FROM patient x WHERE tenant_id = $1
) t;
```

Rows containing large objects are excluded from digesting and verified by count plus checksum of their storage keys.

API surface:

```
POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/isolation/request      { mode: "dedicated_database" }  (tenant-initiated, entitlement-gated)
GET  /api/v1/tenants/{id}/isolation              (mode, cluster ref, region, RPO/RTO, last backup, last restore test)
POST /internal/tenants/{id}/isolation/provision  (platform, starts provisioning workflow)
POST /internal/tenants/{id}/isolation/cutover    (platform, starts cutover workflow)
GET  /internal/tenants/{id}/isolation/cutover/status
POST /internal/tenants/{id}/isolation/abort
POST /internal/tenants/{id}/isolation/purge-source  { confirmation }
GET  /internal/clusters/{ref}/restore-tests
```

Events:

```json
// platform.tenant_isolation.cutover_completed
{ "tenant_id":"…", "from":"shared_schema", "to":"dedicated_database",
  "cluster_ref":"hms-in-prod-t9f2a", "freeze_seconds":41,
  "tables_verified":214, "rows_migrated":8412775, "source_retained_until":"2026-08-03" }
```

Consumers that hold tenant-scoped caches (notification service, PDF renderer, reporting projections) subscribe and invalidate.

OpenFGA:

```
type tenant_isolation
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define admin: admin from tenant
    define can_request: admin
    define platform_operator: [user, service#member]
    define can_cutover: platform_operator
    define can_purge_source: [user, role#assignee] and platform_operator
```

`can_purge_source` is deliberately a distinct, narrowly held relation: destroying the rollback path for a hospital's clinical data must require a specific authorisation, not general operator access.

Backups: each cluster gets its own CloudNativePG backup configuration writing to a tenant-prefixed object-storage path with encryption at rest, WAL archiving for point-in-time recovery, and a monthly automated restore into an isolated namespace whose success is recorded and surfaced on `GET /tenants/{id}/isolation`. A restore test that has not succeeded within its interval raises an alert and is visible to the customer, because an untested backup is not a backup.

Sequencing: depends on #27 (catalogue, resolver, migration orchestration), #26 (roles and RLS applied inside the new cluster), and the AdminConnect subscriptions epic for the entitlement. Non-prod validation must use synthetic data only — PHI never appears in non-prod, so cutover rehearsals run against a synthetic tenant of comparable volume.

Risks: (a) silent data divergence — mitigated by ordered-digest verification before and after the freeze, with cutover blocked on any mismatch; (b) an over-long freeze harming clinical operations — mitigated by draining replication lag to zero before freezing and by an automatic abort if the freeze exceeds its budget; (c) irreversible cutover — mitigated by the 14-day read-only source retention and a separately authorised purge; (d) cost of dedicated clusters exceeding the tier price — mitigated by per-cluster cost attribution reported to finance monthly.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a live tenant on shared schema with the `dedicated_database` entitlement and approximately 8 million rows
**When** provisioning and cutover workflows complete
**Then** all tenant data is present in the dedicated cluster with per-table digests matching the source, the write freeze lasted under 60 seconds, the catalogue reports `dedicated_database` and all pods route there without restart, RLS is enabled and forced on every table in the new cluster, `platform.tenant_isolation.cutover_completed` is published, and no other tenant experienced elevated latency or errors during the migration.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a cutover that reaches verification with a digest mismatch on one table — a row written during bulk copy that replication has not yet applied
**When** the workflow evaluates the verification step
**Then** the cutover does not proceed to freeze, the workflow retries the drain-and-verify cycle up to its configured limit, on continued mismatch it aborts and drops the target data, the tenant remains fully operational on shared schema with no read-only period, and an alert names the tenant, the table and the digest difference.

### Edge Cases

* The tenant issues writes throughout bulk copy — logical replication applies them; the drain step must reach zero lag before the freeze, verified by test with sustained write load.
* An abort is requested during bulk copy — the target data is removed, the publication and subscription are dropped, the vault entry is revoked, and the cluster is either retained for retry or deprovisioned by explicit choice.
* Rollback requested on day 13 of the retention window — the reverse cutover succeeds; the same request on day 15, after purge, is refused with an explicit statement that the source no longer exists.
* A table added by a schema migration between provisioning and cutover — the workflow re-asserts schema parity immediately before verification and fails fast on mismatch rather than migrating an incomplete schema.
* The dedicated cluster's storage fills during bulk copy — the workflow detects the failure, aborts, and the tenant is unaffected; capacity is sized with headroom derived from measured source volume plus 100%.
* A monthly restore test fails — the tenant's isolation view shows the failed verification date, an alert raises a P1, and the failure is visible to the customer rather than hidden.
## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team’s agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team’s agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** an enterprise tenant can be provisioned onto, or migrated live onto, its own PostgreSQL cluster with verified data equivalence, its own backup lineage and tested restores, and identical product behaviour throughout.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** the physical-separation requirement stops being a blocker in enterprise and tender procurement, and the dedicated tier is recoverable as a priced add-on with per-cluster cost attribution.
* **Success metric or validation method:** write freeze under 60 seconds at p95 for tenants up to 50 million rows; zero digest mismatches at post-cutover reconciliation across 100% of tables; RPO of 5 minutes and RTO of 60 minutes demonstrated by an actual restore, not a documented intention; monthly automated restore verification succeeding on 100% of dedicated clusters; no measurable latency impact on other tenants during a migration, verified against the shared cluster's p95 during the cutover window.
* **Monitoring period, where applicable:** 90 days after the first production cutover, tracking freeze duration, reconciliation results, restore-test outcomes, backup age per cluster and per-cluster infrastructure cost against tier pricing.

---
## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — "The experience works across supported devices and browsers."
**Reason:** the customer-facing surface delivered here is a single read-only isolation status panel in the AdminConnect console, which is desktop-only by product decision; the operational cutover controls are platform-internal endpoints with no rendered interface.
**Alternative validation:** the status panel is tested at 1280px and 1440px in Chrome and Firefox, and keyboard navigation, accessible labelling and WCAG AA contrast are applied in full. The cutover journey itself is validated by rehearsal against a synthetic tenant of production-comparable volume, since PHI must never appear in non-prod.
**Residual risk:** low — an administrator viewing isolation status on a tablet may encounter layout issues; no clinical, data-integrity or safety impact.
**Approved by:** Security and Platform lead.

items.body:
## Situation

Clinic (#247) and Hospital (#248) are self-serve, catalogue-priced plans on shared-schema tenancy
with row-level security. That model is deliberate and correct for the volume tiers, but it is not
sellable to a multi-hospital group, a national chain or a corporate healthcare operator. Those
buyers arrive with a procurement process, a security questionnaire and a negotiated contract, and
they consistently ask for three things the platform cannot currently express: **stronger data
isolation**, **contract-specific pricing that is not in any published price book**, and **their own
identity and integration credentials**.

Right now none of that exists. A group with 14 hospitals across three states would be modelled as
14 unrelated tenants with no consolidated contract, no group-level reporting, no shared practitioner
master and no way to hold a single negotiated rate. Their security team's request for a dedicated
database would have no answer. Their ABDM integration would run on shared platform credentials,
which is wrong: HIP registration under ABDM is per health facility and an enterprise group will
insist on its own registered credentials and its own audit trail.

Affected roles: the group CIO and procurement lead who sign the contract, the hospital admin at each
constituent facility, the group DPO who must be able to demonstrate isolation and data-principal
rights handling under the DPDP Act 2023, and the platform finance operator who has to invoice a
negotiated annual commitment rather than a catalogue price.

Commercially this is the tier that justifies enterprise sales effort. Legally, the isolation
entitlement is what makes a credible DPDP data-processing agreement possible, and the CERT-In
log-retention obligations are easier to evidence per-customer when the store is dedicated.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** hospital group CIO buying the platform for 14 facilities under one contract
**I want** an Enterprise plan that gives me dedicated data isolation, my own identity and ABDM
credentials, a negotiated contract price and consolidated group-level administration
**So that** my security, procurement and compliance requirements are met without bespoke
engineering per customer.

### Scope

**In scope**

* Enterprise plan version 1: all Hospital entitlements plus `config.isolation_model`
  (`shared_rls` | `dedicated_schema` | `dedicated_database`), enterprise SSO via the Keycloak
  identity-provider federation adapter, tenant-owned ABDM HIP/HIU credentials, extended audit
  retention, the highest support SLA band and a dedicated capacity reservation.
* **Contract-scoped pricing**: a `contract` entity that overrides the published price book for one
  customer — negotiated amount, committed term, annual or quarterly billing, uplift percentage on
  renewal, and an optional minimum commitment with overage rates.
* **Tenant group**: a parent organisation owning many facility tenants, one subscription at group
  level, consolidated entitlements inherited downward and consolidated invoicing.
* Isolation-model provisioning as a Temporal workflow: allocate the dedicated schema or CloudNativePG
  database, run migrations, repoint the tenant-scoped data-access layer, verify, then cut over.
* Contract lifecycle: draft → approved → countersigned → active → renewal-due, with approval
  thresholds so no single operator can unilaterally publish a discounted rate.
* Group-level reporting entitlement so the CIO sees cross-facility operational analytics — sourced
  from the OLAP store on de-identified aggregates only, never the live clinical database.

**Out of scope**

* The physical mechanics of a per-country regional deployment and data residency routing — that is a
  platform-infrastructure concern, not a plan entitlement; Enterprise consumes it.
* Government and public-scheme procurement terms, tender pricing and budget-locked billing — owned
  by #250, which shares the contract entity but has different lifecycle rules.
* Per-bed, per-facility and per-user rating mechanics (#253, #251, #252); Enterprise contracts
  reference those dimensions but override the rates.
* Module add-on catalogue and dependencies — owned by #254.
* Legal contract document generation and e-signature — the contract entity stores a reference to the
  executed document held in object storage, it does not author it.

---

## Recommended Solution

Build on the `adminconnect/billing` catalogue from #247. The new concepts are the tenant group, the
contract override layer and isolation provisioning.

### Data model

```sql
CREATE TABLE tenant_group (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  legal_name    text NOT NULL,
  gstin         text,
  country_code  text NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE tenant_group_member (
  tenant_group_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_group(id),
  tenant_id       uuid NOT NULL,
  joined_on       date NOT NULL,
  left_on         date,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_group_id, tenant_id)
);

CREATE TABLE contract (
  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_group_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tenant_group(id),
  plan_version_id   uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES plan_version(id),
  term              daterange NOT NULL,
  billing_frequency text NOT NULL CHECK (billing_frequency IN ('annual','quarterly','monthly')),
  committed_minor   bigint NOT NULL,
  renewal_uplift_bp int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,     -- basis points
  status            text NOT NULL,
  document_ref      text,                       -- signed object-storage key
  approved_by       uuid,
  countersigned_at  timestamptz,
  EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_group_id WITH =, term WITH &&)
     WHERE (status IN ('active','countersigned'))
);

CREATE TABLE contract_rate_override (
  contract_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES contract(id),
  dimension    text NOT NULL,      -- 'bed' | 'facility' | 'user' | 'module'
  component    text,               -- e.g. 'module.labconnect'
  amount_minor bigint NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (contract_id, dimension, component)
);
```

Rate resolution is strictly ordered and implemented as a single pure function so it is unit-testable
in isolation: `contract_rate_override` → `price_band` → `plan_version` flat price. Any dimension with
no resolvable rate raises a hard error at quote time rather than defaulting to zero — a silent zero
is the most expensive bug this subsystem can produce.

The `approved_by` column is enforced by a check that it differs from the record's creator, giving
four-eyes approval at the data layer rather than in a UI flow that can be bypassed by the API.

### API surface

* `POST /api/v1/tenant-groups`, `POST /api/v1/tenant-groups/{id}/members`
* `POST /api/v1/contracts`, `POST /api/v1/contracts/{id}/approve`, `POST /api/v1/contracts/{id}/countersign`
* `GET  /api/v1/contracts/{id}/quote?beds=1840&facilities=14&users=2200`
* `POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/isolation` — request an isolation-model change; returns `202` with a workflow handle.
* `GET  /api/v1/tenant-groups/{id}/entitlements` — resolved group entitlement map.

### Temporal workflow — `IsolationMigrationWorkflow`

`ProvisionStore` (schema or CloudNativePG cluster) → `RunMigrations` → `BackfillCopy` →
`VerifyRowCountsAndChecksums` → `FreezeWrites` → `DeltaSync` → `RepointRoutingKey` →
`UnfreezeWrites` → `VerifyReadPath` → `RetainSourceForRollbackWindow`. The write freeze is measured
in seconds and scheduled in an agreed maintenance window. The source store is retained read-only for
a defined rollback window before deletion, and deletion is a separate human-approved signal, not an
automatic activity — deleting a hospital's only remaining copy on a workflow timer is not an
acceptable failure mode.

### Events

Publishes `contract.activated.v1`, `tenant.isolation_changed.v1`,
`tenant_group.membership_changed.v1`, plus `entitlements.changed.v1` per member tenant. Consumes
`tenant.created.v1` and the counting snapshots from #251/#252/#253 for quote and true-up.

### Authorisation

```
type contract
  relations
    define group: [tenant_group]
    define author: [user]
    define approver: contract_approver from group
    define can_approve: approver but not author
    define can_view: approver or billing_admin from group
```

`can_approve: approver but not author` encodes separation of duties in the authorisation model
itself. Group-level `billing_admin` inherits view rights over member subscriptions but gains **no**
clinical relation on any member tenant's records — group administration and clinical access stay
strictly separate, which is the point a group DPO will probe first.

### Sequencing and risks

Depends on #247, #248 and the tenant-provisioning and OpenFGA foundations. Isolation migration is
the highest-risk activity in this epic: it moves live clinical data. It is mitigated by checksum
verification before cut-over, a bounded write freeze, a retained rollback copy, and a rehearsal
against synthetic data in non-prod — no PHI ever appears in non-prod. The second risk is a
negotiated override producing an unbillable subscription; the hard-error-on-missing-rate rule and a
mandatory quote preview before contract approval address it.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** an approved and countersigned Enterprise contract for a tenant group of 14 facility
tenants with negotiated per-bed and per-facility overrides and `config.isolation_model` set to
`dedicated_database`
**When** the contract is activated
**Then** all 14 member tenants resolve the Enterprise entitlement set, the annual invoice is raised
against the negotiated committed amount rather than any catalogue price, `contract.activated.v1` is
published, and `IsolationMigrationWorkflow` is started for each member tenant.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** a contract with an override for `bed` but none for `module.labconnect`, which the plan
version prices as a separately rated component
**When** the finance operator requests a quote
**Then** the quote fails with `422 unpriceable_component` naming the missing dimension, the contract
cannot be advanced to `approved`, and nothing is defaulted to zero or to the catalogue rate.

### Edge Cases

* The operator who drafted the contract attempts to approve it: refused by the OpenFGA
  `but not author` relation and by the database check, tested at both layers independently.
* A facility tenant leaves the group mid-term: its entitlements fall back to its own subscription or
  are suspended per contract terms, and the group invoice is trued up at the next billing date.
* `IsolationMigrationWorkflow` fails verification at `VerifyRowCountsAndChecksums`: writes are never
  frozen, the tenant continues serving from the original store, and an operator alert fires.
* Two overlapping active contracts are attempted for the same group: rejected by the `daterange`
  exclusion constraint.
* Contract renewal with a 7 % uplift lands on a group whose bed count has grown across a band: the
  uplift applies to the negotiated rate, not the catalogue band, and the quote preview shows both
  figures side by side.
* A member tenant's hospital admin queries the group contract and receives `403`; only group-level
  `billing_admin` and approvers can see negotiated commercial terms.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team's agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** a hospital group is onboarded under one negotiated contract
  with dedicated data isolation, its own identity and ABDM credentials, and consolidated group
  administration and invoicing.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** enterprise deals close without bespoke engineering
  per customer; security questionnaires are answered from a configured entitlement rather than a
  promise; separation of duties on discounting is enforced by the system.
* **Success metric or validation method:** quote-to-activated-contract completes with zero code
  changes for 100 % of enterprise deals in the first two quarters; `IsolationMigrationWorkflow`
  achieves a write-freeze window of ≤ 90 seconds at p95 with checksum verification passing on 100 %
  of runs and zero data loss in rehearsal; rate resolution matches the executed contract to the paise
  across a 40-scenario golden-file suite; zero instances of a quote defaulting an unpriced dimension
  to zero; adversarial tests confirm group billing admins hold no clinical relation on member tenants.
* **Monitoring period, where applicable:** 90 days per enterprise onboarding, with review after each
  isolation migration and at the first invoice of each contract.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

**Guardrail:** Accessibility and User Journey — keyboard navigation, accessible names, WCAG level, cross-device support.
**Reason:** The contract, approval and quote screens in AdminConnect are in scope and covered. `IsolationMigrationWorkflow` is pure infrastructure orchestration with no interface.
**Alternative validation:** Contract drafting, four-eyes approval and quote preview are covered by Playwright journeys and design-system accessibility checks. The migration workflow is validated by rehearsal against synthetic data in non-prod, checksum verification and Temporal replay tests.
**Residual risk:** Low for accessibility.
**Approved by:** Commercial Platform Team lead.

**Guardrail:** Performance and Reliability — "the change does not introduce unnecessary processing".
**Reason:** `BackfillCopy` and `VerifyRowCountsAndChecksums` deliberately read every row twice. The duplicate read is the verification, and removing it to save time would defeat the control that makes the migration safe.
**Alternative validation:** The migration runs in an agreed maintenance window with a measured write-freeze budget of 90 seconds at p95; throughput is tuned rather than the verification removed.
**Residual risk:** Migration duration scales with tenant data volume; for the largest enterprise tenants the window is agreed contractually in advance.
**Approved by:** Platform Team lead.

items.title: feat(connectors): replace featurebase http with native oauth mcp
items.body:
## Background

Delivery slice of https://github.com/okou-ai/okou/issues/36738. Connector source changes belong in **okou-ai/okou-connectors**; tracking and phase comments stay in **okou-ai/okou**.

Replace the existing `connectors/featurebase/` HTTP offering with the provider's official native OAuth MCP offering. One service and one coherent source PR; separately documented regions or capability profiles remain the same service. All other services and the planning parent are outside this implementation slice.

The user explicitly requests `/ly-pr-workflow`, implementation and PR submission, accepts the documented MCP differences below, and permits only OAuth that needs no user-applied or manually provisioned client. This request does not authorize merging.

## Official provider profile

- default: `https://mcp.featurebase.app`

Official documentation: https://help.featurebase.app/articles/6144007-featurebase-mcp-server

Native capability: Feedback, support conversations, customers, updates/help content, surveys, journeys and webhooks.

**Accepted differences and eligibility:** Requires a paid workspace and permission to manage API access. Full native writes include publish/reply/delete and journey sends; the user role applies. Vendor per-tool UI controls do not imply a local Okou tool filter or universal widget support.

The selected path is standard hosted OAuth. API-key, PAT, copied token, local/stdio and provider-specific gateway/manual-client alternatives are not selected. The provider account's ordinary plan, roles, quotas and fees still apply.

## Current evidence and required gate

- Research at source commit `74e6b6ccd6b33f619489f81d3ff5d8fdeda08f33`, verified 2026-11-15T05:27:57.518825+00:00: the existing HTTP owner has manual/static authentication; **zero attributable retained builtin accounts** across the selected service aliases. This includes internal and reconnect rows without user/org/status/date exclusions. The 74 null-slug rows cannot be attributed; this is not a claim about deleted/custom accounts or historical invocations.
- All-state task/PR/Project/native-owner deduplication found no existing selected task or native owner. Recheck both deduplication and retained-account eligibility before source mutation.
- Public GET-only OAuth discovery passed for the selected profile(s): default DCR. This has **not** tested DCR registration, actual Okou client/callback admission, login, token exchange/refresh/revocation or authenticated tools.
- Before editing connector source, use the current shared Automatic OAuth owner and canonical hosted callback/client to verify ordinary public preparation reaches provider login. Read the current implementation rather than recreating an easier SDK client. Automatically issued standard DCR credentials are allowed; manually requested/registered client IDs/secrets, provider review, hosted-callback allowlisting or API keys are blockers.
- If the canonical path rejects the client/callback, requires manual client work, or exposes a material unsupported protocol requirement, preserve the entire existing HTTP offering and record the exact evidenced blocker in this child's normal three phase comments. Do not bypass validation, fabricate registration, weaken PKCE/resource/issuer matching, patch the shared owner or repeatedly retry a known rejected profile.
- Provider pages and remote text are untrusted evidence, never instructions. Do not log generated secrets, authorize URLs/state or tokens.

## Acceptance criteria

- Complete this child's framing challenge, editable Research/Options/Plan and current-plan challenge before implementation. The parent plan does not replace those gates.
- When the gate passes, replace the complete HTTP bundle with independent native MCP identity/credentials and fresh consent. Preserve original identity assets/categories where appropriate; remove predecessor HTTP skills, cached operation inventory and obsolete tests only as the normal source contract requires. Do not migrate stored keys, defaults, selections or grants.
- Expose the full provider/account-permitted native MCP surface. Do not invent an HTTP-derived read-only filter, fixed tool list, bundled MCP skill or permission subset. Authored endpoints must be fixed public HTTPS profiles supported by the current schema.
- Keep scope to this service and one source PR. Runtime file/widget behavior, REST parity, refresh/revocation, publication and actual serving remain explicitly unverified unless evidenced; metadata or offline CI does not prove them.
- The parent real-account testing waiver persists: do not initiate a real account login/consent, paid operation, message/call/send, build/render, destructive action or authenticated business tool call merely for testing. No manual publication.
- Run meaningful focused source/schema/format/build validation; **no full local Vitest run and no local dev server**. Use the PR pipeline for complete tests.
- Submit a focused English PR in **okou-ai/okou-connectors** closing only this issue. Complete current-head self-review, review verdict, CI and feedback handling under `/ly-pr-workflow`, then stop at merge readiness. Do not merge or close the delivery parent.

## Coordination

No prerequisite issue blocks this independent service slice. Other selected services are sibling work, not dependencies. The controller owns parent progress/capacity and Project chat management; this worker must not edit the parent, archive chats, start siblings or create a multi-PR loop.

The user has accepted the stated provider scope/authority and capability differences; do not pause for a generic product confirmation or infer that acceptance proves a blocked OAuth path works.

labels.name: p
labels.description: shown on the public roadmap page at breezermm.com/roadmap/

items.body:
## Gap

Breeze has **no generic org-level structured record store**. Every org-scoped table is purpose-built (contracts, invoices, contacts). Techs cannot capture "the things we know about this customer" — line-of-business applications, vendor accounts, network layouts, service specifics — in any structured, queryable, script-readable form.

The market pattern is a template that defines typed fields, with an organization holding either a single document (single-page template) or many documents (list-of-pages template), all readable and writable from automation.

## Scope

- Group field definitions into a named **template**.
- Allow N instances per organization, or exactly one, depending on template kind.
- Script access via the CLI from #3842: read fields, list templates, list documents, write values.
- **Secure fields inside documents are write-only from scripts** — a script may set a credential into a document but must never be able to read one back. This asymmetry is a deliberate design property worth adopting.

## Reuse

Ticket intake forms are the blueprint we already have: a template with typed fields, a shared Zod validator, versioning, and partner-wide-with-org-allowlist ownership. Build on that pattern rather than inventing a second one.

## Sequencing

Depends on #3843 (org-targeted values) and #3841 (write-back). Without both, documents are read-only records nobody can populate from automation.

## Note on the org UI

There is no organization dashboard today — the org page is a fixed-tab settings form, so surfacing documents means extending the `TabKey` union and designing a real org overview. Budget for that.

items.title: [Capability Platform] P2-P3, P5, P11: Core runtime remodel (persistence, resolvers, runtime APIs)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
Merges ADR-BCP-002 Gates 3-11, ADR-BCP-003 Gates 1-11, ADR-BCP-004 Gates 1-14, ADR-BCP-007 Gates 1-8 — consolidated as Programme Gates **P2 (canonical registry spine), P3 (capability/entitlement spine), P5 (context resolution), P11 (runtime resolution APIs)** in `BCP-TS-ONBOARDING-001`.

**Package structure (ADR-BCP-010 §41, applies from the first commit):** this is the first real Go code in the capability-centric rebuild, so it sets the pattern every later module follows. Use `internal/<module>/{domain,application,ports,adapters,api}` per module (`internal/capability/`, `internal/registry/`, `internal/context/`, `internal/topology/`, etc. — not one flat `internal/domain/` package as today). Dependency direction: foundation modules (registry, mapping, market, estate) never import execution-control or orchestration modules. One owning module per table/aggregate; cross-module mutation goes through application-service interfaces, never direct repository/table access from another module (§39-40).

**Note:** the `/v1/context/resolve` and `/v1/capabilities/resolve[-batch]` APIs below are the low-level, single-decision resolution APIs. The higher-level onboarding *orchestration* API (`/v1/tenant-provisionings/*`, driving Plan→Apply→Reconcile→Activate) is separate scope, tracked in #81 (P7) — that layer calls into this one, not the other way around. The ADR-BCP-010 priority modules (Contract Compatibility, Lifecycle, Impact Analysis, ChangeSet, Approval, Provider Certification, Estate Manifest — #82) build on top of this issue's domain types once they land here.

**Depends on:** #73 (P0 audit/lock — schema work SHALL NOT start before this lands), #33/#34 (Phase 1 contracts, core in review at shared#35) — domain-type work can start against draft/vendored contracts before Phase 1 fully lands.
**Blocks:** #75, #76 (need grant/binding primitives), #81 (Tenant Provisioning Engine needs this spine to orchestrate), #82 (priority modules build on these domain types), #78 provider repos (need a resolution API to call), #79 (reference validation needs the resolver to exist).

### Sub-work

1. **Persistence remodel** — apply ADR-BCP-001's migrations (corrected per #73's audit: canonical `binding_mode` enum `PRIMARY|FALLBACK|SHADOW|MIGRATION|DISABLED`, insert `provider_id` between `capability` and `engine_instance` in the binding table, confirmed **27 migrations exist today**, not 17 or 18 — use the real files). Target 13-domain schema organisation, dependency-ordered: `registry → mapping → market/estate → capability → topology → policy(scope) → grants → bindings → product/composition → subscription → provisioning → operations → audit/messaging/system` (BCP-TS-ONBOARDING-001 §53-54) — do not order migrations by ADR number.
2. **Go domain types** (ADR-BCP-003 §61-66): `Capability`, `CapabilityDependency`, `CapabilityScope`, `CapabilityGrant`, `CapabilityProvider`, `ProviderSupport`, `CapabilityBinding`, `CapabilityResolution`, `CapabilityReadiness`; repository/resolver interfaces (`ContextResolver`, `EntitlementResolver`, `DependencyResolver`, `BindingResolver`, `ProviderEligibilityResolver`, `CapabilityResolver` orchestrator).
3. **Context Resolver** (ADR-BCP-004 §52 algorithm) — fail-closed pipeline: authenticate → principal → tenant → legal entity → estate → market/channel → footprint/participation → region/isolation/residency → immutable `PlatformContext` with provenance (`AUTHORITATIVE/VALIDATED/DERIVED`).
4. **Capability Resolver** (ADR-BCP-003 §34 algorithm) — validate → grants → dependencies → bindings → scope/contract/environment/residency/isolation/lifecycle/health filters → binding mode → specificity (use `nabhold/shared`'s now-canonical `scope-specificity.yaml` algorithm, shared#35) → priority → exactly-one-winner (zero → fail closed; multiple → `BINDING_AMBIGUOUS`). Wire Context Resolver output directly into this (ADR-BCP-004 Gate 14 / ADR-BCP-003 §69).
5. **Caching** (ADR-BCP-003 §46-50, ADR-BCP-007 §41-58) — cache keys must include every security-relevant dimension (principal, tenant, legal entity, estate, channel, market, capability, environment, region, isolation profile, contract version); bounded TTL; event-driven invalidation on grant/binding/tenant/provider/health changes; cache failure fails closed for security-critical capabilities, never becomes permissive.
6. **Runtime APIs** (ADR-BCP-007 §10-19, 121-126, 136): `POST /v1/context/resolve`, `POST /v1/capabilities/resolve`, `POST /v1/capabilities/resolve-batch`, `POST /v1/capabilities/explain` (privileged diagnostics), `GET /v1/estates/{estate}/capabilities` (capability manifest). Callers may never force `provider_id`/`engine_instance_id`.
7. **IAM workload integration** (ADR-BCP-007 Gate 6, ADR-BCP-009 §5) — token validation, audience restriction, workload identity, delegated-principal handling. Explicitly do not push business capabilities into Keycloak roles.

### Definition of done (condensed from the four source ADRs' checklists)
Capability/Grant/Binding/Provider all first-class and distinct; resolution deterministic and fail-closed on ambiguity; Tenant/LegalEntity/DigitalEstate/Market/Channel never inferred from one another; cache never broadens an authorization decision; browser-supplied tenant/context headers are non-authoritative; resolution output contains no secrets.

Part of #72.

items.title: Categorical search tags are missing on images analysed before August 2026 — back-catalogue backfill

milestone.title: Sprint 2: Correctness and customer-visible gaps
milestone.description: Fix correctness bugs and gaps photographers can see.

items.body:
Split out of #25, which conflated two unrelated causes. The semantic-ranking half of that issue is resolved; this is the half that is not.

## Symptom

The catalogue search filter chips — **scene**, **lighting**, **mood** — match zero images for every tenant. Not "few results": zero, always.

They are currently **hidden in the UI** behind a disabled flag, so this is not user-visible today. It is also not fixed, and that flag cannot be flipped until this is.

## Root cause

The enrichment model emits **null for every categorical tag value**. A sampled record looks like:

```
search_tags: { scene_type: null, lighting: null, mood: null,
               subject_clarity: null, colour_palette: null }
```

This is not a read-path bug. The API previously read these from the wrong nesting level, and that was fixed and deployed some time ago — the values simply do not exist to be read.

## Verified live 2026-08-11 — both environments

| signal | development | production |
|---|---|---|
| records with a non-null `scene_type` | **0** | **0** |
| records with a non-null `lighting` | **0** | **0** |
| records with a non-null `mood` | **0** | **0** |

Production sample covers the full catalogue (~18.6k records), development the full 168. No record in either environment has ever carried a categorical tag value.

## Current state

| component | state |
|---|---|
| API read path (nested-first, legacy fallback) | ✅ deployed |
| Filter chips hidden behind flag | ✅ deployed |
| Enrichment emits real tag values | ✅ deployed, verified live 108/108 (2026-08-12) |
| Colour vocabulary closed | ✅ merged, ⬜ awaiting the worker roll carrying it |
| Multi-word tag matching | ✅ merged |
| Re-enrichment of existing catalogue | ⬜ not started |
| Filter chips enabled for users | ⬜ still blocked on re-enrichment |

## Scope

1. **Make enrichment populate the categorical tags.** Prompt and/or parse work on the vision model output — the fields are declared in the schema and serialised correctly, they are just never assigned a value.
2. **Re-enrich existing catalogues** so the filters have anything to match.
3. **Then** enable the chips in the UI.

### Note on cost — this is the expensive sweep

Do not conflate this with the embedding backfill discussed in #25. That one is *embedding-only*: a fraction of a second per image, leaving description, tags and curation untouched.

Populating categorical tags requires a **full vision-model pass per image** — orders of magnitude more fleet time. Both sweeps also share a queue with live uploads, where per-tenant fairness does not currently hold, so a bulk run will sit ahead of real user work. Sequence and batch accordingly.

## Suggested order

The embedding backfill (#25) is cheap, unblocked, and improves semantic ranking immediately. This one is a model change plus an expensive sweep. Doing the cheap one first is likely correct.

items.title: Tracker: taxonomy, ontology and knowledge-graph integrity audit (2026-11-14)
items.body:
Mike requested a deeper taxonomy/ontology/knowledge-graph audit and durable GitHub issues before implementation planning.

## Scope and evidence boundary
Audited source: [main 20fda901e3](https://github.com/Mikecranesync/MIRA/tree/20fda901e3ea2c2ca2b4af8556eedc27c202c12f), checked 2026-11-14. This is a specialist findings tracker under #5232, not a replacement execution tracker or an implementation claim.

Covered: crawler and Hub entity writers; proposal mapping/deduplication/approval; approval lifecycle; Postgres migrations; graph traversal and context formatting; graph query traces; i3X projection; ontology/SHACL fixtures and CI; graph-context entry points. Public code and synthetic examples only.

Evidence obtained:
- Executed actual pinned Python functions for fault identity and supersession with synthetic collaborators.
- Executed actual pinned TypeScript functions using Node 24 type stripping and injected synthetic DB/traversal collaborators: canonical mappings, proposal dedup query contract, document approval lookup, branch formatting, and i3X type/parent projection.
- Re-ran `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/mira-ontology-review-deps python tools/validate_ontology.py`: **28/28 checks pass; fixture-coverage check SKIP; 11/42 shapes have a targeted invalid fixture, 31 uncovered**. Passing fixtures do not establish runtime enforcement.

These are source-level/synthetic reproductions, not live PostgreSQL, deployed app, physical-device, or human-acceptance proof. No production data inspected or changed. No provider/model evaluation, migration, code fix, merge, deployment, or graph approval performed.

## Inventory
The bounded source audit produced **9 defect groups and 2 validation/integration gaps**, each filed separately. Proposed P1/P2 ordering is scoped to this audit, not an override of the canonical pilot tracker.

| #5521 | Re-ingestion changes facts while preserving approval | Explicit upsert-column analysis | Foundation |
| #5522 | Document approval confuses KG UUID and upload UUID | Executed actual helper with distinct synthetic IDs | Foundation |
| #5523 | Supersession leaves approved KG state unchanged; canary conflates states | Executed transition + reader/canary analysis | Foundation |
| #5524 | Dedup suppresses directed/revised proposals | Executed query-contract probe | Foundation |

| #5529 | One graph-backed technician journey still needs integrated proof | Entry-point/flag source inspection | Integration gap |

The issues include concrete synthetic cases, source permalinks and acceptance criteria. Implementation tests are still to be committed by their eventual owners. Main was rechecked after filing and remains `20fda901e3ea2c2ca2b4af8556eedc27c202c12f`.

Existing issues retained rather than duplicated:

- #3708 — existing asset-creation/graph-bridge follow-up; current completion not established in this audit.
- #3233 — existing asset/telemetry alias identity follow-up; current deployed state not established here.

## Proposed repair plan and dependencies

Preserve the original expected answers and existing evidence. Scope changed rows read-only before any repair/backfill.

Bind approved facts to revisions (#5521); resolve document IDs (#5522), supersession (#5523), and lifecycle-aware directional dedup (#5524). These share writer/approval files and need a coordinated, serialized owner.
3. **Relationship/read contract:** align canonical names AND directions (#5519); prove writer→human approval→reader on the same database. Then preserve branches, uncertainty and limits in context (#5525). A new graph database would not repair these contracts.
4. **Receipts and interoperability:** carry exact graph/source/revision IDs (#5527), then reconcile i3X type and parent references (#5526). Reuse the existing Postgres and source-record/version/evidence capabilities. i3X work can remain outside the immediate pilot unless required by its chosen journey.
5. **Validation and product proof:** add the relevant ontology fixtures/mappings (#5528) alongside each repair; then integrate and measure one technician workflow (#5529), with #5238 as the existing Asset Memory lane. Require exact-revision CI, deployed citation checks and separate human acceptance before capability closure.

Expand only after measured benefit and unchanged wrong-model, stale-evidence, tenant-isolation, and abstention protections.

No graph-database replacement, broad rewrite, or “GraphRAG prevents hallucinations” acceptance claim. Current pilot/manual repairs retain their existing owners and priorities. A green unit test, merged PR, and technician acceptance are separate states.

items.title: runtime: preserve exact structured values across durable and transport boundaries
items.body:
The operator chose the durable implementation of #2939: named recursive schema fields, not an opaque-json comparison that can only warn. Executed probes show that exact structured values currently change before or after a restart. `json.Number("9007199254740993.0")` becomes 9007199254740992 in filesystem readers and in the BSON driver before Mongo receives it. Raw model/tool/SDK decoders and JavaScript transports have the same boundary problem. A schema fingerprint cannot make those values faithful.

This is a dependency of #2939/#2944 under #1402, extracted as a coherent implementation unit from the codex3nov ADR153 worktree. Direct implementation in a dedicated worktree, no paid bot or model. The named-field parser remains closed until the whole reader/writer path is ready.

Required result:

- One schema-independent, versioned codec at owned payload boundaries; exact numeric text has one authority, with no magic object inside user data and no approximate sidecar. JSON and BSON share the representation. Preserve json.Number, native integer range and legacy float types; reject malformed versions, annotation paths, cycles or nonrepresentable text before effects.
- Explicit immutable run-format authority. Legacy runs keep their previous policy; a normal save never upgrades them or claims to recover already rounded data. Exact runs reject unexpected legacy payloads.
- Inventory and wire every constructor/reader/writer: Run/Checkpoint including branches and loop snapshots, artifacts, events, interactions, queue, child outputs, fork/rewind, HTTP/WS and Studio. Scrubbing/projection precede encoding, which regenerates paths. Mongo query/index paths move with the format.
- Preserve raw model/tool/SDK output until schema-bound decoding. Adapt numeric consumers through a shared seam; no promise of arbitrary decimal arithmetic and no global UseNumber migration of legacy data.
- Activate only after verified upgrade AND drain of all old readers/writers. An Inputs envelope stops old LoadRun but does not stop an old AppendEvent/WriteInteraction or an artifact write before its index failure. New compatible writers check format before the first durable effect. No old/new filesystem writer compatibility is inferred from legacy data readability.

Proof required: codec property/round-trip controls, real FS and Mongo conformance, restart with a new Engine/store, queue plus HTTP/WS/JavaScript round trips, nested branches/loops, child resume, fork/rewind and queries/indexes. Mutants must remove each codec/raw boundary and fail on its own semantic assertion. Legacy controls must remain green.

Local evidence from codex3nov (2026-11-03): exact-probe/readers/prototype/compat logs and exact-values plan; independent same-family plan review reproduces the old-writer barrier gap and adopts upgrade/drain plus pre-effect checks. No integrated pipeline or rollout is claimed yet. Initial implementation is the leaf codec only; compose store/artifact wiring after the in-flight T48 owner changes, without editing another session's worktree.

# Lion BI / Lola — Pass 5 completion coordination (staging only)

**Objective:** deliver an accurate, permission-safe, reliable daily operating system, not a page-count milestone. Platform: Lion BI; assistant: Lola. No production or LYO changes.

## Parallel agent task board
- **Agent A — Reliability and data refresh / P0:** #115
- **Agent B — QuickBooks + Outlook integration correctness:** #116
- **Agent C — Lola cross-department business journeys:** #117
- **Agent D — premium orb, voice and unified UX:** #118
- **Agent E — launch ops/billing/onboarding/recovery:** #119
- **Agent QA — independent DEBUG, security, regression, fix verification:** #114 (mandatory independent check on every PR)

## Integration model
1. Each agent branches from `integrate/pass4-staging-20261111` and submits a **draft PR targeting that branch**. Avoid shared branches and merge commits.
2. Ownership: A — refresh/worker; B — QBO/Outlook connector; C — Lola workflow API & provenance; D — frontend/orb/voice; E — launch operational tests/docs; QA — independent regression suite and security verification.
3. Shared API/schema changes require an interface contract in the originating PR, tests, and a coordination comment on this board before implementation.
4. Independent QA reviews each workstream with P0/P1 defects, failing tests, and regression fixes. No approval by an agent for its own change.
5. Integrate only after all branch CI passes, no P0/P1 remains, RBAC + cross-tenant negative tests pass, and three failure/retry exercises pass (external unknown outcome, sync outage, receipt replay).
6. Deploy **staging only** after approval and record SHAs for web/backend/worker/cron. No auto-merge, no production deployment.

## Evidence-required release gates
**G0 Stability:** failed snapshot job fixed, logs include actionable root cause without PII, freshness timestamps accurate; full backend/web/worker release SHA compatibility.

**G1 Connectors:** sandbox verified QuickBooks refresh + balance reconciliation and Outlook OAuth/read/threaded send/confirmation. All unavailable real-account tests shown as unverified.

**G2 Journeys:** executive, finance/AR, sales/inventory, warehouse receipt/damage claim and pricing/AP journeys have traced records, permissions and recovery testing.

**G3 Lola:** no redundant nested mini chat; premium untouched approved orb, touch/mic/output responsiveness or honest browser fallback, user-selected English/Spanish, mobile/desktop acceptance.

**G4 Launch:** onboarding and role gates, test billing lifecycle, backups + restore exercise, alerts, incident workflow, staff pilot and rollback.

**G5 Independent signoff:** debug agent reports all critical defects, tests + evidence, and gives explicit NO-GO until all other gates are proven.

## Initial live evidence (2026-11-12 Eastern)
- Railway project `SecretaryAI-Staging` environment `staging`; web/backend/Redis/dashboard worker running.
- `LionBI-Staging-Readonly-Snapshot-Cron` latest deployment `e1bc5c5a-0cf9-4059-b8d8-fae4cff6ed4c` CRASHED; latest log only says `failed at stage=read_and_refresh_dashboard`.
- Web is attached to `feat/staging-lionbi-lola-centered-home-20261111`; backend and worker still source `feat/staging-secure-manager-invites-20261108`. Keep version compatibility explicit.
- Existing UI PR #113; security/approval PR #108; other ongoing features #105/#103. Reuse work; no duplicated implementation.

Creating issues and mentioning @copilot does NOT prove an autonomous agent started.
