items.title: [Bug]: list_databases OpenAPI response references collection Vec schema
items.body:
### What happened?

The OpenAPI document served by `/openapi.json` describes the successful response for:

`GET /api/v2/tenants/{tenant}/databases`

as:

```json
{
  "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Vec"
}
```

However, that `Vec` component contains the **collection** shape (`configuration_json`, `database`, `log_position`, `version`, etc.). The endpoint actually returns database objects such as:

```json
[
  {
    "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
    "name": "default_database",
    "tenant": "default_tenant"
  }
]
```

This breaks generated clients that correctly follow the published schema. For example, a generated .NET client deserializes the response as a collection model and fails because `configuration_json`, `database`, `log_position`, and `version` are absent.

The expected 200 response schema is:

```json
{
  "type": "array",
  "items": {
    "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Database"
  }
}
```

Likely source of the collision:

- The route annotation uses `body = ListDatabasesResponse`: https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma/blob/93652ec0869489b803fe1682427fc02bd47bec14/rust/frontend/src/server.rs#L837-L869
- `ListDatabasesResponse` is `Vec<Database>`: https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma/blob/93652ec0869489b803fe1682427fc02bd47bec14/rust/types/src/api_types.rs#L492
- `ListCollectionsResponse` is separately `Vec<Collection>`: https://github.com/chroma-core/chroma/blob/93652ec0869489b803fe1682427fc02bd47bec14/rust/types/src/api_types.rs#L646

It appears these aliases are both represented as a shared OpenAPI component named `Vec`, with the collection item schema winning. An explicit array response schema (for example, an inline `[Database]` response in the utoipa annotation) or uniquely named response wrapper should avoid the collision.

Downstream reproduction and workaround: https://github.com/tryAGI/Chroma/issues/144

The downstream generation pipeline temporarily rewrites only this response to `array<Database>`; after regeneration, the exact call against `chromadb/chroma:latest` returns `default_database`, and the full integration suite plus trimming checks pass.

### Versions

- OpenAPI `info.version`: `1.0.0`
- OpenAPI version: `3.1.0`
- Source snapshot inspected: `93652ec0869489b803fe1682427fc02bd47bec14`
- Runtime reproduction: current `chromadb/chroma:latest` container on 2026-08-26
- Client consumer: `tryAGI.Chroma` (`System.Text.Json`)

### Relevant log output

```shell
System.Text.Json.JsonException: JSON deserialization for type Chroma.VecItem was missing required properties including: configuration_json; database; log_position; version.
```

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

AdminConnect has no commercial packaging layer. Tenants can be created, but there is nothing that
describes what a tenant has bought, and therefore nothing that decides whether a given module,
facility or seat may be used. Every product team is currently one feature flag away from inventing
its own private entitlement check, which is exactly how a platform ends up with eleven different
answers to "is LabConnect switched on for this hospital?".

The Clinic plan is the entry-level commercial package and the first plan the platform will sell:
a single-facility, single-location practice — a small polyclinic or standalone OPD clinic with a
handful of doctors, a front-desk registrar and an in-house dispensary. It is the volume tier and
the acquisition funnel for everything above it, so it must be self-serve: a clinic owner signs up,
picks Clinic, pays by UPI AutoPay, and is productive without a solution consultant.

Because this is the first plan, it carries the design of the **plan catalogue itself** — plan
versions, entitlements, limits and price books — which issues #248 to #254 extend rather than
redesign. Getting the versioning right now matters: a plan's commercial terms change several times
a year, and a subscription signed in March must keep its March terms until it is explicitly
migrated. Retro-actively mutating a live plan would corrupt invoices already issued and filed
under GST e-invoicing.

Affected roles: the clinic owner/hospital admin who buys and manages the subscription, the finance
operator in AdminConnect who maintains price books, and every product service that must ask
"is this entitled?" before rendering a module.

Billing metadata sits in the shared global control plane. It must contain **no PHI** — plan,
entitlement, counts and money only — so the country data-residency boundary is preserved.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** clinic owner onboarding a single-location practice
**I want** to subscribe to a packaged Clinic plan with clearly stated module entitlements and limits
**So that** my clinic is provisioned with exactly the capabilities I paid for, and every service on
the platform resolves my entitlements from one authoritative source.

### Scope

**In scope**

* Plan catalogue data model: immutable, versioned `plan_version` records with an effective-from
  date; a plan version already referenced by an active subscription can never be edited.
* Definition and seeding of the Clinic plan version 1: entitled modules (MediCore OPD, registration,
  appointments, DoctorConnect charting and e-prescribing, PharmaConnect dispensing, MediConnect
  patient app, ABDM ABHA linking and HIP publication), and its hard limits (1 facility, seat cap,
  no IPD/ward/OT, no LabConnect analyser integration, shared-schema RLS tenancy only).
* Entitlement resolution service and Go SDK: `HasEntitlement(ctx, tenantID, key)` and
  `CheckLimit(ctx, tenantID, key, requested)`, Redis-cached, invalidated by event.
* Subscription lifecycle for Clinic: trial → active → past-due → suspended → cancelled, driven by a
  Temporal workflow, with UPI AutoPay mandate as the default payment instrument.
* Publication of `SubscriptionActivated`, `SubscriptionPlanChanged` and `EntitlementsChanged`
  domain events on NATS JetStream so consuming products refresh without polling.
* Limit-exceeded behaviour: reads stay available, the offending write is refused with a structured
  upgrade prompt. Clinical records are never hidden because of a commercial state.
* Rate limits and resource quotas for the tier fed from the plan version, so a Clinic tenant cannot
  degrade a Hospital tenant.

**Out of scope**

* Per-user, per-bed, per-facility and module add-on rating mechanics — owned by #252, #253, #251
  and #254 respectively. This story consumes those dimensions through the price-book interface but
  implements only a flat monthly Clinic price.
* Upgrade path from Clinic to Hospital, including data and tenancy migration — owned by #248.
* GST e-invoice generation and IRN registration — owned by the Subscription invoicing story in this
  epic.
* Discount codes, promotional pricing and channel-partner margins — owned by the Discounts story.
* Dunning email and WhatsApp template content — owned by the Renewal management story; this story
  only emits the state transitions those templates react to.

---

## Recommended Solution

Implement in `adminconnect/billing` as a Go/Gin module with GORM, deployed in the control plane,
backed by its own PostgreSQL 16 database. Tenant scoping goes through the standard tenant-scoped
data-access layer with RLS so no query can omit `tenant_id`.

### Data model

```sql
CREATE TABLE plan (
  id            uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  code          text NOT NULL UNIQUE,          -- 'clinic'
  country_code  text NOT NULL,                 -- country profile, never hard-coded logic
  segment       text NOT NULL                  -- clinic | hospital | enterprise | government
);

CREATE TABLE plan_version (
  id             uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  plan_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES plan(id),
  version        int  NOT NULL,
  effective_from date NOT NULL,
  retired_at     date,
  status         text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('draft','published','retired')),
  UNIQUE (plan_id, version)
);

CREATE TABLE plan_entitlement (
  plan_version_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES plan_version(id),
  key             text NOT NULL,               -- 'module.labconnect', 'limit.facilities'
  kind            text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('boolean','limit','config')),
  bool_value      boolean,
  limit_value     bigint,
  config_value    jsonb,
  PRIMARY KEY (plan_version_id, key)
);

CREATE TABLE subscription (
  id               uuid PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id        uuid NOT NULL,
  plan_version_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES plan_version(id),
  status           text NOT NULL,
  trial_ends_on    date,
  current_period   daterange NOT NULL,
  currency         char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'INR',
  EXCLUDE USING gist (tenant_id WITH =, current_period WITH &&)
     WHERE (status IN ('trialing','active','past_due'))
);
```

The exclusion constraint is the important one: it makes overlapping active subscriptions for a
tenant structurally impossible rather than a race the application hopes to win.

A database trigger rejects `UPDATE` on `plan_version` and `plan_entitlement` rows whose status is
`published`. Commercial changes create a new version; existing subscriptions stay pinned.

### API surface

* `GET  /api/v1/plans?country=IN&segment=clinic` — published plan versions for the storefront.
* `POST /api/v1/subscriptions` — subscribe a tenant to a plan version (idempotency key required).
* `GET  /api/v1/subscriptions/{id}` — current state, period, entitlements snapshot.
* `POST /api/v1/subscriptions/{id}/cancel` — schedules cancellation at period end.
* `GET  /api/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/entitlements` — resolved map, ETag-cacheable.
* `POST /internal/v1/entitlements/check` — batch check used by the Go SDK.
* Admin-only: `POST /api/v1/plan-versions`, `POST /api/v1/plan-versions/{id}/publish`.

### Events

Published: `subscription.activated.v1`, `subscription.plan_changed.v1`,
`subscription.suspended.v1`, `entitlements.changed.v1`. Consumed: `tenant.created.v1` from tenant
management to attach a trial, `payment.mandate_failed.v1` from the payments service to drive
`past_due`.

```json
{ "event": "entitlements.changed.v1", "tenant_id": "…", "subscription_id": "…",
  "effective_at": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z", "revision": 14,
  "changed_keys": ["module.pharmaconnect", "limit.users"] }
```

Consumers key on `revision` and discard out-of-order deliveries; JetStream gives at-least-once, so
handlers must be idempotent.

### Authorisation

OpenFGA carries the commercial relations; nothing about subscriptions is inferred from clinical
roles.

```
type subscription
  relations
    define tenant: [tenant]
    define billing_admin: billing_admin from tenant
    define viewer: billing_admin or admin from tenant
    define can_change_plan: billing_admin
    define can_cancel: billing_admin
```

A ward nurse or doctor never resolves `viewer` on a subscription. Platform finance operators get
`can_publish_plan` on the `plan` type only, not on tenant data.

### Sequencing and risks

Depends on tenant provisioning and the OpenFGA authorisation model landing first, and on the
payments service exposing UPI AutoPay mandate creation. The main risk is entitlement-cache
staleness: a downgrade that does not propagate leaves a tenant using a module it no longer pays
for. Mitigated with a short Redis TTL (60 s), event-driven invalidation, and a nightly Temporal
reconciliation workflow that recomputes every tenant's entitlement map from source and alerts on
drift. The second risk is a commercial change silently altering historical invoices; the immutable
`plan_version` design plus the update trigger removes it.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** a newly created single-facility tenant with a valid UPI AutoPay mandate
**When** the clinic owner subscribes to Clinic plan version 1
**Then** the subscription is created as `trialing` with a 14-day trial, `entitlements.changed.v1`
is published, and within 60 seconds MediCore, DoctorConnect, PharmaConnect and MediConnect all
resolve `module.*` entitlements matching the plan version exactly, with LabConnect analyser
integration and all IPD capabilities resolving false.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** the entitlement cache in Redis is unavailable
**When** a DoctorConnect request checks `module.eprescribe`
**Then** the SDK falls back to a direct read against the billing service within a 250 ms timeout,
and if that also fails it returns the last known good entitlement snapshot with a
`stale_entitlements` trace attribute and a raised metric — it never fails open on a limit check and
never blocks read access to existing clinical records.

### Edge Cases

* A second facility is created for a Clinic tenant: creation is refused with `limit.facilities`
  exceeded and an upgrade path to Hospital (#248), while the existing facility keeps working.
* Trial expires with no successful mandate debit: subscription moves to `past_due`, writes are
  restricted after the configured grace window, and record export remains available so the clinic
  is never held hostage to its own data.
* A duplicate `POST /subscriptions` with the same idempotency key returns the original
  subscription, not a second one; the exclusion constraint proves it even under concurrent calls.
* Plan version 1 is retired while a tenant is mid-period: the tenant stays on version 1 until the
  next renewal, and the renewal workflow requires explicit migration approval.
* A user with clinical roles but no `billing_admin` relation calls `POST /subscriptions/{id}/cancel`
  and receives `403` with no subscription detail in the response body.
* Cross-tenant probe: a Clinic tenant's billing admin requests another tenant's entitlements and
  receives `404`, not `403`, so subscription existence is not disclosed.

---

## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team's agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* **Expected user or system outcome:** a clinic owner completes self-serve signup to a working,
  correctly entitled tenant without any manual provisioning step, and every product service reads
  entitlements from one authoritative source.
* **Expected business or operational outcome:** the platform can sell and bill its entry tier, and
  the versioned plan catalogue built here becomes the foundation the remaining seven stories in this
  epic extend without redesign.
* **Success metric or validation method:** self-serve signup to first entitled login completes in
  under 5 minutes for 95 % of attempts; entitlement check p95 ≤ 15 ms at the SDK; entitlement
  propagation after a plan change is complete for 99 % of tenants within 60 seconds; the nightly
  reconciliation workflow reports zero drift across 30 consecutive runs; 100 % of attempts to mutate
  a published plan version are rejected at the database layer in the adversarial test suite.
* **Monitoring period, where applicable:** 30 days post-launch, with weekly review of stale-cache
  fallbacks, limit-exceeded refusals by key (to distinguish genuine upsell signal from a mis-seeded
  limit), and trial-to-paid conversion.

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

None — all guardrails apply. This story delivers both a backend service and the AdminConnect signup
and subscription-management screens, so the accessibility guardrail is in scope in full: the plan
selection, mandate setup and limit-exceeded upgrade prompt must be keyboard-navigable, correctly
labelled and legible on the low-cost Android devices the console is used from.

items.title: Change the management of data tables and add some interface exposure for agent
items.body:
# Architecture & Design Discussion ## Summary This document proposes a comprehensive architecture and design for `lance-context`, a high-performance, evolvable context management solution for AI Agents. The design establishes a clean separation between the logical information layer and the physical storage layer (LanceDB), defines a clear set of Agent-facing interfaces, and introduces a layered data model (L0-L2) to balance retrieval effectiveness and cost. It also includes specifications for data governance, multi-tenancy, and a phased implementation roadmap, aiming to provide a robust foundation for building and scaling complex Agent systems. ## Motivation / Problem Statement Current Agent development faces several challenges: - **Fragmented Context**: Information is often scattered across various systems, leading to inconsistent and incomplete context for the Agent. - **Suboptimal Retrieval**: Existing retrieval mechanisms lack the sophistication to balance precision, recall, and cost effectively. - **Disorderly Information Growth**: Without a proper strategy, an Agent's memory and knowledge base can expand indefinitely, leading to performance degradation and increased costs. - **Lack of Extensibility**: Tightly coupled business logic and storage implementations make it difficult to evolve the system, such as introducing new storage engines or adapting to new Agent capabilities. The initial version of `lance-context` provides a solid starting point, but a more systematic architecture is required to address these issues and support the long-term growth of sophisticated AI Agents. ## Design Overview The proposed architecture is centered around three key concepts: 1. **Information Layer on LanceDB**: A logical `Information Layer` is introduced on top of the physical LanceDB storage. This layer provides a stable, semantic view of the data, abstracting away the underlying implementation details. It organizes data into three distinct families: `ctx_agent` (core Agent business data), `ctx_kb` (external knowledge), and `ctx_meta` (internal system metadata). 2. **Layered Data Model (L0-L2)**: Inspired by industry best practices, we adopt a three-layer data model to optimize retrieval and processing: * **L2 (Raw Content)**: The immutable source of truth. * **L1 (Structured & Vector)**: The primary retrieval target, containing cleaned, chunked, and vectorized data. * **L0 (Abstract/Summary)**: A high-level summary layer for efficient pre-filtering and low-cost relevance assessment. 3. **Task-Oriented Agent Interfaces**: A set of high-level interfaces (`Add`, `Search`, `Explain`, `Trace`, `Prune`, `Archive`) are defined to provide Agents with intuitive, task-oriented capabilities for managing their context, memory, and knowledge. ## Detailed Design ### Overall Architecture and Data Layers We propose an overall architecture that includes an **Information Layer**, which provides a stable logical view for Agent applications on top of the physical storage (LanceDB). ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph "Agent Application" Agent["AI Agent"] end subgraph "Information Layer (lance-context)" direction LR subgraph "Agent Interfaces" direction TB Add["Add"] Search["Search"] Prune["Prune"] Archive["Archive"] end subgraph "Table Families" direction TB ctx_agent["ctx_agent (Core)"] ctx_kb["ctx_kb (Knowledge)"] ctx_meta["ctx_meta (Internal)"] end subgraph "Data Layers" direction TB L0["L0 (Summary)"] L1["L1 (Structured/Vector)"] L2["L2 (Raw Content)"] end end subgraph "Physical Storage" LanceDB["LanceDB"] end Agent --> Add Agent --> Search Agent --> Prune Agent --> Archive Add --> L2 L2 --> L1 L1 --> L0 Search -- "queries" --> L0 Search -- "queries" --> L1 L1 -- "links to" --> L2 ctx_agent --> LanceDB ctx_kb --> LanceDB ctx_meta --> LanceDB ``` The core of this architecture is a governance strategy based on data layering and separation. #### Data Layers: L0, L1, and L2 we process and store data in three logical layers to optimize retrieval efficiency and reduce LLM token consumption. - **L2 (Raw Content Layer)** - **Semantics**: Unprocessed raw data, serving as the "Source of Truth" for all information. Examples include complete conversation logs, user-uploaded original documents, and full tool-call logs. - **Generation Pipeline**: Data enters the system via the `Add` interface and is directly stored in the corresponding L2 table. - **Storage Strategy**: Stored in tables like `ctx_agent.agent_l2_raw` or `ctx_kb.kb_l2_raw_documents` in binary or text format. - **Retrieval Strategy**: Not directly involved in retrieval by default. It is accessed only for "evidence traceability" or deep analysis, via links from L1/L0. - **L1 (Structured & Vector Layer)** - **Semantics**: The result of cleaning, chunking, extracting metadata from, and generating vector embeddings for L2 data. This is the **primary retrieval target** of the system, balancing information density and contextual granularity. - **Generation Pipeline**: Triggered by a background task or write pipeline, it processes new L2 data to generate L1 records. - **Storage Strategy**: Chunked text and metadata are stored in `ctx_agent.agent_l1_chunks`, and vectors are stored in `ctx_agent.agent_l1_embeddings`. - **Retrieval Strategy**: This is the main layer for hybrid retrieval (Scalar + FTS + Vector). An Agent's `Search` request first retrieves candidates from this layer using vector similarity, keywords, and metadata filtering. - **L0 (Abstract/Summary Layer)** - **Semantics**: A brief summary generated for a group of L1 Chunks or an L2 object (like a session or a document). Its core function is **pre-filtering**, helping the Agent or retrieval strategy quickly determine if a larger entity (like an entire session) is worth exploring in-depth. - **Generation Pipeline**: Triggered by a background task or after L1 processing is complete, it calls an LLM to summarize L1 Chunks or L2 content. - **Storage Strategy**: Stored in the `ctx_agent.agent_l0_summaries` table and linked to the corresponding L1/L2 entities. - **Retrieval Strategy**: Acts as the first line of defense in retrieval. For instance, in cross-session retrieval, it can quickly filter L0 summaries of all sessions to locate the most relevant ones before performing a precise search within their L1 Chunks. #### Retrieval Chain The standard retrieval chain follows the **L0 → L1 → L2** sequence: 1. **L0 Pre-filtering**: Based on the query intent, a quick, low-cost match is first performed on the L0 summary layer to identify highly relevant entities (e.g., sessions, documents). 2. **L1 Main Retrieval**: Within the scope of entities filtered by L0, or directly in the global L1 Chunks, a hybrid search is executed to recall the most relevant atomic information blocks. 3. **L2 Evidence Traceability**: The L1 retrieval results are presented to the LLM. If more complete context or fact-verification is needed, the LLM or user can trace back to the L2 raw data using the links saved in the L1 records. ### Table Families and Naming Conventions To decouple business logic from internal management, we have designed three independent table families (which can be mapped to different databases or directories in LanceDB), each with clear naming conventions and responsibilities. #### `ctx_agent` Family: Agent Business Core Stores runtime data directly interacting with the Agent. | Logical Table Name | Description | Core Field Suggestions | Index Suggestions | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `agent_sessions` | Session metadata | `session_id` (PK), `agent_id`, `user_id`, `status`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `metadata` (JSON) | B-Tree: `agent_id`, `user_id`, `start_time` | | `agent_l2_raw` | L2 raw data | `raw_id` (PK), `source_id` (e.g., session_id), `content` (bytes/text), `content_type`, `created_at` | B-Tree: `source_id`, `created_at` | | `agent_l1_chunks` | L1 structured chunks | `chunk_id` (PK), `raw_id`, `content` (text), `metadata` (JSON), `created_at`, `agent_id` | FTS: `content`; B-Tree: `agent_id`, `created_at` | | `agent_l1_embeddings` | L1 vector embeddings | `chunk_id` (FK), `vector` (fixed_size_list), `model_name`, `created_at` | Vector (IVF_PQ): `vector` | | `agent_l0_summaries`| L0 summaries | `target_id` (PK), `target_type` (session/doc), `summary` (text), `updated_at`, `agent_id` | FTS: `summary`; B-Tree: `agent_id`, `target_type` | | `agent_skills` | Agent skill definitions | `skill_id` (PK), `name`, `schema` (JSON), `description`, `agent_id`, `version` | B-Tree: `agent_id`, `name` | | `agent_tool_calls` | Tool call records | `call_id` (PK), `session_id`, `tool_name`, `params` (JSON), `result` (text), `status`, `timestamp` | B-Tree: `session_id`, `tool_name`, `timestamp` | | `agent_relations` | Entity relationship graph | `source_id`, `target_id`, `relation_type` (e.g., 'cites', 'triggers'), `agent_id`, `created_at` | B-Tree: `source_id`, `target_id`, `agent_id` | #### `ctx_kb` Family: External Knowledge Base Used for storing relatively static, shareable background knowledge. Its structure is similar to `ctx_agent` but with an independent lifecycle and management strategy. | Logical Table Name | Description | Core Field Suggestions | Index Suggestions | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `kb_l2_raw_documents` | L2 raw knowledge documents | `doc_id` (PK), `source_uri`, `content`, `metadata` (JSON), `imported_at` | B-Tree: `source_uri` | | `kb_l1_chunks` | L1 knowledge base chunks | `chunk_id` (PK), `doc_id`, `content`, `metadata` (JSON) | FTS: `content` | | `kb_l1_embeddings` | L1 knowledge base vectors | `chunk_id` (FK), `vector` (fixed_size_list), `model_name` | Vector (IVF_PQ): `vector` | #### `ctx_meta` Family: Internal Metadata The system's "Information Schema," used for self-management and internal task scheduling, transparent to the Agent. | Logical Table Name | Description | Core Field Suggestions | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `meta_tables` | Registry of tables | `table_name`, `db_name`, `table_type`, `version` | Records which logical tables exist in the system and their ownership. | | `meta_columns` | Column attributes | `table_name`, `column_name`, `data_type`, `is_time`, `is_vector` | Queries and manages table schemas, especially special attributes like time and vectors. | | `meta_jobs` | Background task queue | `job_id` (PK), `job_type` (prune/index), `payload`, `status`, `scheduled_at` | Schedules asynchronous tasks like index rebuilding, data pruning, and archiving. | | `meta_mem_candidates` | Memory candidate pool | `session_id`, `chunk_id`, `score`, `candidate_level` (promote/prune) | The core table for implementing the daily pruning mechanism. | #### Temporal Attributes and Indexing Conventions - **Temporal Attributes**: All fields involving timestamps (e.g., `created_at`, `timestamp`) should use a uniform UTC Timestamp type. - **Vector Indexing**: The `vector` field is the primary target for vector indexing. IVF_PQ is recommended. - **FTS Indexing**: All `content` or `summary` fields should have a Full-Text Search (FTS) index. ### Multi-Tenancy, Concurrency, and Data Governance - **Multi-Tenancy and Versioning**: - **Logical Isolation**: All records in `ctx_agent` must include an `agent_id`. - **Physical Isolation**: Data can be written to different directories based on `agent_id`. - **Versioning**: Relies on LanceDB's native transaction and versioning capabilities. - **Concurrency and Isolation**: - **Read-Write Isolation**: Ensured by LanceDB's Copy-on-Write mechanism. - **Write Concurrency**: A write queue at the API layer is recommended to batch-merge high-concurrency `Add` operations. - **Index Maintenance and Archiving**: - **Index Maintenance**: Handled by background jobs in `meta_jobs` during off-peak hours. - **Data Archiving**: Triggered via the `Prune` interface, performs a soft delete and migrates data to cold storage via a background task. ### Agent Interface Mapping The interfaces provided by `lance-context` to the Agent should be task-oriented and highly abstract. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Agent direction LR A[Add] S[Search] E[Explain] T[Trace] P[Prune] AR[Archive] end subgraph Backend direction TB subgraph ctx_agent agent_l2["agent_l2_raw"] agent_l1["agent_l1_chunks/embeddings"] agent_l0["agent_l0_summaries"] agent_relations["agent_relations"] agent_tool_calls["agent_tool_calls"] end subgraph ctx_meta meta_jobs["meta_jobs"] meta_mem_candidates["meta_mem_candidates"] end end A -- "Writes to" --> agent_l2 A -- "Triggers async write to" --> agent_l1 A -- "Triggers async write to" --> agent_l0 S -- "Queries" --> agent_l1 E -- "Traverses" --> agent_relations T -- "Fetches from" --> agent_l1 T -- "Fetches from" --> agent_tool_calls P -- "Filters in" --> meta_mem_candidates P -- "Creates job in" --> meta_jobs AR -- "Creates job in" --> meta_jobs ``` #### Core Interface Prototypes (DTOs) | Interface | Input Parameters (DTO) | Output (DTO) | Core Logic & Table Mapping | Error Code Suggestions | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `Add` | `content: Union[str, bytes]`, `content_type: str`, `session_id: Optional[str]`, `metadata: Dict` | `job_id: str` | 1. Write to `agent_l2_raw` (L2).
2. Trigger background task: write to `agent_l1_chunks`/`embeddings` (L1).
3. (Optional) Trigger LLM to write to `agent_l0_summaries` (L0). | 400, 503 | | `Search` | `query: str`, `filter: Dict`, `top_k: int`, `search_type: Literal[...]` | `results: List[Chunk]` | 1. Concurrently query `agent_l1_chunks` (FTS) and `agent_l1_embeddings` (Vector).
2. Use RRF to fuse results.
3. Perform scalar filtering. | 400, 404 | | `Explain` | `entity_id: str`, `entity_type: str` | `graph: Dict` | Recursively trace relationships from the `agent_relations` table. | 404 | | `Trace` | `session_id: str` | `events: List[...]` | Fetch all records for `session_id` from `agent_l1_chunks` and `agent_tool_calls` and sort by timestamp. | 404 | | `Prune` | `policy: Dict` | `job_id: str` | 1. Filter candidates in `meta_mem_candidates`.
2. Create a `prune` task in `meta_jobs`.
3. Background task performs soft delete/archiving. | 400 | | `Archive` | `session_id: str` | `job_id: str` | Create an `archive` task in `meta_jobs` to migrate all session data. | 404 | ### Daily Compaction Mechanism This mechanism distills incremental conversation data (Episodes) into valuable long-term memory (Profiles) and cleans up low-value information. 1. **Scoring and Candidacy** - A daily background task scans recent `agent_sessions` and `agent_l1_chunks`. - **Scoring Dimensions**: Activity, Importance, Reusability, Time Decay. - Based on a weighted score, each item is marked in `meta_mem_candidates` as `PROMOTION`, `RETENTION`, or `PRUNING`. 2. **Promotion to Episode/Profile** - A background task processes records marked for `PROMOTION`. - It aggregates content, calls an LLM to generate a narrative **Episode** or update a structured **User Profile**, and stores the result in a long-term memory table. - The operation is transactional and can be rolled back. ## Limitations / Open Questions - **Performance at Scale**: While LanceDB is highly performant, the FTS and complex scalar query capabilities might become a bottleneck under heavy load. The hybrid storage model in Phase 2 is designed to mitigate this. - **Write Concurrency Management**: The proposed write queue adds a layer of complexity. Its implementation and tuning will be critical for high-throughput scenarios. - **Cost of L0 Generation**: Generating L0 summaries via LLM calls for every L1/L2 update can be costly. A selective or batch-based strategy for L0 generation might be needed. - **Complexity of Query Router**: The Query Router in Phase 3 is a significant engineering effort and will require careful design to handle query parsing, distribution, and result fusion correctly. ## Rollout Plan / Roadmap We recommend a phased approach to implement this design. - **Phase 1: Unified Information Layer View based on LanceDB** - **Goal**: Implement the complete L0/L1/L2 data model and core APIs (`Add`, `Search`) using only LanceDB. - **Outcome**: A functionally complete but limited-performance context database. - **Phase 2: Hybrid Storage and Query Offloading** - **Goal**: Introduce external specialized engines (e.g., Elasticsearch for FTS) where LanceDB's native capabilities are insufficient. - **Outcome**: A hybrid system with better performance and stronger query capabilities. - **Phase 3: Engine Adapter Layer and Query Router** - **Goal**: Evolve `lance-context` into a universal "context virtualization layer" that supports any combination of backend storage engines. - **Outcome**: A highly scalable context database platform completely decoupled from the underlying storage. ## Checklist - [ ] Finalize table schemas for all three families. - [ ] Implement Phase 1 `Add` interface and async processing pipeline. - [ ] Implement Phase 1 `Search` interface with hybrid search capabilities. - [ ] Set up `meta_jobs` and a basic daily compaction framework. - [ ] Develop adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex. - [ ] Benchmark performance of the Phase 1 implementation. - [ ] Document all public APIs and data models. ## Impact Assessment - **Performance**: The layered data model and hybrid retrieval strategy are expected to significantly improve query performance and reduce LLM context size. Write latency will be managed via asynchronous processing and a write queue. - **Cost**: While LLM calls for L0/L1 generation introduce costs, the overall architecture aims to reduce token consumption during retrieval, potentially leading to net savings. The phased rollout allows for cost-effective scaling. - **Compatibility**: The design is framework-agnostic. By providing clean DTOs and adapters, it ensures easy integration with existing and future Agent frameworks. The reliance on LanceDB in Phase 1 simplifies initial deployment and dependencies.

items.title: Monthly Dashboard v2 — unified RAW/core/template for W + CPR
items.body:
## Goal

Build **Monthly Dashboard v2** as a shared architecture for W and CPR first, using the same raw data foundation as Daily/Weekly while preserving Monthly-specific business logic and visual structure.

Do **not** work on Orange yet. Do **not** spend time on visual polish or SKU-specific analysis until this task is complete.

## Core principles

1. **One raw data foundation**
   - Daily, Weekly and Monthly must read from the same normalized RAW layer in Supabase.
   - Monthly must not be derived from `sku_daily`.
   - Reports may apply different business logic, but must not maintain separate primary data sources.

2. **One Monthly template**
   - W and CPR must use one shared frontend/core implementation.
   - Cabinet-specific differences live in config/data, not duplicated code.
   - Architecture should be extensible to Orange and future clients after W/CPR are validated.

3. **Monthly lifecycle**
   - LIVE = current month.
   - CLOSING = previous month after cutoff, while validation/enrichment completes.
   - CLOSED = frozen month.
   - Month cutoff is 00:00 on the first day of the next month.
   - Closed month must not drift when order statuses change later.

4. **Compensations are separate**
   - Base Monthly economics must work without compensation/decompensation.
   - Compensation layer is applied independently later.
   - CPR logic: actual SKU compensation.
   - W/Orange logic later: category-level allocation.
   - For now, keep compensation excluded from the core validation of September.

## Existing verified September baseline

### W
- Finance API September 01–30 loaded to Supabase.
- Official Ozon accrual report reconciled exactly: **0.00 RUB difference**.
- Net sales: **6,387,302.00 RUB**
- Result after standard Ozon charges, before compensation: **2,034,525.91 RUB**
- September is now stored in `sku_monthly_w`.

### CPR
- Finance API September 01–30 loaded to Supabase.
- Official Ozon accrual report reconciled exactly: **0.00 RUB difference** at raw Finance level.
- Net sales: **7,159,659.00 RUB**
- Result before compensation/decompensation: **2,536,482.50 RUB**
- Difference to Ozon grand total = **8,533.90 RUB**, intentionally excluded decompensation.
- September is now stored in `sku_monthly_cpr`.

### Shared raw finance table
- `public.ozon_finance_lines_raw_v1`
- tenant_id distinguishes W / CPR.

## Required architecture

Target flow:

```
Ozon API
  -> shared RAW tables in Supabase
  -> normalized/core SQL layer
  -> Daily views
  -> Weekly views
  -> Monthly views
  -> shared Monthly frontend
```

n8n should be used for ingestion/schedules/integrations, not as the business-logic source of truth.

## Data layer tasks

### A. Audit current sources
Document what Daily, Weekly and Monthly currently read from for W and CPR.

Identify:
- duplicated sources;
- report-specific tables that are acting as primary data;
- hardcoded month/account logic;
- duplicated expense classification;
- any dependency on Google Sheets.

### B. Normalize raw entities
At minimum define/confirm shared raw sources for:
- orders/statuses;
- finance accrual lines;
- product/SKU dictionary;
- price history;
- cost history;
- business expenses;
- compensation imports.

Every shared source must include tenant/account identity.

### C. Central expense classification
Create one source of truth for Ozon fee classification:
- type_id;
- Ozon label;
- internal expense_group;
- direct/shared;
- allocation basis.

Daily/Weekly/Monthly must consume the same classification.

Unknown type_id must fail validation or appear in an explicit audit table; never silently go to an unreviewed bucket.

## Monthly core

Create a shared Monthly Core schema/view set parameterized by tenant.

Expected output per SKU/month should include at least:
- tenant_id / account_id;
- month;
- marketplace;
- SKU;
- article;
- product_name;
- master_category;
- sale_operations;
- return_operations;
- sold_units;
- sales;
- returns;
- net_sales;
- commission;
- logistics;
- storage;
- promotion;
- other;
- direct expenses;
- allocated shared expenses;
- total Ozon expenses;
- result without compensation;
- compensation placeholders;
- result with compensation;
- economic units;
- received per unit;
- source;
- month status: LIVE/CLOSING/CLOSED;
- updated_at.

Do not duplicate this logic for W and CPR.

## Month close mechanism

Implement a reusable closing process:

1. At 00:00 first day of next month, previous month leaves LIVE.
2. Freeze order/status snapshot.
3. Backfill full Finance API for all dates of previous month.
4. Validate completeness.
5. Store closed month result.
6. Current month becomes the only LIVE month.
7. Later data changes must not mutate CLOSED month membership.

If exact historical status at cutoff cannot be guaranteed from a current-state table, introduce append-only status history or another reliable capture mechanism.

## Validation / acceptance checks

Build automated checks for every closed month:

- every expected calendar day loaded;
- raw Finance total equals normalized Finance total;
- sum SKU + shared allocations equals account total;
- shared allocation conserves the original shared amount exactly;
- no unknown type_id;
- no duplicate accrual keys;
- no duplicated SKU/month rows;
- closed month is immutable;
- LIVE month remains dynamic;
- W September matches verified control:
  - net sales 6,387,302.00
  - result before compensation 2,034,525.91
- CPR September matches verified control:
  - net sales 7,159,659.00
  - result before compensation 2,536,482.50

Produce a validation report/query that can be run after every monthly close.

## Shared frontend

After the data/core layer is stable:

Create one Monthly frontend/template for W and CPR.

Cabinet differences must be configuration only.

Suggested structure:

```
monthly/
  core/
  config/
  data/
  components/
  tests/
```

No separate W Monthly app and CPR Monthly app.

### Monthly visual structure to preserve

Top KPI block:
1. Net sales
2. Marketplace expenses
3. Ozon result without compensation
4. Compensation
5. Business expenses
6. Final result after all expenses

Below:
- Financial funnel
- Month dynamics: 3 closed + current live
- Expense structure
- Business expenses/capital
- SKU table
- SKU detail card

The frontend must clearly label LIVE vs CLOSED.

## Dashboard data access

Current W/CPR management dashboards are served via n8n webhook and read SQL tables.

For v2:
- prefer a direct prepared API/view layer over using n8n as a read proxy;
- if keeping n8n temporarily, isolate it as transport only;
- frontend schema should be identical for every tenant.

Target API shape conceptually:
- `/monthly?tenant=W`
- `/monthly?tenant=CPR`

## Account config

Create a shared account configuration model/table with fields such as:
- tenant_id;
- marketplace;
- account_id;
- display_name;
- active;
- category/default master category;
- compensation method;
- cost method;
- business expense method;
- dashboard enabled.

Goal: onboarding another cabinet should be configuration-driven, not code duplication.

## Historical cost model

Costs must be time-valid:
- SKU
- valid_from
- valid_to
- unit_cost

Historical months must not change when a new cost is entered.

## Scope order

### Phase 1
Audit + unified RAW/data model.

### Phase 2
Shared Monthly Core for W + CPR.

### Phase 3
LIVE/CLOSING/CLOSED lifecycle + month close automation.

### Phase 4
Automated reconciliation/tests against July/August/September.

### Phase 5
Single Monthly frontend for W + CPR.

### Phase 6
Compensation layer.

### Phase 7
Business expenses + historical costs.

### Phase 8
Only after W/CPR are stable: Orange.

## Non-goals for this task

- No Orange migration yet.
- No SKU-specific pricing analysis.
- No cosmetic UI tweaks unless required for shared-template refactor.
- Do not change Daily business logic.
- Do not break Weekly.
- Do not delete legacy tables/views before parity is proven.

## Definition of done

Monthly v2 is complete when:

- W and CPR use one Monthly template.
- Daily/Weekly/Monthly share one RAW foundation.
- September is CLOSED without manual Excel dependence.
- October is the only LIVE month.
- Next month can transition automatically.
- Finance API reconciliation is automated.
- Expense classification is centralized.
- Unknown fees are surfaced.
- Historical costs are time-valid.
- New cabinets can be added by config.
- Legacy W/CPR monthly paths are archived only after parity tests pass.
- A short migration/readme document explains:
  - final architecture;
  - table/view ownership;
  - close workflow;
  - validation commands;
  - how to onboard a new cabinet.

## Delivery expectations

Work in small verifiable commits/PR(s). For each phase, include:
- what changed;
- impact on dashboard;
- how to verify it;
- any migration/backfill required.

Do not require the user to shuttle implementation details between ChatGPT and Codex. Keep implementation notes in the repository/issue/PR.

items.title: [Epic] Axal VC WorkGraph — universal agent task coordination, asset versioning and controlled publishing
items.body:
# Axal VC WorkGraph — Universal AI-Native Work Coordination and Asset Versioning

**Scope:** Internal StudioOS engineering AND tenant-scoped customer venture teams. **Priority:** P0 architecture, incrementally delivered. Builds on #5564 (portable agent execution) and #3742 (AI team task engine), extends—not duplicates—#5569 (GitHub publisher), #4101 (closed shared-file conflict prevention), #5500/#5501/#5506 (merge/release CI). Existing domain workflows remain canonical for their business records, including legal_templates, Contracts/e-sign, Pitch, Deals, Learning/Stream, Approvals.

## Decision
Build **one shared WorkGraph / ChangeSet / AssetRevision coordination layer** in the existing Cloudflare Worker/Hono control plane, not a homemade replacement for Git, Figma, Blender, Drive or legal signing. The layer is a permissioned, typed graph of tasks, assets, source references, immutable versions, dependencies, agent contributions, human decisions, and released manifests. Use modality-specific merge/render/storage adapters. Default to Cloudflare D1 (metadata, transactional refs, ACL, review state), R2 (original masters/immutable blobs and variants), Durable Objects (scoped leases/fencing/collaboration), Queues/Workflows (existing durable execution), and Cloudflare Stream for video streaming/derivatives where appropriate. External GitHub/Drive/Figma/3D tools remain their respective authoring sources when selected; import/publish into a versioned Axal-controlled manifest with source-of-truth rules, not blind duplication.

## Canonical source-of-truth matrix
| Artifact | Authoritative content | Authoritative registry/state | Delivery / derivatives |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code / IaC | Customer/owned GitHub Git repository + immutable Git SHA | D1 mapping venture/task/PR/review; GitHub authoritative merge/ref status | OCI image registry and deployment |
| Legal template | Existing Cloudflare `legal_templates` revision lineage and counsel-approved text; e-sign provider owns signed-envelope evidence | Existing Contracts/legal/governance tables; append-only approval trail | Frozen PDF/DOCX in R2; signed evidence hash/refs; never auto-merge legal clauses |
| Pitch deck, offers, proposals, editable documents | Axal-native structured source revision in existing module, or explicitly linked external canonical document with connector revision | D1 revision + approved manifest; no competing draft ledger | PPTX/PDF/preview in R2; exports are derived |
| Brand system / design | Versioned brand token / design-source package and editable Figma/other source when explicitly selected | D1 design system revision, rights, dependencies, approval | R2 originals, previews, image variants |
| Images | Original editable source when available plus immutable master; generation recipe/model/settings/seed where available | D1 asset revision + rights/consent and provenance | R2 renditions + thumbnails; CDN delivery |
| Video/audio | Original source timeline/project + immutable masters, timecoded edit decisions | D1 version graph + rights, approvals and review comments | R2 masters/project files; Stream for playback and transcoded versions |
| 3D/CAD | Versioned editable native project + exchange format and dependencies | D1 scene/assembly metadata, licenses and revision graph | R2 meshes, textures, previews, glTF/USD exports, CDN |
| Composite deliverables | Immutable release manifest pinning exact component versions | D1 approval/publication pointer | Signed/hashed R2 package, Stream playback where used |

**Principle:** D1 is the *index and authority for Axal workflow/policy*, not a large blob store. R2 is the *object authority for Axal-managed media binaries*, not a collaborative editor. GitHub remains authoritative for Git code content. Existing signed legal instruments are immutable evidence with their own governing record.

## Critical concurrency model
- A WorkItem references canonical venture/scope, deliverable, proposed modification scope, base version, dependency IDs, actor (person/agent), run, priority, risk and idempotency key.
- On admission, calculate impact/overlap across code paths + symbols, doc sections/clauses, slide/component IDs, image layers/masks, video timeline ranges/tracks, 3D nodes/materials, and rights/approvals.
- **Non-overlap:** work concurrently. **Mergeable structured text:** optimistic concurrency + scoped 3-way merge where semantically safe; review resulting combined version. **Media conflicts:** independent immutable variants / version DAG + explicit compositor/owner choice; never binary-union files. **High-stakes legal, security, money, signed or released material:** exclusive publication gate with human approval; avoid automatic semantic merges.
- Short, renewable leases only on critical shared resources (legal clause review/final signature, central schema, brand master, release pointer), with generation fencing, expiry, deadlock prevention, priority inheritance and revocation. A lease does not grant edit authorization.
- Every outcome is an immutable content-addressed revision with parents and provenance; a publication manifest atomically advances an expected revision pointer (CAS). No stale result overwrites a newer approved version.
- Composite releases pin exact versions of slides, graphics, legal terms, video clips, captions, translations and evidence; any component change invalidates dependent approvals where policy requires.

## Execution layers
- Reuse existing AI agent roles/task runner; #5564 executor adapters route workload by modality to Cloudflare Containers, external clouds or BYOC where security/capacity/policy requires. Interactive editing is separate from batch compute.
- The same WorkGraph APIs operate for Axal internal PRs and tenant ventures with strict tenant/repo isolation.
- Tooling connectors may bring revision IDs and metadata, but remote editor remains authoritative until explicit snapshot/publish; no invisible dual-master sync.
- Never treat generated previews as source masters; all manifests include R2 object digest, rendition type, source/model/edit recipe, license, provenance, retention, residency and ACL.

## Delivery gates
P0: source-of-truth ADR + typed contract; internal PR overlap dashboard / prework reservations; immutable asset revision registry and permissions.
P1: doc/deck/legal guarded workflow + creative asset rendition/rights pipeline + composite release builder.
P2: video/3D timeline/scene adapters, interactive collaboration where justified; multi-provider/billing/load benchmark. Use measurements and customer use cases before bespoke binary diff engine or Git replacement.

## Acceptance
- Two independent agents create revisions without overwriting each other; independent sections merge or build a shared candidate; overlapping edits produce a human-resolvable conflict.
- Same mechanism works with 10/50/100 synthetic tasks spanning internal PRs, pitch, legal, brand image/video/3D, gated by owner-approved quota; one logical publish per idempotency key.
- For every released asset, trace tenant → source → revision → agent/human contributions → approval → exact binary hashes → publication. Revocation blocks further release without mutating historical signed records.
- Wrong-tenant/missing rights, lost callbacks, concurrent updates, stale approvals, quota exhaustion, partial upload and provider failure fail closed.
- No automatic modification/publication of legal agreements, no external cloud provisioning or production changes without owner approval.

## Related issues — preserve implementation ownership
#5569 GitHub publisher; #5500/#5501 protected merges; #5506 CI queue; #4101 closed hotspot work; #5456/#5458 deal revisions/review; #3716 pitch builder; #3726 Stream/Learning; #5049 licensed agreements. All child issues must link here and avoid duplicate domain state tables or APIs.


## Child implementation issues created — 2026-11-11

| Order | Issue | Package |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | #5579 | Canonical source-of-truth ADR and asset/changeset contracts |
| P0 | #5580 | StudioOS internal PR conflict graph, reservations and integration triage |
| P0 | #5581 | Cross-modality immutable revision DAG, leases and concurrency |
| P1 | #5582 | Legal, document, pitch and offer coordination adapters |
| P1 | #5583 | R2-based media vault, branding, image and 3D versions |
| P1 | #5584 | Video/audio timeline and Cloudflare Stream delivery |
| P1 | #5585 | Approved composite release manifests and publishing |
| P1 | #5586 | Swarm budgets, fairness and multi-modality recovery benchmarks |

**Recommended critical path:** #5579 → (#5580 and #5581) → (#5582 and #5583) → (#5584 and #5585) → #5586. #5580 can begin with a read-only GitHub dashboard immediately; enforcement waits for proven risk classification. Security and existing runtime #5564 are parallel dependencies.

items.body:
<!-- local-draft: artifacts/local-ai/out/issue-draft-obligations-assessor.md -->
## Summary

Create a dedicated Claude Code agent, `test-obligations-assessor`, that decides per file, per line and per test flag (unit, guard, contract, property, integration) which test obligations apply, whether a target of 0 is legitimate, and what the demanding-and-realistic targets and their justifications are. It records a verdict in the coverage manifest and is mandatory in worker briefs, SPEC-003 audits, the zero review and doubtful areas, always as a party distinct from the code's author. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-10-26 as option (D) of #2890 (agent for judgment plus deterministic syntax tripwire).

## Motivation

- Use cases and scenarios: Today targets are chosen by whoever writes the code or the brief; zero unit/guard/contract targets are accepted for files with executable code and nothing can tell (#2840), and 22 package/flag pairs have no package target while a 0 per-file target reports as met (#2841).
- Industry comparison: A deterministic gate cannot judge context (is this 0 legitimate? is 60% demanding enough for this branching?); an agent can, but acts only when invoked and is not reproducible. The maintainer's decision pairs both: the agent judges, the tripwire of #2890 (Roslyn syntax analysis against a closed list of non-executable constructs) fails CI when a 0-target file gains executable lines, or when a file under `src/` has no verdict or a verdict older than the file's last change. Together nobody can skip the agent and no verdict can silently go stale.
- Strategic context: EPIC #2845 (measurement integrity); AGENTS.md section 9 (obligations are justified, demanding and realistic); the obligations policy of 2026-10-05; #1762 (justifications in the manifest); #1763 (rule (b) of the test-auditor). A distinct assessor removes the author's incentive to set low targets and gives the audit pipeline one owner for obligations.

## Proposed Solution

- Agent definition `.claude/agents/test-obligations-assessor.md`: model Sonnet (effort high, because reasoning is the job), tools PowerShell, Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write. Read-only on `src/` and `tests/`; the only file it writes is the verdict inside `.github/coverage-manifest/{Package}.json` (and its own report under `artifacts/`). Hooks follow `.claude/agents/test-auditor.md` (block-worker-publish, block-main-checkout-writes, block-prohibited-commands, enforce-path-ownership with `-Agent test-obligations-assessor`, no-background-specialists, block-worker-spawn). Never pushes, opens PRs or issues. It also needs a lessons file `.claude/agents/lessons/test-obligations-assessor.md` and a row in `.claude/agents/README.md` (agent table and delegation table).
- Verdict format, recorded per file in `.github/coverage-manifest/{Package}.json`: per flag a `target`, a one-sentence `justification` tied to the file's code, a `verdictDate` (yyyy-MM-dd) and an `assessor` (agent name and run id); for a line-level argument, a list of lines or ranges with the reason they are raised or lowered. A legitimate 0 carries the reason and the closed-list construct (if any) it relies on. The schema extension is shared with #2890's tripwire, which reads `verdictDate` and compares it with the file's last git change.
- The assessor may argue raising or lowering obligations for specific lines and test types, not only whole files.
- Integration points:
  - `worker-brief` skill: a brief for any `src/` change has a mandatory step "assessor verdict before code"; the worker reads the verdict and the PR reports measured coverage against it.
  - `issue-audit` skill, test stage: the assessor runs next to `test-auditor` on the scope list and its verdicts are the baseline for the obligations findings (rule (b)).
  - `pr-cycle` skill: before the PR is opened, files touched under `src/` have a current verdict.
  - Zero review of EPIC #2845 and doubtful areas: the assessor reviews every 0 target.
  - Spawn-hook enforcement: a hook denies spawning an `issue-worker` on a brief that touches `src/` unless the brief records the assessor step (or a verdict newer than the files' last change exists), and the assessor must be a different spawn from the worker that authors the code.
- Relation to other issues: #2890 is the deterministic tripwire that consumes the verdicts (closed list of non-executable constructs, CI failure on missing or stale verdict); #2840 (zero targets accepted for files with executable code) and #2841 (package/flag pairs without target) are the debts the assessor and tripwire make visible and fix; EPIC #2845 is the parent.
- Implementation plan required before work: `docs/plans/test-obligations-assessor-implementation-plan-<issue>.md` generated with the plan prompt `docs/engineering/prompts/implementation-plan-prompt.md` and linked from this issue (AGENTS.md section 11).

## Alternatives Considered

List every implicit choice of this feature (defaults, error semantics, storage, public names, behaviour on missing context, dependencies, ordering, retention) and classify each one:

- **Trivial**: follows a cited convention.
- **Settled**: the only option that complies, with a verifiable citation (an `AGENTS.md` section or rule, a SPEC id, an ADR number, a law article, a link to an earlier maintainer decision, or named comparable products). Write the choice and its citation; do not present it as an open option.
- **Dilemma**: two or more valid options, each better in a concrete named scenario. Write each option with its pros and cons and the scenario where it wins. Only an issue with a Dilemma carries the `needs-decision` label.

Zero Dilemmas is valid: write "No open design choices" and keep the settled choices with their citation.

1. **Judgment by an agent plus deterministic tripwire** (Settled): maintainer decision of 2026-10-26 on #2890, option (D). Cited: https://github.com/dlrivada/Encina/issues/2890 (decision comment).
2. **Model Sonnet with high effort** (Trivial): follows the routing rule in `.claude/agents/README.md` (Sonnet with high effort only where reasoning is the job, as for `issue-auditor`).
3. **Verdict stored in the coverage manifest, not in a separate file** (Settled): the maintainer decision states "Its verdicts are recorded in the coverage manifest, where this issue's tripwire checks them"; `AGENTS.md` section 9 makes the manifest the source of per-file targets and justifications.
4. **Assessor is always a party distinct from the code's author** (Settled): same maintainer decision.
5. **Read-only on `src/` and `tests/`** (Trivial): follows `test-auditor` ("Analysis only: never change src/, tests/ or docs/").

No open design choices.

## Affected Packages

Which Encina packages would this feature affect? None of the library packages.

- [ ] Encina (core)
- [ ] Encina.EntityFrameworkCore
- [ ] Encina.Dapper.*
- [ ] Encina.ADO.*
- [ ] Encina.AspNetCore
- [ ] Encina.MongoDB
- [ ] Encina.OpenTelemetry
- [ ] Encina.Caching.*
- [ ] Encina.Messaging
- [ ] Encina.Polly
- [ ] Encina.Cdc
- [x] Other: .claude agents, .github coverage manifests and tools/ai (no library package changes)

## Provider Implementation Matrix

> Per `AGENTS.md` §5 (Providers): All provider-dependent features MUST be implemented for ALL applicable providers.
> **Note**: Omit this section if the feature does not touch provider-specific code.

Not applicable: the feature touches no provider-specific code (agent definition, manifest schema, skills and hooks only).

## Cross-Cutting Integration

> Per `AGENTS.md` §6 (Cross-cutting integration check): Every new feature MUST be evaluated against ALL 12 transversal functions.
> Mark each: ✅ Included in this feature | ⏭️ Deferred (separate issue) | ❌ N/A (explain why)

| # | Function | Status | Notes |
|---|----------|--------|-------|
| 1 | **Caching** (`ICacheProvider`, decorator, `[Cache]`) | ❌ N/A | no read path to cache |
| 2 | **OpenTelemetry** (`ActivitySource`, `Meter`) | ❌ N/A | tooling, no runtime operation in the library |
| 3 | **Structured Logging** (`[LoggerMessage]`, `Log.cs`) | ❌ N/A | no library code; hook output goes to the hook's own messages |
| 4 | **Health Checks** (`IEncinaHealthCheck`) | ❌ N/A | no checkable runtime dependency |
| 5 | **Validation** (`IValidationProvider`, pipeline) | ✅ Included | the manifest verdict schema is validated by the existing `--check-justifications` step of `.github/scripts/coverage-report.cs` |
| 6 | **Resilience** (retry, circuit breaker, timeout) | ❌ N/A | no external system calls |
| 7 | **Distributed Locks** (`IDistributedLockProvider`) | ❌ N/A | no shared runtime state |
| 8 | **Transactions** (`IUnitOfWork`, atomicity) | ❌ N/A | no atomic multi-operation store |
| 9 | **Idempotency** (`InboxPipelineBehavior`, dedup) | ✅ Included | a verdict with an unchanged file and an unexpired verdictDate is not re-assessed |
| 10 | **Multi-Tenancy** (`TenantId`, `ITenantContext`) | ❌ N/A | no tenant data |
| 11 | **Module Isolation** (`ModuleId`, `IModuleContext`) | ❌ N/A | no module scoping |
| 12 | **Audit Trail** (`IOperationAuditStore`, audit events) | ✅ Included | each verdict records assessor, date and justification in the manifest, which is versioned in git |

### Observability Details (if applicable)

Not applicable (no library metrics or spans; usage is recorded in `artifacts/agent-usage/ledger.csv`).

## Test Matrix

> Per `AGENTS.md` §9 (Testing obligations): All applicable test types must be implemented or justified.

| Test Type | Required? | Scope | Notes |
|-----------|:---------:|-------|-------|
| **UnitTests** | Required | the verdict-schema validation and the staleness comparison in `coverage-report.cs` and the spawn hook, exercised through `.claude/hooks/tests/Test-Hooks.ps1` and the coverage-report tests | |
| **GuardTests** | Not applicable | | no public C# API with parameters is added |
| **ContractTests** | Not applicable | | no public interface or abstract class is added |
| **PropertyTests** | Not applicable | | no complex logic; the verdict check is a date comparison |
| **IntegrationTests** | Not applicable | | no database or external system; justified in the plan |
| **LoadTests** | Not applicable | | not concurrent code |
| **BenchmarkTests** | Not applicable | | not a hot path |

## Implementation Tasks

### Core Abstractions

- [ ] Write `.claude/agents/test-obligations-assessor.md` and its lessons file.
- [ ] Define the verdict schema in `.github/coverage-manifest` and update the manifest validation in `coverage-report.cs`.
- [ ] Update `.claude/agents/README.md` agent and delegation tables.
- [ ] Update skills `worker-brief`, `issue-audit` (test stage) and `pr-cycle`.
- [ ] Add the spawn hook that requires the assessor step in a brief touching `src/` and its tests in `Test-Hooks.ps1`.
- [ ] Seed verdicts for the files the zero review of EPIC #2845 covers first.

### Provider Implementations (if applicable)

Not applicable.

### Observability

Not applicable (usage ledger row per spawn).

### Testing

- [ ] GuardTests
- [ ] ContractTests
- [ ] PropertyTests
- [ ] IntegrationTests (Docker)
- [ ] LoadTests (if applicable)
- [ ] BenchmarkTests (if applicable)

### Documentation

- [ ] XML doc comments on all public APIs (not applicable: no public C# API)
- [x] README updates
- [x] Configuration guide

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Agent definition, lessons file and README rows exist; the agent is read-only on `src/` and `tests/` and writes only manifest verdicts and its report
- [ ] The manifest verdict format (target, justification, verdictDate, assessor, optional line-level arguments) is documented and validated by `coverage-report.cs`
- [ ] `worker-brief`, `issue-audit` (test stage) and `pr-cycle` require the assessor step; a spawn hook blocks a `src/` brief without it; the assessor is never the author's spawn
- [ ] Hook tests added to `Test-Hooks.ps1` pass
- [ ] The tripwire of #2890 consumes the verdicts (a missing or stale verdict fails CI)

## Documentation

What documentation artifacts are needed?
