- [x] #40 — `ci.3` level 3: server image artefact on green `main`, no deploy
- [ ] #44 — `sec.1` security gate: CVE scanning in CI (landed), headers/CORS, auth rate limits, negative-path e2e, ZAP baseline *(added 2026-09-09)*

## Who does what

**The course requires every member to touch frontend, backend and CI/CD.** The earlier plan — one backend lane each (`adr/README.md`, *"แบ่ง Lane B / Lane C ให้อีกสองคนในทีม"*) — does not satisfy that, because all three lanes are backend. Superseded 2026-09-05 by three cross-cutting bundles: **9 backend slices + 1 CI slice + 1 frontend slice each.**

Labels `team/1`, `team/2`, `team/3` carry the assignment. They are placeholders for names — remap freely.

| | `team/1` — transaction path | `team/2` — schema, catalogue, reports | `team/3` — platform, infrastructure, ops |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Backend** | #15 #18 #19 #20 #21 #22 #23 #24 #28 #30 | #5 #16 #17 #25 #26 #27 #29 #32 | #14 #4 #6 #43 #31 #33 #34 #35 #36 #37 |
| **CI/CD** | #38 backend workflow · #40 image artefact · #61 #62 release images | #39 path filters + isolation check · #63 #64 ops | #44 security gate · #65 #67 deploy · #66 ops |
| **Frontend** | #53 Drift schema v3 · #56 Checkout, Returns, Cash Drawer on `ApiRepository` writes | #55 Products, Customers, Mechanics, PO, Quotes, Reports on `ApiRepository` reads | #54 auth + device-token storage, login flow, the seven new server error strings | 
| **Decisions to chase** | #11 | — | #12 #13 |

**Remapped 2026-09-11 to match what actually landed.** #15 (`p2`) and #38 (`ci.1`) were built and merged by `NuimanLP` in PR #42, so both moved from `team/2` / `team/3` to `team/1` (assignee + label). #53 (`fe.0`) was already on `team/1` (see #52). The CI/CD row now also lists the #60 slices (#61–#67, ticketed 2026-09-10). Strikethrough = closed.

~~**Frontend slices are not ticketed yet.**~~ Ticketed 2026-09-10 as #52 → #53 #54 #55 #56. The work exists in `03_ARCHITECTURE.md §8` as task `q1` and in [ADR-0010](docs/Backend_design/adr/0010-client-write-through-cache.md); the row above reserves the split. Ticket it before anyone finishes their backend bundle, or the third area gets rushed at the end.

**Why these groupings.** Each bundle is one coherent area of the system, so nobody context-switches across every module. The frontend column deliberately mirrors the backend column: whoever built `POST /sales` wires the Checkout screen to it, which is the cheapest way to make the client work real rather than busywork added for the grade.

**Ordering.** The foundation is serial no matter how it is split: `team/3` does #14, then `team/2` does #15, then `team/3` does #4 and #6 while `team/2` starts the catalogue. `team/1` is blocked until #6 lands, since the money path needs device roles — the deepest cross-member dependency in the plan, so it goes first.


Phase 1 closes when the 17 done-criteria in `03_ARCHITECTURE.md §8` all pass. Each is assigned to a child issue above.

## Problem Statement

The shop runs a single-machine, offline-only Flutter POS whose entire truth lives in a browser-local SQLite file. That works for one shop with one counter, but:

- There is no server, so nothing protects the data from a wiped browser profile, no second machine can ever see the same stock, and every business rule (stock deduction, returns, weighted-average cost, cash-drawer shifts) exists only inside the client.
- The course assignment fixes the stack (Nginx → NestJS ×3 → PostgreSQL + Redis + BullMQ, JWT-stateless, Docker Compose, k6) and adds **multi-tenant** to the scope: many independent auto-parts shops, different owners, one database. The current app cannot be submitted against that brief at all.
- The project owner is also the shop's successor owner: the deliverable has to be **both** the graded assignment and the real backend the shop will eventually cut over to. A throwaway server would have to be rebuilt.

## Solution

Build `server/` — a NestJS modular monolith that becomes the **source of truth** for every shop, with PostgreSQL holding the data, Redis for cache and per-tenant rate limits, BullMQ for post-commit work, and Nginx in front of three NestJS instances. Every transactional invariant currently in the Dart repositories is ported server-side, verbatim in behaviour and in Thai error text, and closed against the races the single-machine app never hit.

Tenancy is shared-schema with `tenant_id` on every row, composite foreign keys, and PostgreSQL row-level security as the last net. Shops are provisioned by a separate platform-admin plane; devices are enrolled by the owner and carry a role (`pos` or `backoffice`) that the server, not the client, asserts.

Phase 1 ships on a **demo tenant loaded with the shop's real snapshot**. The shop keeps running today's Drift build; nothing is cut over. Done means: one `docker compose up`, the 17 done-criteria in the architecture plan pass, k6 targets are met, and a backend CI job runs the integration suite on every server change.

## User Stories

**Cashier at the counter (`pos` device)**

1. As a cashier, I want to log in each morning with my username, password, and this machine's stored device token, so that the server knows I am selling from the shop's one registered selling machine.
2. As a cashier, I want my session to stay valid for the whole trading day without re-login, so that a token expiry never fires mid-bill with a customer waiting.
3. As a cashier, I want to complete a sale in one request and get back the receipt number, points granted, and the new stock of every line, so that I can print the receipt and my screen is immediately correct.
4. As a cashier, I want a sale with several short lines to be rejected once with a single Thai message listing **every** failing line, so that I do not have to retry the bill repeatedly to discover what is missing.
5. As a cashier, I want a double-tap or a retried request to never create a second bill or deduct stock twice, so that a bad Wi-Fi moment cannot corrupt stock.
6. As a cashier, I want the server to accept the totals my app computed as long as they are within one satang of its own arithmetic, so that a receipt already printed is never contradicted.
7. As a cashier, I want a sale on mechanic credit to raise that mechanic's balance, and a sale to a customer to raise their points and spend, so that credit and loyalty behave exactly as they do today.
8. As a cashier, I want to sell over a mechanic's credit limit after confirming, with the override recorded, so that the shop's daily practice with regular mechanics keeps working.
9. As a cashier, I want to find a bill by receipt number and see how much of each line was already refunded, so that I can process a return correctly.
10. As a cashier, I want a return that exceeds what is still returnable to be refused with the existing Thai message, so that over-refunds cannot happen.
11. As a cashier, I want a return to reverse discount, points, and mechanic figures proportionally and to reduce credit balance only when the refund method is "หักจากเครดิต", so that returns behave as they do today.
12. As a cashier, I want a full return to void the parent bill automatically and a second return on a voided bill to be refused, so that the ledger stays consistent.
13. As a cashier, I want to park a bill and retrieve it later without stock being touched, so that I can serve the next customer.
14. As a cashier, I want to open the drawer with a starting float, add cash in/out entries, and close it with the counted cash, so that the day's cash is accounted for.
15. As a cashier, I want adding a cash entry after the drawer is closed to be refused with the existing Thai message, so that closed shifts stay closed.
16. As a cashier, I want a closing report whose expected cash includes cash sales, mechanics' cash debt payments, cash refunds, and drawer entries, so that the drawer balances every day.
17. As a cashier, I want to record a mechanic paying down their debt and get a receipt number for it, so that credit statements are complete.
18. As a cashier, I want to look a product up by exact part number, so that a barcode scan returns one product, not a search list.
19. As a cashier, I want the bootstrap data (products, categories with colours, customers, mechanics, settings) in one request with an ETag, so that opening Checkout is fast and cheap on repeat.

**Back-office staff (`backoffice` device or no device)**

20. As back-office staff, I want to log in from a laptop or phone without a device token and still read stock, manage products, customers, mechanics, quotes, and purchase orders, so that stock work does not need the selling machine.
21. As back-office staff, I want any attempt to sell, return, park, take credit payments, or touch the drawer from my device to be refused with a clear code, so that only the selling machine touches cash and receipt numbers.
22. As back-office staff, I want to receive a purchase order and have stock and weighted-average cost update atomically, with a cost of zero on a PO line never dragging the average toward zero, so that profit reports stay honest.
23. As back-office staff, I want receiving the same PO twice to be refused, so that stock is never double-added.
24. As back-office staff, I want unmatched part numbers on a PO receipt returned as a list rather than an error, so that I can decide whether to create them.
25. As back-office staff, I want manual stock adjustments to clamp at zero and to create a movement record, so that manual corrections are traceable.
26. As back-office staff, I want deleting a customer, mechanic, or product that has history to succeed and hide the record rather than fail, so that everyday cleanup works and old bills keep their names.
27. As back-office staff, I want Thai substring search on products to find "เบรก" inside "ผ้าเบรกหน้า", so that search is at least as good as the current in-memory filter.
28. As back-office staff, I want to create, edit, duplicate, and delete quotations without stock changing, so that quoting stays free of side effects.
29. As back-office staff, I want report KPIs (summary, top products, by category, stock value, low stock, per-product sales) computed server-side, so that a shop with years of bills does not download every bill to a phone.
30. As back-office staff, I want gross profit to use the cost recorded on each sale line and to be told how many lines were estimated from current cost, so that last month's profit does not change when new stock arrives.
31. As back-office staff, I want CSV exports with every field passed through the formula-injection guard, so that a spreadsheet cannot execute a customer's name.
32. As back-office staff, I want a heavy request (quote purge, backup export) to be accepted immediately and processed in the background with a job I can poll, so that the UI does not hang.

**Shop owner**

33. As an owner, I want to enrol a new device by creating it with a label and role and receiving a one-time enrolment code, so that a browser becomes a known machine only because I said so.
34. As an owner, I want the system to refuse a second active `pos` device, so that the shop can never have two cash drawers and two receipt series.
35. As an owner, I want to retire a device, and if it was the selling machine with an open shift, have that shift closed with the cash I enter in the same step, so that moving to a replacement machine never leaves an unclosable shift.
36. As an owner, I want a retired device's tokens to stop refreshing within fifteen minutes, so that the old machine cannot keep selling all day.
37. As an owner, I want to deactivate a staff member and have their access die within fifteen minutes with no extra infrastructure, so that dismissals are safe.
38. As an owner, I want to request an export of my whole shop in the existing backup file shape and receive an expiring download link, so that I always hold my own data.
39. As an owner, I want every export to be audit-logged and rate-limited to about once a day, so that the file containing every customer's phone number is not casually copied.
40. As an owner, I want receipt numbers in the form `RC01-2569-09-0042` issued by the server in strict per-device, per-month sequence, so that accounting can audit gaps and order.
41. As an owner, I want receipts imported from the old app to keep their old random numbers untouched, so that history is never rewritten.
42. As an owner, I want exceeding 9,999 documents in a month on one device to fail loudly rather than wrap, so that numbers never silently collide.

**Platform admin (our team)**

43. As a platform admin, I want to log in through a separate endpoint with a token that no shop endpoint accepts, so that admin credentials can never be replayed as a shop user.
44. As a platform admin, I want to create a shop in one transaction that yields the tenant, its first owner, its settings row, the five seed categories, and its first `pos` device with an enrolment code, so that a shop can log in and sell without anyone touching psql.
45. As a platform admin, I want to suspend or close a shop and have its very next request refused, so that suspension does not wait for a token to expire.
46. As a platform admin, I want a suspended shop's queued background jobs to be skipped, so that suspension covers the worker path too.
47. As a platform admin, I want to import a shop's legacy snapshot only into a tenant that has no bills yet, with a pre-flight scan and a six-value verification afterwards, so that onboarding is safe and can never act as a restore.
48. As a platform admin, I want every call I make audit-logged with my admin id and the tenant touched, so that the account that can see every shop leaves a trail.
49. As a platform admin, I want a `loadtest` plan that lifts the rate limit and a `demo` plan excluded from platform statistics, so that k6 measures the system and demos do not pollute reports.

**Any shop, relative to every other shop**

50. As a shop, I want no request, cache key, background job, or report to ever return another shop's rows, even if a developer forgets a `WHERE`, so that a competitor's data cannot leak into mine.
51. As a shop, I want my usage to be limited per tenant so that one busy shop cannot slow every other shop.
52. As a shop, I want a Redis outage to neither un-suspend suspended shops nor block active ones, so that a cache failure is invisible to me.

**Developer and CI**

53. As a developer, I want `docker compose up` to bring up Nginx, three NestJS instances, PostgreSQL, two Redis instances, a worker, and Bull-Board in one command, so that a reviewer can run the whole system.
54. As a developer, I want the integration suite to run on real PostgreSQL and Redis service containers on every push touching `server/`, so that RLS, locking, and idempotency are tested for real and never mocked.
55. As a developer, I want the Flutter CI to skip on server-only changes and the backend CI to skip on client-only changes, so that one monorepo does not double every pipeline.
56. As a developer, I want a server container image produced on every green build of `main` with no deploy step, so that the artefact exists before a production host is chosen.
57. As a developer, I want liveness and readiness endpoints that are genuinely different and exempt from rate limiting, so that a database blip cannot restart every container at once.
58. As a developer, I want structured JSON logs with a correlation id propagated to workers and no PII in them, so that an incident across three instances is debuggable and PDPA-safe.

**Instructor / grader**

59. As a grader, I want to see 200 concurrent sales against 50 units yield exactly 50 bills and stock exactly zero, so that data integrity is proven.
60. As a grader, I want k6 scenarios for read-heavy, write-heavy, idempotent-retry, and mixed load with the pass criteria from the design package, so that the load-test requirement is verifiable.

## Implementation Decisions

**Repository, process, and stack**

- `server/` lives at the root of this repo (ADR-0011). It starts clean; the faculty lab project in the course summaries is reference only and is not copied.
- NestJS modular monolith, TypeORM, PostgreSQL, two Redis instances, BullMQ, Nginx, Docker Compose. No microservices. Modules: auth, tenancy, platform, devices, products (with categories, suppliers, movements), customers, mechanics, sales, returns, purchasing, quotes, parked, shifts, reports, backup, common (filters, interceptors, idempotency, cache, rate limit, health).
- Work order is the dependency checklist in the architecture plan §8, not a calendar: compose skeleton → schema and migrations → auth + tenancy guard + RLS → platform plane → device roles → then three parallel lanes (A: sales + returns; B: CRUD → PO/quotes/shifts → reports; C: cache → rate limit → BullMQ + Bull-Board → export job → k6). Lane A is the project owner's; B and C are unassigned.
- Schema is applied only through TypeORM migrations run as a separate compose job before the app starts. `synchronize` is never true, in any environment, including tests — tests must exercise the real migrations.

**Tenancy model (T1, shared schema + RLS)** — all six rules are mandatory:

1. `tenant_id` comes from the JWT claim `tid` only; never from body, query, or header. The same rule applies to `did`.
2. Every business table has `tenant_id NOT NULL`, a composite primary key `(tenant_id, id)`, and every foreign key carries `tenant_id`. Every unique constraint and every index starts with `tenant_id`.
3. RLS is enabled **and forced** on every business table, applied by a migration loop, with this policy shape (fail-closed: an unset GUC yields zero rows, not an error):
   ```sql
   USING      (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid)
   WITH CHECK (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid)
   ```
   The application role is neither superuser nor table owner.
4. A single `TenantGuard` verifies the token audience, checks `tenants.status`, and only then executes `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id` inside the request transaction. There is no separate interceptor. A non-active tenant is rejected before `SET LOCAL`, so RLS independently returns nothing.
5. Every request that touches the database runs inside a transaction so `SET LOCAL` cannot leak across pooled connections. Consequence accepted: no read replica in phase 1.
6. Every Redis key is prefixed `t:{tid}:`. Every BullMQ job carries `tenantId` and `correlationId`, wraps its body in a transaction, sets the GUC inside it, and re-checks `tenants.status` before doing work.

**Platform admin plane (ADR-0001, 0002, 0003, 0005)**

- Platform operators live in `platform_admins` (no `tenant_id`), log in at `POST /platform/auth/token`, and receive a JWT with `aud: "platform"` and no `tid`. The `/api/*` guard rejects `aud != "tenant"`; the `/platform/*` guard rejects `aud != "platform"`. No shop role, including `owner`, can reach `/platform/*`.
- The `/platform/*` plane uses a **separate DataSource** whose role has `BYPASSRLS`; the tenant guard does not run there. Nginx keeps `/platform/*` and Bull-Board off the public internet (internal network or IP allowlist).
- Phase-1 admin endpoints are exactly five: login, create tenant, change tenant status, import snapshot into a tenant, list tenants. Every one writes `audit_log`, which has `platform_admin_id` alongside `user_id` and a CHECK that at least one actor (or a `system.` action) is present.
- Creating a tenant is one transaction producing: the `tenants` row (`status='active'`, `plan`, `timezone` default Asia/Bangkok), the first `users` row with `role='owner'`, one `settings` row, the five seed categories (เครื่องยนต์ / ไฟฟ้า / น้ำมัน / เบรก / ตัวถัง — copied per shop, no demo products, no unit-of-measure entity), and the first `devices` row (`role='pos'`, `device_no=1`) with an enrolment code. Any failure rolls back everything.
- `tenants.plan` is the single field for `basic` / `demo` / `loadtest`. There is no `is_demo`.
- Tenant status is `active` / `suspended` / `closed`; `closed` behaves like `suspended` in phase 1. Status is cached at `t:{tid}:status` with a 300s + jitter TTL, purged immediately on change; on a cache miss or Redis outage the guard reads `tenants` by primary key — never fail-open, never fail-closed.
- Import (`POST /platform/tenants/{id}/import`) is an onboarding tool only: it refuses if the tenant has any row in sales, returns, purchase orders, credit payments, quotes, or shifts. It runs as a BullMQ job, one tenant per transaction, in FK dependency order, after a JSON-only pre-flight scan (negative stock, orphan categories, unparseable dates, duplicate document numbers), generates shift ids because the snapshot has none, migrates `zone` → `category`, keeps historical `cost` on sale lines, rounds floats to two decimals, and verifies six totals afterwards (sum of sale totals, sum of stock, per-table counts, customer points and spend, mechanic balances against payments, last shift's drawer total). The original snapshot is retained for at least 90 days. No owner-facing import exists.

**Authentication and sessions (ADR-0004, 0009)**

- Shop users: `users` with `role` in `owner` / `manager` / `cashier`, Argon2id password hashes, one user bound to exactly one tenant forever.
- Access token lifetime 15 minutes. Refresh token expires at **04:00 in the tenant's timezone**; a refresh issued after 03:00 expires at 04:00 the following day. No refresh rotation, no Redis denylist. `POST /auth/refresh` checks `users.is_active`, `tenants.status`, and `devices.retired_at` for the token's `did` on every call.
- JWT claims: `sub`, `tid`, `role`, `aud`, `exp`, plus `did` and `drole` when a device token was presented.
- Devices: `POST /devices {label, role}` (owner) allocates the next never-reused `device_no` and returns a single-use, short-lived enrolment code; `POST /auth/device {code}` exchanges it for an opaque device token stored hashed with a global unique on the hash; `POST /auth/token` accepts an optional `deviceToken` and resolves `did`/`drole` server-side. A `deviceId` in any request body is rejected. No token means no `drole`, and the caller is treated as `backoffice`.
- A partial unique index allows at most one non-retired `pos` device per tenant. `POST /devices/{id}/retire` (owner) closes that device's open shift with the supplied physical cash and sets `retired_at` in one transaction, writing `audit_log`.
- Device-role split follows "does it touch the cash drawer or a bill": sales, returns, credit payments, shift open/close and drawer entries, parked sales, and receipt-number issuance are `pos` only. Everything else, including reading shifts and the closing report, is both. This list is the project owner's confirmed interpretation and applies as written unless the owner changes it.

**Database shape and types**

- 27 tables in phase 1 (the 28th, `change_log`, is phase 2 and must not be created). New relative to the client: tenants, platform_admins, users, devices, idempotency_keys, doc_counters, audit_log, tenant_meta.
- Ids stay client-generatable TEXT. Money is `NUMERIC(12,2)` with a string transformer on the wire; never floating point. Timestamps are `TIMESTAMPTZ` in UTC. Parked-sale payloads are JSONB. Child lines use a client-assigned `line_no` in the primary key instead of autoincrement. `shifts.id` is TEXT.
- `sales` gains `shift_id`, `user_id`, `device_id`; `returns` gains `shift_id`. `sale_items.cost_at_sale` is written in the sale transaction from the same locked read that deducts stock, never from the client, never backfilled for imported rows.
- CHECK constraints (`stock >= 0`, `points >= 0`, `credit_balance >= 0`, `cost >= 0`, positive quantities and amounts, enum statuses, `last_no <= 9999`) are assertions against our own bugs; all running totals are clamped in code with `GREATEST(0, …)`.
- Soft delete (`deleted_at`) for products, customers, mechanics; `DELETE` returns 200 and reads filter tombstones out. Part-number uniqueness is a partial index that ignores soft-deleted rows. Categories are hard-deleted and **there is no foreign key from products to categories**; orphaned category names are by design. Ledger tables (sales, returns, movements, credit payments, shifts) are never deleted; sales are cancelled only by `voided`.
- `movements` is append-only, written by the server only, with a real enum (`sale`, `return`, `receive`, `adjustment-in`, `adjustment-out`), a `ref_id` to the originating document, and a unique guard on `(tenant_id, type, ref_id, product_id)` so replays are safe. Writing sale and return movements is new behaviour, accepted deliberately.
- **The movements unique guard must be a partial index, `WHERE ref_id IS NOT NULL`.** Legacy rows imported from a snapshot carry only `receive` / `adjustment-in` / `adjustment-out` and have no reference, because `ref_id` is new. Two manual adjustments of the same type on the same product is ordinary shop history, and under an unconditional index the second one fails the import.
- Product search uses `pg_trgm` with a GIN trigram index over part number, names, and compatibility text; `to_tsvector` is not used because Thai has no word boundaries.
- `shifts` uniqueness is `(tenant_id, device_id) WHERE is_active`; `is_active` keeps its current meaning of "this device's current drawer", not "open".

**The sale transaction** (the port of `saveSale`, with the pre-check race closed)

1. Resolve the idempotency key. 2. Lock the products: `SELECT … WHERE tenant_id = $t AND id = ANY($ids) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE` — the ordering is the deadlock guard. 3. Build the complete Thai error from that result, one line per failing product, distinguishing insufficient stock from a missing product, and throw once. 4. Deduct with `stock >= qty` in the predicate as an assertion. 5. Issue the receipt number from `doc_counters` under a row lock using the token's `device_no`. 6. Insert the sale header and lines with `cost_at_sale`. 7. Insert movements. 8. Update the customer (`points += floor(total/10)`, `total_spend += total`) and the mechanic, whose fields are named exactly: `total_sales += total`; `total_discount += −delta` when `mechanic_delta` is negative; `total_markup += delta` when positive; `credit_balance += total` only when the payment method is `เครดิตช่าง`. 9. Commit. 10. Only after commit: invalidate cache keys and enqueue post-processing. No external call ever happens inside the transaction.

Money ownership: the server recomputes from the submitted lines (quantity × unit price) and compares with the submitted total; a difference above 0.01 is `409 TOTAL_MISMATCH`, otherwise the client's values are persisted. The server never compares line prices with the current catalogue price. `pointsGranted = floor(total / 10)` is computed by the server from the persisted total.

🔴 **`mechanics.total_credit` is an open decision an implementer must not settle by inference.** The database design §7.1 requires `total_credit += total` on a credit sale, but the Dart reference never writes it: `sales_repository.dart` updates only `total_sales`, `total_discount`, `total_markup`, and `credit_balance`, and nothing anywhere in `lib/` ever increments `total_credit`. The column is seeded to zero, displayed on the mechanics screen, and read once in `returns_repository.dart` as a discount base because the legacy app used `(totalDiscount || totalCredit)`. Following the design doc therefore diverges from the numbers the shop sees today. Decide explicitly before building sales: either write it as deliberate new behaviour, or leave it unwritten to preserve parity. Do not guess.

The response returns the receipt number, points granted, the new stock of every touched product, `mechanicCreditBalanceAfter`, and `customerAfter {points, totalSpend}`, so the client can patch its cache without re-reading. **`products[].offlineOk` is not returned in phase 1.** The API design shows it in the response example, but no column, materialized view, or average-per-bill storage for it exists anywhere in the database design, and its threshold is still an open question for the shop. It arrives in phase 2 together with its storage; emitting a constant or inventing a column now would pre-empt that decision.

**Returns, purchasing, shifts** — ported as documented in the database design §7 and the Dart repositories: over-refund guard with the existing Thai message; proportional reversal; credit reduced only for `หักจากเครดิต`; auto-void on full return; `cost_at_sale` carried from the original line; weighted-average cost with both fallbacks (`effective_new_cost = cost > 0 ? cost : old_cost`; divide-by-zero guard) rounded to two decimals; receiving twice is `409 PO_ALREADY_RECEIVED` checked inside the transaction; PO lines matched by part number with unmatched ones returned as a list; open-shift-same-day returns the existing shift, a new day archives the previous one (auto-archived if never closed); drawer entries after close are `409 DRAWER_CLOSED`; the closing report is computed by `shift_id`, not by timestamp window, with the formula:

```
expected = starting_cash + cash sales + cash credit-payments from mechanics
         − cash refunds + drawer in − drawer out
variance = physical_cash − expected
```

**Document numbering (ADR-0007)** — server issues every number in phase 1. Format `RC01-2569-08-0042`: prefix (RC / CN / PO / QT / CP), two-digit zero-padded `device_no`, Buddhist year and month, four-digit sequence reset monthly, from `doc_counters` keyed by `(tenant_id, device_id, doc_type, period)`. Clients send no number. Legacy numbers coexist under `UNIQUE (tenant_id, receipt_no)`. `GET /doc-counters` is not built in phase 1.

**API contract**

- Base path `/api/v1`; bearer JWT everywhere except auth and health; JSON; ISO-8601 UTC; money as strings; pagination `page`/`limit` (default 50, max 200); response envelope `{status, data, meta}` / `{status, error: {code, message, details}}` per the course assignment.
- Thai `message` text is copied verbatim from the existing app. The seven new codes (`PO_ALREADY_RECEIVED`, `DUPLICATE_PART_NO`, `TOTAL_MISMATCH`, `OFFLINE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `TENANT_SUSPENDED`, `DEVICE_ROLE_FORBIDDEN`, `RATE_LIMITED`) use the provisional wording in the API design §8.1 as string constants in one place, so the three counter-facing ones can be swapped when the shop chooses words. `RATE_LIMITED` always carries `Retry-After`.
- Credit-limit excess is **not** an error: `POST /sales` accepts `overrideCreditLimit: true` and audit-logs the override.
- Idempotency: every write touching money or stock requires an `Idempotency-Key`; same key and body replays the stored response, same key and different body is `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`; keys live 24 hours in `idempotency_keys` with a Redis fast layer and an hourly cleanup job. `sales.id` is client-generated and doubles as a natural duplicate guard.
- `?partNo=` is exact match and separate from `?search=`. `/categories` returns `[{name, color}]`. `GET /bootstrap` returns products, categories, customers, mechanics, settings with an ETag and `304` support. `?updatedSince=` is supported on products, customers, mechanics, settings, and every sale bumps `products.updated_at`.
- Reports are server-side aggregates: summary (with the count of profit rows estimated from current cost), top products, by category, stock value, low stock, per-product sales, closing by shift id. `refunded-qty` keeps the original `getRefundedQty` meaning.
- Endpoints that have no counterpart in today's app are built in phase 1 only where an existing screen needs them to avoid downloading every bill: bootstrap, per-customer and per-mechanic sales, per-product sales report. The rest (direct sale void, customer summary, mechanic statement, by-payment and daily reports, quote PDF, atomic quote convert) are deferred pending the owner's yes/no (see Further Notes).

**Cache, rate limit, queues, ops**

- Cache-aside in `redis-cache` (`allkeys-lru`) with TTL plus jitter on every key, stampede lock, invalidation only after commit, `SCAN` or tag sets never `KEYS`, and a try/catch with database fallback around every cache call.
- Per-tenant rate limit in a guard keyed `t:{tid}:rl:{route}:{window}` (fails open on Redis outage — this fail-open rule applies to rate-limit counters only), `429` + `Retry-After`, exempting health endpoints, disabled for `plan='loadtest'`. Nginx adds a coarse per-IP limit.
- BullMQ on `redis-queue` (`noeviction` + AOF): queues `sale-post`, `inventory`, `maintenance`, `backup`; jobs idempotent, three attempts with exponential backoff and jitter, dead-letter queue, failed jobs kept, completed jobs aged out. Bull-Board behind basic auth on the internal network. The sale itself is answered synchronously; workers never own the user-facing result.
- Export job returns the legacy `sa_*` + `__meta` snapshot as an expiring signed link, owner-only, audit-logged, once per day.
- `/health/live` touches nothing; `/health/ready` checks Postgres and Redis. Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM. Structured JSON logs with correlation ids; no card numbers, full phone numbers, or full customer names in logs. Pool sizing obeys `instances × poolSize ≤ 80% of max_connections`. Compose sets `mem_limit` per container to fit the faculty VM (4 vCPU / 6 GB); k6 runs from another machine.

**CI/CD (level 3, deploy unwired)**

- A second workflow, path-filtered to `server/**`, runs lint, unit tests, and the integration suite against Postgres and Redis service containers with the real migrations applied. The existing Flutter workflow already ignores `server/**`.
- ⚠️ Because `flutter.yml` sets `paths-ignore: ['server/**', 'docs/**', '**/*.md']`, a server-only pull request runs **no** Flutter jobs at all. If those job names are configured as required status checks on `main`, such a pull request can never satisfy them and will block forever. Either leave both workflows' jobs out of branch protection, or add a small always-runs job that reports the shared check name.
- On green `main`, build and upload the server container image as an artefact. No deploy step until a production host is chosen before cutover.

## Testing Decisions

**Seams.** One primary seam: **HTTP through the fully booted NestJS application, against a real PostgreSQL and real Redis** (compose services locally, service containers in CI), with the real migrations, real guards, real RLS role, and real locking. Every behavioural rule is asserted at this seam, because the things most likely to be wrong — tenancy isolation, row locks, `SET LOCAL` scope, idempotency, RLS fail-closed — are invisible to a test that mocks the repository. Service-level unit tests are reserved for pure functions (money rounding, number formatting, closing-report arithmetic, weighted-average cost, refresh-expiry computation). No test mocks TypeORM or Redis.

The same seam serves k6: the load scripts hit the composed stack through Nginx and the data-integrity proof is a SQL assertion after the run.

**What a good test looks like.** It sets up state through the API (provision a tenant via the platform plane, enrol a device, log in), performs one externally observable action, and asserts the response envelope, the Thai message text verbatim, and the resulting rows. It never reaches into service internals. Concurrency tests run real parallel requests, not simulated interleavings.

**Modules tested, and the cases that must exist.** The 17 phase-1 done-criteria in the architecture plan §8 are the acceptance suite and every one is a named test:

- compose boots the full stack; health endpoints are genuinely split; two Redis instances; Bull-Board authenticated.
- 200 concurrent sales on 50 units → exactly 50 bills, stock 0, never negative.
- `pos` selling while `backoffice` receives a PO and adjusts stock on the same product, 200 rounds → final stock equals the arithmetic, no lost update.
- cross-tenant read returns 0 rows in every table, both through the API and through a raw query on the app role with the GUC unset.
- a bill with three short lines → one response listing all three lines in Thai.
- deleting a customer with bills → 200 soft delete.
- provisioning via the platform plane, then login and a sale, with no manual SQL.
- `backoffice` calling `POST /sales` → 403 `DEVICE_ROLE_FORBIDDEN`; a login without a device token can read products but not sell.
- suspend a tenant → next request refused; a queued job for that tenant is skipped; with `redis-cache` stopped the suspended tenant stays refused and an active one keeps working.
- retire the `pos` device with an open shift → shift closed in the same transaction, its refresh fails within 15 minutes, a new device gets a new `device_no` and can sell.
- imported real snapshot passes all six verification totals.
- audience separation: a tenant token on `/platform/*` and a platform token on `/api/*` are both rejected; every platform call leaves an audit row.
- idempotency replay: same key five times → one bill; same key different body → 409.
- total mismatch above 0.01 → 409; within tolerance → client value persisted; points computed server-side.
- receipt numbers are sequential per device per month, zero-padded, and the 10,000th fails clearly.
- refresh after 03:00 expires at 04:00 next day in the tenant timezone; a deactivated user cannot refresh.
- rate limit: 429 with `Retry-After`, health exempt, `loadtest` plan exempt, Redis outage fails open for the limiter only.
- k6: the four scenarios in the API design §9 with their pass criteria. **§9 is the gate**, so `POST /sales` p95 under 500 ms is what passes or fails phase 1. The tighter round-3 figure of 300 ms at 50 virtual users is not tracked and must not be tuned for.

**Prior art.** Each test in the Dart repository suite (`sales`, `returns`, `purchase_orders`, `shifts`, `mechanics`, `customers`, `products`, `quotes`, `parked`, `snapshot`) is a behavioural case to port one-for-one to the HTTP seam, including its Thai assertion strings. The course's Backend06 assignment demonstrates the e2e-on-compose pattern for NestJS; its code is not reused, only the pattern.

## Out of Scope

- **Phase 2 entirely:** outbox, `POST /sync/*`, `change_log`, `GET /doc-counters`, device-issued receipt numbers, `sales.sync_status`, the reconciliation queue, `offlineOk` enforcement and its threshold, `POS_OFFLINE`, replay ordering by `client_seq`, offline PIN login at shift open.
- **The Flutter client work** — the `ApiRepository` write-through layer, Drift schema v3, wiring `products.updatedAt`, and the client's use of `?updatedSince=`. That is its own spec (task `q1`).
- **Cutover of the real shop.** The shop keeps the Drift build; phase 1 is delivered on a demo tenant.
- Self-service signup, billing/subscriptions, platform-wide statistics, admin MFA, per-tenant point-in-time restore, PDPA retention/hard-delete workflow for closed tenants.
- Read replicas, PgBouncer, Sentinel, a second Nginx.
- The deploy step and the production host decision (due before cutover, not now).
- Final Thai wording of the seven new error strings and the three report strings; the receipt sample sign-off.
- Full tax invoice (ใบกำกับภาษีเต็มรูป), thermal printing, barcode camera scanning, LINE notifications (the `sale-post` job leaves a hook, nothing is sent).
- Applying the round-3 QA proposals to the design documents (they are recorded, not adopted; see Further Notes).

## Further Notes

- **Origin of this spec.** The session had no prior conversation; the content is a synthesis of the checked-in design package, ADRs, handoffs, and the Dart reference implementation. The issue tracker setup skill was never run, so this spec uses GitHub Issues with a `ready-for-agent` label created for the purpose.
- **Round-3 scrutiny.** All three review agents concluded the architecture doc's §7 in practice recommends **A + T1 for phase 1 with C kept as an additive option**, and listed twelve proposals (#23–#34) not yet applied to the docs. None changes phase-1 server behaviour except two that this spec already reflects: the server validates in-bill arithmetic only, never against catalogue price (#32), and `sales.id` is a natural duplicate guard alongside the header (#31). The proposed tighter latency budget (`POST /sales` p95 ≤ 300 ms at 50 VU, ≤ 800 ms end-to-end on 4G, #34) is **not adopted and not tracked**; the gate is the API design §9 (p95 under 500 ms). Two new human questions from that round remain open: how often the shop's internet actually fails, and whether §7's wording should change from "recommend C" to "recommend A, keep C".
- **Decisions still owed by a human before or during build** (collected at the end of the ADR index, phrased for the shop): which counter machine is the selling machine and who may move it; whether the shop ever trades at 04:00; receipt sample and monthly-vs-yearly reset; whether cost-at-sale includes freight; whether suspended shops may still read/export; whether "no rollback of yesterday's data" can be stated in writing; how the first owner password is delivered; whether single-factor admin accounts are acceptable. Also the yes/no on each deferred "NEW" endpoint listed under Implementation Decisions, and the Lane B / Lane C assignment.
- **Three strings will be seen by customers** with the provisional wording: `DEVICE_ROLE_FORBIDDEN`, `TENANT_SUSPENDED`, `OFFLINE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Keep them as swappable constants and do not let tests hard-code them as parity strings the way the `db.js` strings are.
- **Known behaviour changes versus today**, accepted on purpose: sales and returns now write movements; receiving a PO twice is refused; stock pre-check moves inside the lock; deletes become soft; the closing report is keyed by shift id; receipt numbers are sequential.
- **Non-ASCII path constraint** still applies to this repo checkout for Dart codegen only; Node tooling under `server/` is unaffected.
- **The faculty VM** is demo-only and confirmed to accept inbound connections from outside the university network.

items.title: Implement Yi-De multi-page Astro + TinaCMS brand site
items.body:
## Goal

Deliver the `design_handoff_yide_site` v2 brand site as a static Astro multi-page website backed by TinaCMS editorial content and the STDS backend property availability endpoint.

The final public site should include:

- `/` home page
- `/tenant` tenant landing page with the tenant-page property availability list
- `/landlord` landlord landing page
- `/news` news list
- `/news/[slug]` article pages

## Source of Truth

- `design_handoff_yide_site/README.md`
- `design_handoff_yide_site/CONTENT-MODEL.md`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `CICD.md`

## Architecture Boundary

- TinaCMS owns editorial copy, images, site settings, contact details, FAQ, and news/blog content.
- The STDS backend owns property availability only.
- The only backend endpoint the brand frontend should consume is `GET /api/v1/public/properties/availability`.
- Cloudflare Pages remains the hosting target.
- Public pages must be static/crawlable Astro output, not client-only rendering.

## Scope

Coordinate the child issues required to migrate from the current early single-page Astro implementation to the v2 multi-page handoff.

Expected child work includes:

- TinaCMS build/admin foundation.
- Tina schema and seed content.
- Shared Astro layout, tokens, assets, and SEO helpers.
- Shared header/footer chrome.
- Home, tenant, landlord, and news page implementation.
- Availability-only backend boundary and CI fixture alignment.
- Cloudflare Pages/Tina env documentation.
- Tina editor workflow smoke.
- v2 Cloudflare Pages staging smoke evidence.

## Non-Goals

- Do not implement or modify backend endpoints.
- Do not add booking, reservation, public write APIs, or contact form submission.
- Do not add realtime availability.
- Do not use Firebase Hosting rewrites, `stds_brand_backend`, or a brand Cloud Run proxy.
- Do not perform production promotion.
- Do not record secrets, deploy hook URLs, Tina tokens, or Cloudflare credential material.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Home, tenant, landlord, news list, and news detail pages are implemented from the v2 handoff.
- TinaCMS is the source for editorial/site settings/FAQ/news/page content.
- Backend usage is limited to `GET /api/v1/public/properties/availability`.
- Public pages include crawlable HTML and route-specific title, description, canonical URL, and Open Graph metadata.
- PR CI passes for the completed implementation.
- Cloudflare Pages staging smoke evidence is recorded without secrets.

## AI Handoff Constraints

- Keep child issue scope narrow and verifiable.
- If handoff, architecture, and implementation disagree, follow `design_handoff_yide_site` for product/content/design and `ARCHITECTURE.md`/`CICD.md` for deployment.
- Do not infer private backend data, env values, staging URLs, Cloudflare details, Tina tokens, or production release behavior.
- Do not move core public content behind client-only rendering.

items.title: Meta-epic: MCP-native CRM playbook (Phases 0–4, ~12 months)
items.body:
## Vision

CPCRM becomes the first SMB CRM that is **MCP-native end-to-end**: discoverable from inside Claude, with Interactive components for visual surfaces, agentic automations, and a per-tenant continuous-learning store. Foundations already in place: multi-tenant, Descope auth, four registries, Companies House angle, dynamic records system.

## Stage map

| Stage | Window | Epic | Theme | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Week 1 | #537 | Unblock current state | ✅ Complete (2026-04-29) |
| 1 | Weeks 1–2 (parallel) | #538 | Foundation decisions + infra | ⚠️ 1/5 done (#551 RLS ADR closed); #549, #550 decisions not locked (54 days); #552, #553 not started |
| 2 | Weeks 3–8 | #539 | MCP MVP + AI Attributes | ⏳ 1/14 done (#557 RLS policies closed); blocked on Stage 1 decisions |
| 3 | Months 3–4 | #540 | Interactive + intake | ⏳ Future |
| 4 | Months 5–6 | #541 | Agentic layer | ⏳ Future |
| 5 | Months 7–12 | #542 | Defensibility | ⏳ Future |
| ⨯ | Cross-cutting | #543 | Concurrent deployment strategy | ⏳ Not started |

## Parallel tracks (independent of MCP stages)

| Track | Epic/Issue | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page builder zones | #514 | ✅ Complete (8/8 sub-issues closed 2026-04-30) |
| AI edit contract impl | #593 → #594 → #595 → #596, #597 | ⏳ **PR #601 for #593 awaiting merge for 51 days — over 7 weeks** (CI clean — all 5 checks green, no blocking reviews). Entire downstream chain blocked. |

| Frontend test coverage | #390 | 59 web / 81 api test files — no coverage tooling (no istanbul/c8/vitest coverage config). Stalled 54 days. |
| Activity timeline | #384 | Partial — `activity_timeline` and `activity` component types registered in ComponentRegistry (`apps/api/src/lib/componentRegistry.ts`); render as `PlaceholderWidget` (empty state). No `ActivityFeed.tsx` or `ActivityPanel.tsx` UI components exist yet. Backend `record_events` table + event bus not started. |

| Frontend logging | #381 | Partial — lightweight logger shim landed at `apps/web/src/lib/logger.ts` (swappable interface, dev-only console output). Application Insights SDK not yet installed in `apps/web`. (Note: API-side config accepts `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` in `apps/api/src/lib/config.ts` but no active telemetry wiring.) |
| File attachments | #383 | Partial — `file` system object seeded with fields (filename, file_url, size, content_type, category, description) and relationships in migrations 011/012. No Azure Blob Storage infra, SAS URL endpoints, or upload UI yet. |
| Workflow automation | #388 | ⏳ Not started — no `workflow_rules` table or engine code exists |
| CSV import/export | #385 | ⏳ Not started — no import/export code exists |

Remaining: verify all app secrets reference Key Vault (not plain env vars). |

| Security warnings | — | ✅ **Complete** — All 62 CodeQL warnings resolved (ReDoS, SQL injection, XSS, prototype pollution, missing headers). Documented in `docs/codeql-resolution.md`. Draft PR #608 opened to mark tracking as complete. |

## Open PRs requiring action

| PR | Description | Status | Age |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| **#610** | **Dependabot: undici 7.24.7 → 7.28.0 (⚠️ SECURITY — 7 CVEs, 3 High severity)** | **CI FAILING** — "Lint, Typecheck & Test" fails. Root cause: `@types/react@19` vs `react@18` mismatch on `main`. **Security-critical: addresses CVE-2026-12151 (WebSocket DoS, CVSS 7.5), CVE-2026-9697 (TLS cert bypass, CVSS 7.4), CVE-2026-6734 (cross-origin routing, CVSS 7.5) + 4 moderate/low.** | **1 day** |
| #609 | Dependabot: 23 minor/patch dep bumps (supersedes #607, #604, #602) | **CI FAILING** — same `@types/react` mismatch root cause. | 6 days |
| #608 | docs: mark security warnings tracking as complete | **Draft, CI FAILING** — same `@types/react` mismatch root cause. Docs-only. | 7 days |
| #606 | Dependabot: `qs` 6.15.0 → 6.15.2 (security bugfixes) | **CI FAILING** — same `@types/react` mismatch root cause. | 29 days |
| #605 | docs: update TODO-CATALOGUE — all deprecated code removed | **Draft, CI FAILING** — same root cause. Docs-only (1 file changed). | 30 days |
| #603 | Dependabot: kysely 0.28.16 → 0.28.17 (security: hardens JSON path `.key()`/`.at()` against SQL injection) | **Awaiting review** (all CI passing, mergeable: clean) — **security-relevant** | 41 days |
| #599 / #598 | Anthropic SDK bump (0.90.0 → 0.91.1) | **Awaiting review** (all CI passing) — likely duplicates (one for root, one for apps/api) | 53 days |
| #592 | Roadmap docs: MCP-native playbook | Awaiting review (all CI passing, mergeable: clean) | 54 days |
| #434 | @eslint/js 9.x → 10.x major bump | Stale — breaking change, needs evaluation | 69 days |
| #433 | @descope/node-sdk 1.x → 2.x major bump | Stale — all CI green but major breaking change, needs evaluation | 69 days |
| #432 | vite 7.x → 8.x major bump | Stale — breaking change, needs evaluation | 69 days |

**Dependabot CI failure root cause (confirmed 2026-06-14):** PRs #605, #606, #608, #609, and **#610** all fail on the "Lint, Typecheck & Test" job. **Root cause: `@types/react` is at v19 (`^19.2.14`) while runtime `react` remains at `^18.3.1` on `main`.** This type mismatch causes TypeScript compilation failures across all branches that don't independently resolve the version skew. Fix path: either upgrade `react` to 19.x (#419) or pin `@types/react` back to v18 until the upgrade is ready.

**⚠️ The @types/react mismatch is now blocking a security-critical PR (#610 — undici, 3 High-severity CVEs). Resolving #419 or pinning the types is urgent.**

## Current blockers

1. **PR #601 merge** — The AI edit contract PR has been CI-clean and waiting for human review since May 1 (**51 days — over 7 weeks**). Merging it immediately unblocks 4 downstream issues (#594, #595, #596, #597).
